2022 I love cyberpunk settings. There's so much darkness and imagination that can go into the setting. It's also a setting we could possibly be heading into ourselves with the way technology is advancing and how much we rely on it. Stray is all about exactly this issue. You play as an unnamed orange cat who ends up in the middle of trying to help a race of robots see the "Outside" again. You befriend a robot named B12 who helps you communicate with these robots and he also learns about his identity along the way.Stray has some really good pacing. It's a very short game that can be completed in a single sitting, but it has exploration, puzzles, scripted action events, stealth, and collectibles. That's a lot to back into 5 hours and it's done very well. Let's start out with the obvious. This is the best representation of a cat in any video game. The animations are insanely realistic, you get a meow button that's pretty much useless, but it's there, and you can do cat things like knock stuff over, sleep, scratch on carpets and walls, and get paper bags stuck on your head that reverse the controls. While it may seem superfluous on the surface it helps add to the love of cats that the developers have even though none of these things really involve advancing the game further.Jumping around in the game is dealt with context buttons. The jump button will appear on top of the platforms you can climb onto. Outside of this, there are no other actions except accessing B12's menu to look at items and the flashlight. On occasion, you will have chase sequences in which you are running from a swarm of insect-like creatures, but most of Stray involves finding ways into rooms, platforming, and minor puzzles such as rolling barrels underneath things to jump up to. There are three major cities you end up in. The first one involves vertical platforming that lets you find lost music pages, B12 memories, and various item gathering to progress past certain points. The second city is a brief visit, but the last one is pretty large and looks beautiful. You can also talk to the various robots in the city to help you find out where to go or give you hints.My favorite parts of Stray were the areas in between cities. I liked climbing around, jumping, and running from the insects. The city areas slowed the game down too much for me especially trying to gather the items needed to progress out of the city. The game looks gorgeous with lots of neon lights, and it's surprisingly dark and gritty for a cat starring a cute cat. The story is pretty touching and tugs at your heartstrings towards the end. Despite the short length, the developers did a great job connecting you with these characters. However, there does seem to be a missed opportunity here. This is a game that would benefit from being open-world. A vast cyberpunk city with side quests and tons of areas to explore. While quite ambitious for such a small team, it would be great, and I think a lot of people are mistaking this game for something like Cyberpunk 2077 in its scope.Overall, the game is a lot of fun and quite enjoyable despite the limitations of exploration. The game is sadly, poorly optimized on PC with lots of stuttering, terrible temporal anti-aliasing, and shader caching issues. I played the entire game on Steam Deck and it suffered from stuttering when going into new areas. When it's all said and done, Stray is a very unique game and the love of the domestic feline companion oozes through the screen and pulls on your heart.

2013 This is one of my personal favourite games. The gameplay is basically Sid Meier's Pirates!, but with a medieval theme, more elaborate combat and more depth (you can earn XP to level up your character and companions, for example). After you choose your character's background, gender and starting attributes and skills, you set out building an army and doing miscellaneous tasks for the various lords and kings of the 6 factions and mercenary work. Once you gain enough renown and a decent army, you can become a lord for any of the factions and get your own castles and cities to look after, or even create your own faction to rule over. The gameplay as a monarch in the vanilla game is a bit lacking compared to playing as a lord, but there are mods like the Diplomacy mod that elaborate on this.The combat system is one of the most fluent i've seen in a medieval combat game. There are a varied amount of weapons, shields and weapon types to choose from, you can swing, chop or thrust your weapon by flicking the mouse and clicking and you can fight on foot or on a horse. Nothing feels delayed, there's a nice flowing feel to it and it's satisfying to kill things. Horse combat takes a while to get used to, but it's fun to charge people with a lance and to circle groups of soldiers while pouring arrows into them. It's especially fun once you get into a big 400 man battle. At times, it feels like playing a Total War game with all the soldiers running around and killing each other.To conclude, this is an addictive game that's well worth checking out.

2019 After having played close to 1.000 battles I think I have a pretty formed opinion on the game and to be honest I think people don't know what's to grind on an online game. I've seen plenty of people whining about how P2W the game is and so on and so forth, when the truth is that it isn't. People who pay AND play well can maybe advance tiers faster but that doesn't affect you because you only can face players of 2 tiers of difference with your actual ship. If you wanted to call the game that way it would be a P2F which is definitely not the same. Maybe people expect to get to the high tier content with no difficulty whatsoever. If they've played Heroes & Generals (as an example) then they would know what is to really grind on a game for real. There you not only don't get a noticeable reward feeling but you get punished because you end up spending more money the more modded you have your gun so what's the point to advance, right?. But leaving crybabies to their sadness and coming back to this game, if you liked the AC: Black Flag due to the naval battles you will probably have a lot of fun on this game. It's not as complicated as World of Tanks in my opinion, but it isn't simplified enough to feel like the game is "casualized" at the same time. Similarly to WoT here you advance by tiers and you have different branches (roles might sound more familiar to some players) on the country you select, with each one having it's weaknesses and strengths. You can advance pretty fast and not lose credits even being bad UNTIL you get to Tier 7. When you start playing Tier 8 you HAVE to know how to play properly if you don't want to lose credits, and even if you're not that good and you just do something you don't lose high amounts of credits. Another story is on T9 and 10, which is the reason why people whine about. At T9 you need to be really good and/or run premium time, or flags, or something that help you with costs. Another option is to go back to play on a lower tier for a few matches to recover some credits and then go back to your tier but people don't want to do this. People don't realize that not only the company need to sell things, but if everybody were able to play on top tier always then there would be no people to play with if you're new and are on a lower tier cause you would have astounding wait times. And even then, you don't need to pay to play on the Tier 10. Is just that you can't play ALWAYS on T10 unless you're really good and you aren't grinding multiple lines on multiple countries at the same time.TL;DRThe game is really fun, the battles are engaging and if you love naval battles you should really give it a try. Yes, the matchmacking is awkward because it doesn't sort players by how good or bad they play but for their ship tier. You play against people with 2 tiers of difference at maximum which is something fair to me. You don't hit the wall of costs of battle until you're at Tier 8-9 (out of 10) depending on how good you are. IDK, to me the game seems pretty fair towards the players (yes, even the free ones like me). If I had something to complaint about that would be a) the restriction they've put on Steam to not let you use your old WG account (yes, there is a workaround for it but you don't get achievements at least which would've been cool). And b) the fact that Limited events SOMETIMES have long tasks (which you can't complete at the same time because you have to end the previous task to start the next) for the time we have to play that event. Other than that is one of the few online games of this kind that I don't feel like a boring and endless grind and the advance in tiers is more noticeable (for the good and the bad) as you go up on tiers.

2023 Party Animals is a delightful and chaotic multiplayer game that has left me grinning from ear to ear. At first glance, the game's premise may seem simple: play as a variety of cute, cartoonish animals, such as rabbits, dogs, and penguins, and engage in brutal battles with each other. But as I delved deeper into the game, I discovered a depth and complexity that kept me coming back for more.The gameplay is fast-paced and frenetic, with a focus on frantic combat and quick reflexes. Each character has its own unique abilities and strengths, which adds a welcome layer of strategy to the proceedings. The rabbits, for example, are quick and agile, making them perfect for darting around the battlefield and dodging attacks. The monkeys, on the other hand, are masters of misdirection, using their prehensile tails to swing around the map and catch opponents off guard. And the penguins? Well, they're slow and plodding, but their powerful ice-based attacks make them formidable opponents in close combat.But what really sets Party Animals apart is its sheer sense of humor. The game's characters are all adorable and endearing, with expressive animations and hilarious death screams that will have you laughing even in the midst of intense battle. The stages themselves are also cleverly designed, with environmental hazards like spinning blades, falling platforms, and exploding barrels that add an extra layer of excitement to the mix.One of the most impressive aspects of Party Animals is its online multiplayer mode. With up to eight players competing in chaotic free-for-alls or team-based matches, the game's online capabilities are seamless and easy to navigate. The community is also surprisingly active, with many players creating their own custom matches and game modes.If I have any criticisms of Party Animals, it's that the single-player campaign can feel a bit lacking at times. The story is cute but forgettable, and the AI opponents can be a bit too easy to defeat. However, this is more than made up for by the game's addictive multiplayer mode and its wealth of customization options.Overall, Party Animals is a delightful and entertaining game that is sure to appeal to fans of fast-paced action games and cute cartoon characters. With its clever gameplay mechanics, humorous characters, and seamless online multiplayer capabilities, it's a must-play for anyone looking for a fun and lighthearted gaming experience.

Not everything is up-to-date.I played a ton of FSX and was unbelievably excited for this but it is pretty much ruined for me.PROS:-The graphics are amazing -The flying experience feels pretty accurate from my experience. -The world is MUCH more detailed and accurate than FSX, though a pretty spotty, except in hand-crafted sites. -The airplane cockpits and models are incredible, though not all the buttons are functional that would be useful in-game. (only like 5-10% of what you might wish for is missing.)-Real-time weather is great.-Always online, MMO-type world is neat, but I honestly haven't run into any other players. (Probably because I fly in non-populated areas.)CONS: -Not all of the airports are up to date. I flew to the one I used to fly out of two years ago and they haven't updated the runway and ramp, which was modified OVER 15 YEARS AGO. I'm not sure how their technology works, or how they can be this behind. A simple 'satellite' image would show the updates. -The cities might be a little less accurate than you hope, but the buildings are roughly the right size, shape, and position. (HUGE upgrade from FSX)-Some MAJOR landmarks are missing. Prime example: One of the most iconic tourist locations in Ireland is the Cliffs of Moher. You'll see it on 75% of travel brochures. In MSFS, they're literally a brown drop-off that looks like someone's first custom Warcraft map. This was AFTER the Ireland and UK update. UPDATES are the major issue. -The bulk of updating is done IN-GAME, taking up a huge chunk of your CPU and GPU. This means NO BACKGROUND UPDATING. -No download speed throttling, you can only pause it when a file fully downloads. (Sometimes they're 3GB files.) -60 of the 70 hours I have logged are from updates. (I have 25Mb/s internet, so that may be slow for others' standards.) -The excuse for this is that the game is always-online, but it'd be nice to have an option. The best workaround is to cache any areas that you want to use, then start steam offline for the rest of your playtime. -I ran into an issue with the current update where it'll restart a file's download infinitely, so I can never play again. I'll try uninstalling, but that's a HUGE commitment. I'm severely disappointed, because if you only fly once a month, there's a very good chance that you'll need to plan for 100GB updates and hope they download. It's so bad that I would seriously recommend thinking long and hard about if it's worth the effort. One of the most powerful ways to keep people coming back to your game is to remove friction: time to get in a lobby, time to boot, etc. but this game creates MAJOR friction. I could excuse EVERYTHING if they let us do steam-based updates. I'm going to uninstall this, reinstall it completely, and give it one more chance, then delete it from my account if it doesn't work.UPDATE: The uninstaller doesn't even work properly, I had to manually remove the 100GB. Drive C>Users>username>AppData>Roaming(Hidden folder by default)>Microsoft Flight Simulator. I did this, then reinstalled it and it got stuck on a file, redownloading it over and over forever. 2013 It takes every ounce of your energy to not take this game at face value, but is imperative to this sublime simulator that you don't. Yes, it is a game about driving trucks. Yes, the hauls get to be long distance. If you're looking for something that keeps you on the edge of your seat, with non-stop action, this is not your game.However, if you're looking for one of the most true to life, masterfully done, in-depth simulator you've ever sunk your teeth into, you've come to the right place.I remember joking with my buddies "LOL who wants to drive truck". Then a few weeks later, I find myself bored on a Saturday, lo and behold, ETS2 has a demo. I'll give it a shot, what do I have to lose? Just my entire Saturday.I can't quite put my finger on the exact thing that kept me playing this game for an 8 hour marathon session (I had stand alone before the Steam version). Beautifully, accurately crafted European countryside is a brilliant start. I plopped my trucking company down in London, as I wanted to tour the UK. I buy my first truck, and jump right into my first haul. Well, the minutes turn into hours, and suddenly I'm the owner of a successful trucking company, myself and 2 employees with my own fleet. As you progress, you level up and can spend points on hauling more dangerous/fragile cargo, longer hauls, more economic hauls (gas/wear and tear), and more. As your employees complete more hauls, they also level up and start bringing in more cheddar.My only gripe are the punishment systems. I was expecting active traffic police, aka being pulled over for breaking the law. However, the only punishment system is a series of fines. A fine for running a red light, for driving in the wrong lane, for hitting other cars, and traffic cameras (which I'm told are quite common in Europe) for speeding. No lost time in accident investigation or being pulled over, just a popup fine. The only other punishment system is a damage system to your truck and trailer. Damaging the trailer results in a poor score for the haul, and damaging your truck ends up costing you hefty repair bills. It's also worth mentioning that it seems you get to a point where you make enough money that any punishment is negligible. You make enough money on the haul where a few $500 tickets don't phase you, nor does a small repair.This game is a perfect getaway when you're looking for a lazy escape. Throw on your favorite tunes, and get to haulin'. ETS2 gets a 4/5.Apocky+Tawokwww.GuildLeaders.com

2023 Early Access Review "The radio fell silent; our overwatch in the ship murmured through the line about growling in the distance, and that he didn't feel safe. Looking behind me, I saw my partner ensconced in an orange jumpsuit on the walkway, carrying a giant axle in his arms.In the dimness of the industrial back-light he hunkered down and whispered in my direction, "Slow down, I think something's waiting in that hallway to the right."I nodded, and crept slowly across the grate toward the far exit, keeping the right hallway in my periphery.Skittering noises emanated from the side toward us. We walked faster.Suddenly, I heard a 'thunk'. My partner behind me stared down the hallway in horror. "IT'S THERE, RUN!"I bolted down the hallway, heart thumping my ears, breaching closer towards the engine room and my escape. Then, my partner's noises ceased. I heard more skittering, and a sickening crunch.I wildly turned, and illuminated in the faraway light, a teakettle slowly rolled down the hallway towards me. It stopped a few meters from my shoe, and there down at the left corner of the entryway was a single, pale foot.I backed away, hearing more skittering to my side.Before I could react it latched on to my visor, and my vision went black."This is an early access review, and for now, it is currently neutral. For starters, I CANNOT recommend this game to anybody who is completely immune to horror in videogames. If you are unable to live vicariously in the experience and feel some sort of attachment to your teammates through either roleplay or imagination, this is not a game for you. Where this game shines, is when you discover context about a situation that is outside your team's knowledge. Stumbling across the corpses of your allies wondering what the hell happened, or getting separated from your group and being forced into a pulse-pounding excursion make this game riveting to me. However, I am easily scared when playing a videogame, and live for the experience of this one rather than the progression.The game offers a good amount of unique threats and challenges. Learning about them through trial and error is actually really engaging and can sometimes be a great source of laughter. The industrial setting is gigantic and intimidating, and there is no end to the amount of possibilities for outstanding environments. Where this game lacks is in the overall gameplay loop. The progression is very tight, and sometimes death is inevitable. Not only is losing very costly to potential earnings in the future, it can also mean not meeting quota, which can start your entire team from the very beginning. Playing this game to win will likely be a frustrating experience, as opposed to treating it like an horror movie, where bonding with teammates makes the world more palpable. Due to the game being solo-developed, there is a distinct lack of variation in the environments at the moment. You will probably attempt to travel to two different 'moons' and wind up seeing the same scenery: trees, dust, or desert. Development of these things are essential to making the players feel like they've actually traveled to a new place, and not just a re-hash of another environment. The interiors also possess a short amount of variety as well, with said indoors being the procedurally generated portion of the game. It almost feels like there's only twenty interior rooms, and when you sprint through fifteen of them in a single run, it can feel way too predictable on subsequent runs. Hopefully more variation is implemented in the future.Another issue is how quickly you die. Death is almost always instant, and many times it can feel unfair, as you do not get a chance to counter the gimmick the enemy will toss at you. For now the methods to fight back are weak, and running away is usually your best chance. Hopefully long-term survival is buffed. With that in mind, be aware that the game time is also very short. Runs are limited to about fifteen minutes or so. Rescue operations or deep exploration become very difficult without rushing through wildly. The limited time also means that biomes with larger complexes cannot exist in the future, as things are already very tight. Adjustable rate of time passage would be an interesting addition. Overall the community is extremely friendly. As with new communities, nobody knows what's happening within the game, and everyone is there for the experience. I'm afraid of the loop being boiled down to uninteresting meta strats guarded by elitist pricks who only exist to minmax the game. This I believe would detract from the horror setting and elements, but to each their own.There is very great potential for more unpredictability and scares. To me this is a game meant to be enjoyed through the loss of teammates, the piecing together of what's happening around you, and discovery of the unknown. If those things suit you, then suit up, shut up, and stick close with your team.

I have completed the game and seen both endings. Currently in chapter 2 of new game plus. This game is visually stunning with captivating music and animation (i have rewatch them more than 6 times now XD). The story is actually layered with meaning that requires reading the journal of each monster or listen to dialogues to understand what it really meant. If you are only rushing through the game, you will only understand the surface level interpretation and miss out on the multiple meanings each chapter is trying to convey, how it ties with the destined ones journey at the end and hints of some hidden quests. This game is truly made with love and care. For the story, it helps if you have prior knowledge of journey to the west but it is not a requirement as this is set after the journey. You just need to read each of the journal entry as you obtained them. It is arranged in a way that slowly unfolds the background story. This game requires you to pay attention to what is written and listen to dialogue for potential hints. You will be rewarded.There is no map in game and invisible walls in certain areas. After playing it, i understand the design choice. By having no map, you have to look around to get your bearing and try to explore every possible area that might be a path. The invisible wall actually help in that regard. The game is visually stunning, the last thing i want is getting lost in an open world (map gets bigger in later chapter) or artificial high walls or impossible to reach areas that would ruin the beautiful scenery. The game also rewards those who explore by discovering rare items or secret quests that makes bosses of each chapter easier to beat. Combat is also very satisfying especially after you understood the mechanics. You actually have one block spell, 2 parry methods (not including certain transformations). Rock solid is an instant block that cost mana, resolute counterflow (smash stance) that cost one focus point or offence in defense (thrust stance) that is free. Stance parry requires at least one light attack followed by heavy attack to activate, so time your parry properly. This is on top of your dodge/perfect dodge. There is also a skill whereby you can dodge once without cancelling your attack chain so you can technically attack, dodge, attack, dodge/parry and so on. I do notice some input lag for healing but not a big deal. The game allows free reset of all your skill points (at shrine) and respec your stats upgrade in chapter 2 (hidden npc) so experiment on what works best for a given boss. What you experience in the start of the chapter is but a glimpse of the full fighting potential of sun wukong. You will be working your way up as you progress. And since you don't lose your progress, you are only going to keep getting stronger.I highly recommend this game. The game does not hold your hand but gives you hints and teaches you what to expect as it prepares you for later chapters as more complex battle mechanics are introduced. It has been a satisfying experience and i can tell a lot of work has been put in this game to make it. Totally worth the full price. 9/10 for me.

2016 Early Access Review Our only doctor, aptly named Doctor, got a bad case of the Mondays and decided to take a walk while the colony's leader suffered from an extremely infected neck wound he had recieved defending the colony. Our leader struggled bravely but without medical care he died a painful labored death. Farter, our brave leader's dog, took this loss especially hard and lacked an emotional coping strategy. He tore out our cook Herman's throat out as he was preparing his famous boomalope casserole. Sprinkles, the custodian, was the next to go. The dog found our one armed janitor enjoying a beer in the common room. Sprinkles defended himself admirably but all was in vain as there is no viable defense against a grief stricken canine. Farter ripped off Sprinkles' remaining arm and dutifully trudged outside. He found Doctor strolling amongst the palm fronds, feeling sorry for himself and presumeably writing weepy poetry about his trials and sorrows. Doctor pleaded his case to Farter. How could this dog not understand that the living room had been too dirty? THREE DIRT PILES IN THE LIVING ROOM!? How can he save lives if there are THREE DIRT PILES IN THE LIVING ROOM? What kind of kiddy pool operation would make a PROFESSIONAL work under conditions like that? Is it any wonder he had to get out of there and take a power jog? Surely, our great and brave leader would have understood, right? THREE DIRT PILES!Death did not come quickly for Dr. Doctor. The bite had crushed his spine and only after two hard days did he finally succumb to the elements and starvation. As for Farter, his job was over. It was time to rest. His victories had come at too great a cost and the defensive wounds he had taken each battle were taking their toll. Farter limped his way back into the colony base, past Herman still bleeding out amongst his boomalope meat, over Sprinkles' now armless body, by his master's gangrenous corpse, through the three dirt piles and into the freezer. Farter laid down. His frozen body was the last they found, behind a crate of strawberries.Good boy, Farter. Good boy.

2023 I grew up with Sonic Adventure DX and Sonic Adventure 2, and this game just isn't it. I'll be comparing this game with those games because others have drawn the comparison already, so I'll be giving my review in that context.It feels a lot like someone who had only ever played Breath of the Wild was told about Sonic Adventure by someone and this was their interpretation.It strikes the same sort of confusion into me as I'd expect to get if you gave Mario a gun and tossed him into Skyrim, but also added a handful of yellow ? blocks and pipes randomly throughout the landscape.I will also add that I have only played this for an hour, as I have decided to refund it. My negative points here may be invalidated further into the game, but I found them egregious enough that I'm just not willing to give the game the chance, and want my money back before Valve decides I enjoyed it too much.Having played Adventure and Adventure 2 again recently, comparing those to Frontiers:- Frontiers soundtrack does not come close to the older games. It's very "abstract" - stages have a random cacophony that sounds like American pop-rock/emo-rock, while the overworld has a very BotW "quiet random piano keys in the distant background" vibe. If you like that, go for it - I find myself missing the hard rock of the older games. I guess Jun Senoue/Crush 40 weren't involved at all.- While very pretty (unsurprisingly, graphics have come a long way since ~2000), the overworld feels very empty, and is reminiscient of a windswept and bleak Scottish island I visited several years ago. It's been peppered with a sort of playground of random little toys, enemies and minibosses, with nothing to offer any real cohesion or context. I don't feel very motivated to explore any of it after the first few minutes - I think this is a combination of a few factors.- Levels feel very short. Again, may be an early-game thing. Sonic Adventure 2 in particular had relatively complex levels with a few different paths through them, the complexity of Frontiers levels makes me think "mobile game".There are good things:- Controls are very good. This was a major frustration of the older games where camera angles were often fixed; this has fully embraced the dual-stick control system and feels good on a modern controller.- New take on abilities. In the older games, you had to find specific items in levels to unlock certain things. This lent itself to replayability (in a sense - my 9 year old self was a lot more patient than I am today), but could be frustrating, particularly when paired with the occasionally janky controls (remember trying to light dash over a line of rings and somersaulting off a cliff instead?). I find myself liking the unlockable "tree" abilities more.- Graphics are decent, as mentioned above. The general design and theme doesn't sit well with me, but the implementation of it is good.Overall the game feels like a confused mess trying to be Sonic Adventure game while also specifically targeting the Breath of the Wild audience. I compare with BotW a lot because I see the same "abstract digital something plus old stone ruins" stuff in both. Perhaps its a sign of my age that I find myself longing for a style from 20-25 years ago - this game is definitely a lot more modern, for better or worse. The soul of it is very different from what I'm used to and expect in a Sonic game. If you've only ever played Sonic Adventure DX/2 and find yourself missing the wacky, comic-book sort of action storytelling, I'm quite confident you won't find it in this game.

2020 "The truth is, the game was rigged from the start." Fallout: New Vegas is... another Fallout. That should already say a lot about it. It's good.This game takes place in New Ve- I mean, the Mojave Wasteland (Although a big part of the story is settled in New Vegas and it's clearly the main shining dot here). A big lovely desert with all the perks from a post-Great War location, such as: super mutants, giant mutated animals and a constant struggle of power. Lovely! Seriously now. The Mojave Wasteland was and it still is a desert, they nailed that perfectly. There's a LOT of locations to go to. Caves, cities, mountains, underground bases! VAULTS! So many locations with each of them being (mostly) different from each other. A lot of effort was put into them and it shows. So many items and loot scattered and hidden around... it was always nice finding a valuable item hidden between a seemingly empty room. Although it definitely felt boring and repetitive sometimes to just open every container in a room and hope there was something useful inside of them otherwise welp, you wasted time! My favorite location has to be Novac. A motel becoming a town and having its "No Vacancy" sign, now in ruins and only displaying "No Vac", being used as the place's name was such an interesting (and funny) background to the place. The dinosaur and the giant thermometer were also nice details. I loved that town so much that I still kept using it as my main "house" even though I already had other houses in far prettier and comfier places. The diversity in equipment in this game is simply AMAZING. So many outfits, so many drinks, so many drugs, drank an drugs... SO MANY GUNS!! From the throwing spear to the plasma grenade, from the 9mm pistol to the gatling laser, this game's weapon diversity truly amazed me. And the game's skill system made it really fun to make a character focused on certain weapons, adding even more fun to the whole deal (even if it didn't felt like it actually changed much).With the exploration and looting being so nice, it's a shame to know that the combat is HOT GARBAGE. The hud feels weird plus, mainly, gunplay feels clunky and actually aiming with guns feels like a chore. Most of time I just found myself either sniping an unmoving target with a shot to the head and if enemies were moving I'd just walk to them or wait until they were close enough to me so I could "aim" at their general upper-torso area and hope they got enough headshots to die. V.A.T.S. Truly is a mechanic made so you could ACTUALLY shoot at stuff. I tried using True Iron Sights during my first hours of the game and it felt so unnatural that I had to switch to the old normal game aim. It wasn't just the guns that felt bad to use, the melee combat was just... ouch. It can be summed in just running up to the enemy and spamming attack on them until they die or doing heavy running attacks (run + hold attack)/heavy attacks on them until they are forcefully thrown dead to the ground or, if you have companions (why wouldn't you?), just sitting back, relax, and watch your companions slowly poke away at the enemies' health bar while you do cheap potshots at the baddies. Animations mostly for the melee combat are just... not good. Everyone seems way too fast. Looking at your character doing a heavy running attack in third person (or better yet, looking at ANYONE doing a heavy running attack) they move WAAAAAY too fast. It's like they do an action that should take 5 seconds in 1 second. Bodies spin and arms move unnaturally fast. It's off-putting. Combat is basically you just shooting at enemies' weak spots/Heavily bashing enemies repeatedly until they drop dead while in-between drinking 10 bottles of Sunset Sarsaparilla and Nuka Cola while poking yourself with stimpacks... Still. Even with all that being said, I'd be lying if I said I didn't have fun with it. Fun made even better with the equipment and perks I had. Do you know how fun it is to pull out a Holorifle (GODDANGIT I LOVE THAT WEAPON SO MUCH) and Oneshot-Headshot a Legionnaire running at you and watching their body explode into a gory red paste?? AS FUN AS IT SOUNDS. The story is basically: you get shot by this dude. You don't die. You now want REVENGE. but just summarizing it like that makes me feel bad and is in general a bad way to talk about it. You have simply SO MANY CHOICES!! You can choose to do things your own way, ally with others or just plainly kill everyone. It's amazing! Factions and characters all have well fleshed out backstories and there's no "true" way to do things, you are supposed to do whatever you want to do (or roleplay, if that's your thing).One thing (or MANY things) that hampered my progress were bugs. This game is REALLY buggy and sadly it shows a LOT. It crashed about 30 times for me during all the time I spent with it and I played it for about 130 hours. That's one crash every 4.3~ hours (quick mafs). That's really not good. Now it would be ok if it were just crashes, I save like a maniac anyways, but textures "flashing". Enemies bodies bending and "stretching" infinitely across the horizon, items "re-setting" themselves when you pick something where other items are (now this seems more like an engine thing but I'll still add it to the list) and having the sound slowly disappearing until I couldn't hear anything and it crashing after that. Random crashes, crashes after entering or exiting an area, items noclipping through the ground and other smaller things (killing an enemy and seeing their body fly to the horizon, Companions getting "stuck" somewhere and going around a massive area to get to you, etc). This game is RIDDLED with bugs and even though some were small and funny, saving every 3 minutes because at any moment you could just crash and lose progress is not a fun thing. I had some mods to help ease the bugs too and they still happened. Ouch.Oh wait. This game has "Vegas" in its name. That's right folks. Gambling, games of chance and casinos! Yay! Everything that I hate. Now this is more of a personal opinion but I just dislike anything gambling-related so naturally with this game having "NEW VEGAS" stamped in bright and shining letters I couldn't help but go "eugh" every time I saw anything gambling-related... which is about half of the game and one of the game's main focus. Ok. Still, I have to say, everything was so well made. Roulette, Slots, Blackjack... I can't help but feel happy whenever I win BIG and end up leaving the place with 5x the amount I put in the machine. This whole "odds" thing also ends up being a main point of the game, considering the Courier survived getting double headshot by Benny and how he is the "Wild Card" in the New Vegas power struggle. Music: Game music? Eh. It sets the mood and can be ominous and scary sometimes (the one with the laugh in the background is a tad spooky) but I wonder who thought that nails on metal, horns being blared and more cacophonies like that would sound like something good Hoover Dam music is a MASSIVE bop though . Radio music, though? FANTASTIC. Some absolute BANGERS there. Big Iron, Ain't That A Kick In The Head, Something's gotta give and many many more jazzy classic old tunes to wish for a nuclear winter to.Fallout: New Vegas has a lot of problems and it simply felt boring sometimes to do the same stuff over and over again but goddangit was the grind... "fun". Getting better guns and armor, finding secrets, doing actually interesting missions and shaping the future of New Vegas... it was fun. The game does feel dated and "ugly" but it still has charm and I had a nice experience with it.Good game!

review: 2020 Early Access Review Have you ever wanted to build an industrial supply chain? Ever wanted to get machinery running at perfect efficiency? Want to run water and oil pipes across a hostile alien landscape? Of course you have! Just like compound interest, the sooner you start the better you'll be off, so just buy it now and race toward perfect optimized manufacturing today!PROS: -- An enjoyable planet to explore and plunder -- A progression system that provides rewards you'll actually want (Jetpacks and larger industrial storage?! Sign me up!) -- Adorable slug friends that you can harvest for the sake of increased productivity. -- An incredible amount of control on the machinery. Find the exact spot in your supply chain that's bottlenecking your production and either overclock the machines using slug-friends or underclock other parts of the chain for the sake of efficiency. Or just stockpile the over-produced parts. Maybe you'll need thousands of iron rods one day! -- Exploration is rewarded but not needed. Exploring for slugs or crashed ships rewards you with overclocking devices (that aren't expended, so no maybe-I'll-need-that-later worries) and alternate crafting recipes (that usually take more raw goods but produce items quicker but they always have a use in some strategy of optimization), but if you'd rather only leave your home base to find a resource point and chose to focus on production you aren't missing out on anything but flawless optimization. Which, while arguably the point of the game, is not actually required. -- First person makes the production all feel like your work. An overhead camera makes you feel more like a foreman or a god simply ordering things to be done where first person enforces that it's all your own hard work and that makes for a lot of satisfaction at a job well done. -- Lines are used when placing buildings to show you when what you're placing is lined up with buildings or pipelines and assembly lines, making it a lot easier to get everything just right than if you have to go off of anything else. CONS: -- Some of the aliens are mean and don't like you exploring their planet. :( -- Sometimes the only oil is kilometers away and that's a lot of pipe. -- It's still in early access and multiplayer is even newer so minor graphical glitches in multiplayer aren't remotely unexpected, but they're there. It's funny in multiplayer watching someone run into a pipe for a few minutes before the game figures out where they actually are and less fun when you're trying to chop down trees and the game isn't removing the models. I've only encountered these issues in multiplayer. Single player has been really solid, particularly for an Early Access game. -- Being in first person is a real give-and-take. You can build towers to get a better view but it still makes laying out a perfect production line a bit harder than an overhead camera production game. EDIT: As of Update 5, there's a hoverpack that connects to power lines and this makes it much easier to layout your production line from above!As with any early access game, only buy it if you _really_ want to support the developers or you're happy with the product as it is now. All too often an early access game is stuffed full of promises of great things to come before the project gets cancelled and you're left with a boring and barely functional shell of a game. Not here! Satisfactory is 100% worth buying as it is. It's got more than enough features for hundreds of hours of fun and it's stable enough (my only issues have been graphical and only in multiplayer) that you won't be frustrated trying to play an incomplete game. If the studio got bored tomorrow and quit working on this you'd still have an amazing game. So if it looks like your kind of game, just pick it up now and enjoy it.

2015 Where to start, I wonder. I wish Steam would show my real hours in this sim. We are talking about 1000’s. I joined early 2009 and even I thought this is good, it wasn’t my thing at the moment. Learning curve was really steep because I didn’t know how to drive a race car. Rare are those who do. I was too stubborn to admit it and seek for help, yet there was a huge community to offer it if I would’ve just asked.But the worst thing was the pressure when racing. I could not take the adrenaline rush which was overwhelming. I seriously thought I’m going to have a heart attack, and I’m not alone with this one. No matter how well I did in practice, my hands and feet were shaking so much in race that I couldn’t drive properly. If you spin or drive out of the track, nobody waits for you. If you crash, your race is done. And races aren’t just 3 lap sprints, but even at the Rookie level they last for 20 minutes. You have to stay focused for the whole time, and then you should be fast also. It was too much for me and I quit.I went back to other titles, of which I’ve driven almost all since late 80’s. But I found out that they gave nothing to me anymore. There was simply no thrill in any of them. Racing or other. I felt like I’m totally numb. After a period of time, I renewed my subscription to iRacing and that’s been a big part of my life ever since. Now I need that thrill and I need that adrenaline rush.Iracing can bite you hard sometimes. Frustration can be off the scale. But on the other hand the success feels so good you’d like to laugh and cry at the same time. I can’t think of any other game that gives one so much satisfaction.Iracing should not be approached like a game, and not because of the age old “it’s a sim, not a game” argument. But because it’s a hobby. It’s not a game you play through, or even a sim-like game you play over and over again like Civ, until next version comes out. You can never play it through and it never repeats itself any more than real racing. And not like many racing games out there, you’re not buying a new version anytime soon. Major updates come 4 times a year, and iRacing is planned to be there at least next ten years. This was just recently confirmed. One can argue over individual aspects of iRacing vs. other sims. And many times other sims win these arguments. But as a whole picture, in all that comes into one single service (and that’s what iRacing is – a service) iRacing is without a slightest doubt the king of the hill. I do, from the bottom of my heart, wish there was some other sim that was better than iRacing. I would buy it in a heartbeat. But there isn’t. So for now I’m going with the best one out there.One thing is astonishing about iRacing, and it’s the fact it does the open lobby gaming better than any other online game or sim out there. That is something anyone has hard time to prove wrong. And since we are talking about an online sim, that is its strongest point. Another thing is the community side. It takes quite some time to understand how strong and wide-ranging it is.I’m not going into actual “game mechanics” here, since I don’t want to get into frustrating arguments over people who don’t take time setup their gear properly and don’t understand the iRacing’s long-term development plan.If you decide to give it a go, be darn sure to go to the forums and ask guys how to set up your system by telling what hardware you got. Someone will reply within 15 minutes. And then, have fun.

2013 I hated Warframe for years. I didn't like how mindless the combat was. I didn't like how grindy the process of earning anything was. I didn't like how every weapon did the same thing but just looked different. But all that changed in 2016. Warframe's balance shifted from a World of Warcraft "Nerf everything" style to a DotA "Everything is OP in it's own way" method, and it's glorious. GAMEPLAY:-Weapons are finally fun to level and collecting a vast armory is an absolute joy.-Missions are no longer pointless kill-5-magical-pig grinds and are more like choose your own adventures. Very Killing Floor / Payday-esque, except SPACE NINJAS.-Movement isn't restricted to console-like loot hallways and reminds me more of Tribes than I'd like to admit. -You can play the game like Elder Scrolls and ignore the "main quests" and story completely to just do alerts. I didn't start doing quests until I was 600+ hours in.-Every 3 months new Prime parts (Arcana-esque cosmetics with minor perks) are released and available for 140$ (!!!!) but DE allows you to craft them in game for free with a little bit of effort. I've done this every time, for free, without having to spend a dime on the game. -Nothing requires a team, you can solo the entire game as far as I'm aware. It's as MMO as you want it to be.-Rocket League-esque Lunaro mode.-Pokemon Snap quests (I'm not joking, these devs are awesome.)-Tamigachi pets which can join you in combat or simply dig up loot. Space dogs, floating robot eyes and soon magic space cats to tame and breed.-Full PhysX combat and gore combined with abilities identical to jedi force powers makes fighting fun and interesting. I love throwing people off cliffs or slicing them in half. -Warframes are like Heroes/Champs and have their own role/playstyle. Vauban plants traps, Ash's ultimate is identical to Omnislash and Ember throws fireballs. Combat for spellcasters is very much like Skyrim (free targeting / throwing nukes) and City of Heroes (press 3 to freeze everyone around you, collect loot to restore mana quickly) Healers heal through combat and not passive beam nonsense like every other game these days.-Everything is modular/customizable Crazy things you can do: Combine different elemental enchantments on your weapon to make a new one.Stack crit% well over 100% so every hit is a critical. Your criticals can crit red numbers.Strap tons of +damage % to a slow-swinging axe and cleave everything in half in one click.Stack lots of +% Range and nuke an entire room or blink across the map.-Gameplay scales well into "End game" depending on your commitment. It's a PVE game, so how much you commit is up to you, but the ability to buy, sell and trade "Primed Mods" means you are never done if you want to squeeze out an extra % of damage. (Primed Pressure Point costs a lot, but if you invest in it the damage scales past normal Pressure Point you get for free.)Free versions are practically as good as Primed, but the option to min-max to all hell are available for hardcore folks.-EXP is based on how much of the game you've experienced meaning it's impossible to find noobs at high levels. Levels are a reliable way to gauge how invested a player is and how knowledgable they are at the game. I LOVE THIS SYSTEM because it's the OPPOSITE of modern MMO's are designed - The game does not START at END-GAME. To increase your level you gain "mastery" which is given when you use/level a new weapon, frame or item to level 30. Very Planetside 1-esque and means you're always playing with new tools you'd normally never even consider - Nunchucks, Bows, Crossbows, Electric Whips, Dual swords, a bladed staff... Grab the blueprints for in-game money and craft 'em all. Then go adventure until they're level 30, sell the item OR craft it into something else (Craft 2 pistols together to make the Akimbo version, or turn a katana into a two handed blade of death, combine two assault rifles into a pistol-slot akimbo item. It's hilarious and fun, Love these devs.) ECONOMY: -Free to play game where you can actually get premium currency by just playing: Doing missions and Void towers nets you random Prime parts which you can sell to other players for real money currency. It's very easy to make a lot of Premium Currency without spending a dime. Made 100p off one piece last night. -Logging in has daily rewards, including 75% off (!!!) currency coupons - Buy 200$ worth of platinum for 50$ and get 600+ hours out of Warframe instead of 6 hours in some steam sale game for the same price. -Devs give you the option to buy anything for crazy high prices (in platinum) BUT Player-set prices are ROCK BOTTOM. You can buy Saryn Prime's pieces (3 pieces + blueprint to craft them together) for 120 platinum(1-3$ usd) TOTAL (1 trade with 1 player), or 10p per piece. (4 trades with 4 players) Sites like warframe.market[warframe.market] make this an absolute breeze but if you knew how to use Trade Chat in World of Warcraft it's the same thing. A little bit of effort saves you 80$ usd. -The option to pay the devs (support the game) at much higher prices is available if you choose to not interact with people at all / instant grantification -Everything in the game is crafted on your ship except for exclusive cosmetics, but every mmo/f2p has those.-Healthy economy with people buying and selling all the time at reasonable prices, very competitive market model means you can barter for better prices if you know what you're doing. Or just pay the price listed for hastle-free trades.-Boosters increase amount gained, not drop numbers, thus rare resources stay rare and no pay2win (It's a PVE game anyway, so it's not a big deal.)-Pay for Convienece model makes casual play tolerable (Crafting takes 12 hours, so queue up some things and go to bed/work/school/etc) Eve-like offline progress. Can pay to rush things (3 day uber items are 50p which is 50cents-1$ which is reasonable when people spend 2.50$ on crate keys in other games and get 0.03$ items for it without blinking an eye)-It's entirely possible to collect all of the "Prime" versions of warframes for under 40$ usd, most only costing 1-5$ and Ember Prime currently rocking a whooping 20-30ish in platinum. (I paid 800p for the set but most of the prices I see are 1200-1500p) Basically you can get all the premium stuff just playing the game, selling parts to other players and then buying the parts you need from other players in the Ironforge-like locations (hub cities) Or do what I did and get a 75% off coupon, buy some currency and grab all the premium gear for a fraction of it. I've only bought currency one ever and It's all I needed - check out my screenshots.-Devs support Humble Bundle often with FREE boosters, skins, weapons,etc (Donate 0.01 for promo keys) Or 1$ (The week-long boosters during E3)-Anniversary events award any player who finished the tutorial with incredible gear. Dual swords that use a discontinued (Vaulted) Prime Sword model? Hell yes.2016 Warframe pretty much requires you to use the wiki as nothing is explained in game, so if you're looking for an adventure you can go in blind and just figure it out as you go - most people will use a wiki or ask friends though. Next update (summer 2016 is expected) will streamline the map and make the new player experience less of a chore to research.Just playing the game you'll eventually run into developers also playing the game, which is an awesome thing to see. Met them at Pax East - Literally the coolest people at the convention and super friendly and fun. They're the reason I gave Warframe another try and I'm so glad I did, so the least I can do is write a legit review detailing the game if you haven't tried it yet. {LINK REMOVED}Referral link if you'd like to start with boosters / play with me.

overall i really enjoy this game, it's a good way to kill time, though it can be incredibly formulaic. this is my first gundam breaker game, but i've heard most people prefer 3's gameplay. the missions generally come down to destroying as many mobile suits as you can as quickly as possible, and most missions don't put up much of a challenge, especially in the story. the moment-to-moment action feels very similar to a dynasty warriors gundam / gundam musou game, but with fewer enemies, less complex scenarios and objectives, and slightly more depth to the combos.the real strong point of this game is in the customization, you could easily spend hours at a time creating your perfect custom mobile suit just on an aesthetic level, let alone the time spent fine-tuning its skills and buffs to make an overpowered loadout. the depth and variety of aesthetic customization is nearly perfect, and most of my complaints with it would just be bias that more of my personal favorite obscure mobile suits aren't here (haze'n-thley II-rah when?). if i had to pick a universal negative though, it would be the menus for in-depth color, finish, and decal customization. some of the options are several menus deep, especially when you start color picking new palettes. an option to save your own preset palette would be nice, though i don't see myself using it as much because i like to pick exact color applications. the decal placement tool is really finicky and sometimes completely changes orientation, especially on curved surfaces, so most of the time i left the decals in their default placement. another feature i don't see but would absolutely love is a customization mode that is fully for cosmetic purposes and doesn't require you to currently own a piece to use it as long as you've previously acquired that mobile suit. like a gunpla dress-up with no stats involved.there are a few big negatives, namely the story and the menu UI.the menus for ... really anything are too difficult to navigate and easy to get lost looking for one specific option. some buttons and sliders in the customization seem to work inconsistently and have to be understood through trial-and-error. as i said before, some options are buried behind several sub-menus and it's not always obvious what the point of those sub-menus are. managing your items is a complete nightmare, and the filters and sorting options are obtuse, unhelpful, straight up don't do anything for certain item types, or just don't work intuitively. same goes for abilities and stats themselves. some of them are so obtuse or poorly translated that they've already become notorious ("wild dance" and "hate up" are obvious examples). others seem really redundant or just poorly explained, and there's no in-game glossary to explain what these do ... except that one item type DOES have an explanation screen that tells you what abilities do but still does a poor job at explaining them AND has unweighted randomized debuffs included so you could just get one of these items that has all downsides and no upsides. another frustration is that certain items will pop up with an "are you sure?" prompt when you want to merge them into another item, for high-rarity items, items with a paired part, items that are already saved to one of your mobile suits, or when the item you're merging them with is already max level. so in theory you could click one item and have to click through 4 "are you sure?" messages to do what you want (these prompts default to "no"). all of this combined makes leveling up and improving items incredibly tedious.the story on the other hand is really worth ignoring if you just want to burn through the missions to unlock everything. but if you choose to stick with it, you'll be met with a "quirky" band of misfits:tao: the nerd who is annoyingly pathetic and "someone wrote a gamer character"-corelin: the slightly tsundere girl who is secretly really tragic (they promise)lillin: obviously a robot but they will annoyingly drag out any and all discussion surrounding her as if they didn't let the audience in on this fact the moment she was introducedsheena: would probably be the best character if it weren't for the fact her whole story is about how difficult it is to be rich and important and how being really really rich is actually tragic"mister gunpla": someone using a fake name and avatar who pretends to be good at the game but doesn't really seem that experienced but is revealed to be someone who should be really experienced??mashima: annoying pickup artist "ladies' man" who literally can't open his mouth without saying something creepy or embarrassing, and yet everyone just accepts him and says "oh, you!" when he does his white knight shtick. literally says "m'lady" multiple timesand besides that you have tons of other annoying or bland characters that aren't worth recounting in this review. the plot itself is just "this is a video game. play video game" until the end when it gets worse. i have to also address that they use "AI" in the sense of a true artificial intelligence but conflate it with our current trend of learning algorithms that use the buzzword "AI" ... and in turn basically just feed every misconception about it while being complicit in manufacturing consent. so that's cool.on the more pet peeve-y side of things, they ask you to name your character and make your own custom profile, custom gunpla, etc, but also assume you're male and thus every single line of dialogue referring to you, the player, uses male pronouns and male nicknames. in fact they bring up the gender of characters often enough that it would just be weird and awkward if you're not male and not making a point to embody a male character for the sake of the story. in most games this is avoided by either recording different dialogue for different gender options, using non-gendered terms, or just cleverly writing dialogue that avoids that issue. but this game seems to be making a point of bringing that to the forefront as often as possible.on the other end of annoying writing is the fact that in this game you're very overpowered. you have an infinite on the team for each mission. 2023 Lies of P isnt just another souls clone, its a love letter to fromsoftware and fans. Developers managed to preserve what makes souls games tick and at the same time add enough elements of their own to make their game stand out. Not only that but it also comes as a complete package: great gameplay, great locations design, great visuals, great soundtrack, great characters and story, etc.Game's difficulty is slightly on a harder side. LoP gives equal importance to blocks, parries and dodges, and expects player to learn when its better to use different mechanics instead of always spamming the same move.There aren't many weapons (around 40) but almost everything has its own unique moveset and its possible to make custom weapons by combining blades and handles from different stock weapons.World design/progression is linear with plenty of optional and rewarding exploration to do inside each area.LoP doesn't have the most technologically advanced graphics but visual design is simply amazing and its the most optimized UE4 game I've ever seen.Storytelling is much more straightforward than typical fromsoftware, most of the story is given through cutscenes and dialogues (with some exceptional voice acting). And at the same time there are still many lore details left to discover on your own.Overall Lies of P easily deserves 9/10 and in my opinion is the only "clone" comparable to fromsoftware's own games.

2023 Admittedly I'm making this review because of the Autumn Sale event. With that out of the way, I completely recommend this game.You will likely die, a lot... I certainly did in the beginning. And over time, got good enough to manage basic survival on my own. This game is harsh, and quite unforgiving. I don't think I have any issues with the game itself. In fact, I'm glad the devs continue to still work on it. I don't think there's an update yet I dislike. And the shorts they create along side them are wonderful. I haven't tried all of the characters after their update, but I am glad that they did character refreshes. Wolfgang and Wx needed one the most. Since one would eat up all the food, and the other would eat up all the gears. But those issues are no more. The only refresh that seems to have an issue, is Wormwood's ability to make regular berry bushes. They require juicy berries to craft, which spawn on a different berry bush. And unless I've missed something, which is possible, they don't spawn in the same world. So you either have one or the other on the map, never both.As you can see from my playtime, I clearly like the game a lot. But this game also takes a lot of time to "progress." I don't really consider that to be a con. But it becomes frustrating when dealing with certain players. It's one thing to be new, or a noob. We've all been there. But there are some with nothing to do in their lives besides troll. I happened to still be alive on an official server by myself. When someone joined trying to convince me to restart the world. When I didn't give in, they tried to jynx me hoping I would die during the hound wave. I didn't, so they, somehow, found where I was and used a fire staff to burn down my base. And because it was just the two of us, there was nothing I could do about it. What made it worse, is there were several US servers that were probably already empty that they could have restarted.Now obviously this sort of thing isn't new for online games. And if the server had more people on it, that person would have been kicked. And the server would have been rerolled to the previous day to repair the damage. But it is something that still has the potential to happen, so it's worth mentioning. Especially when so much real world time spent progressing through a season can get ruined by just one person at a moments notice.I guess another con could be that it's sometimes hard to understand what to do besides survive. It's hard for me to adequately speak on this topic, because I've played the game long enough that it's hard to put myself in the shoes of a new player. But the devs felt similarly and made changes to the ui that they hoped would help address those issues.All in all, it's definitely worth trying. I feel the game has something for just about every type of player. Base building, cooking, gardening, fighting, exploring. And even has mod support, some of which are usable on official servers. Generally, the more people you have, the better your chances at survival.Edit: It is possible to have both berry bushes on the same map. I'm not sure how often it happens, but sometimes the other type will be in the caves. So as long as you have caves enabled, there's a chance for the other berry type.

Dying Light: 100% COMPLETION REVIEW If you love completing games, take a look at our curator site. Ok so, games where you forget completely what your objective was supposed to be due to getting distracted with its own gameplay and just roaming around are absolutely awesome. Dying Light AKA the Vertigo Simulator just so happens to be one of them. You can completely ignore quests and instead go ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, killing every zombie in the open world, much like I myself did before doing the quests! I suggest completing them however, to start leveling up and making combat that much cooler. I keep laughing my ass off when I climb high buildings, then grapple the zombies and throw them off. I then watch them fly!Where Dying Light shines, is definitely on the gameplay. It has the perfect recipe: responsive parkour movement, and zombies. The cherry on top is the punchy feeling of melee combat. Crane feels very nimble as we control him. And I have to mention how well optimized this game is, despite the graphics being pretty high quality!The story is where it drops the ball. I wouldn't say it sucks exactly, since you do feel motivated and truly understand Crane's feelings and actions. Things are justified, and the environmental lore is not too bad either. Harran feels very much alive, like there used to be an actual thriving city before chaos struck. However, it's nothing to write home about, in essence. It's your average Far Cry-esque plot, with a villain, people you're supposed to root for, a reason is given to hate this and that character, etc. Everything is there, but it's not incredibly well written.The Following DLC manages to have an even worse story than the base game, with poorly written characters, and nobody's personality is expanded on. The whole plot could be summed up to two or three sentences. Again, the gameplay is to be celebrated here: despite parkour being one of the selling points of Dying Light, The Following cuts down on it and instead has us explore the countryside, with significantly less opportunities to climb stuff, but gives us a pretty cool buggy to drive instead! Running over zombies never gets old, and it's a nice breath of fresh air.Hellraid is a strange DLC, to say the least. It's a totally separated short story that looks like a Skyrim quest mod more than anything. The "Mostly Negative" reviews for it here on Steam speak for themselves. Terrible DLC, that feels like a boring hack-and-slash fest. Even though this game genre is absolutely amazing, Dying Light does NOT pull it off well. One of the worst DLCs I have ever played, despite having a bit of fun.There's a Co-Op multiplayer component in Dying Light. Personally, I didn't enjoy it too much, since the game is now pretty much dead. Every player is either AFK on the pause menu and doesn't acknowledge your presence at all, or just runs laps around a safezone, or kicks you instantly. Zombie invasions where people "invade" your lobby and have to attack you while playing as a night hunter is too unbalanced to be fun. The concept sounds great, but once you start getting stomped by players with 3k hours in the game while you want to play the game at your own pace, you'll realize it's poorly executed. Dying Light is best played entirely as a singleplayer experience. Plus, seeing other players ruins the immersion entirely, since the story is about YOU, Kyle Crane, being the best runner in The Tower capable of everything, and having someone else just throws that narrative point right out the window.When it comes to achievements, it's where the game gets EVEN worse, and it hits the fan... As a committed achievement hunter for 5 years at the writing of this review and 55 finished games on my belt, I declare Dying Light the WORST completion I have ever undergone. The vast majority of them can be obtained solo and pretty easily. Some are extremely difficult to pull off, but doable, shall you put on your try hard shoes. But the ones that require the cooperation of other players towards the same goal, and the ones that directly need RNGesus' blessing are the equivalent of waterboarding torture. Trying to accomplish and/or organize anything with the VERY few people playing a dead multiplayer game is a terrible endeavour, and I'm referring to the "Together Till The End", "Polyamory", "Harran Athletics" and "Lucky 7" achievements. Relying on pure luck and exploits is also an idiotic move from Techland, when it comes to the stupidly named "♥♥♥♥ Homini Lupus Est" achievement, that is IMPOSSIBLE to unlock once you advance enough in the main story, and the only mean to farm for it is by using a famous exploit.Despite all these negative points I've listed, Dying Light remains one of my favorite games of all time. This game is incredible in what it does well! I expect to put more hours in it in the future, long after reviewing it, since it is permanently up for revisiting for me! 2023 I make this review with little comparison to the rest of the genre. I have played every game, 100% of all of them, I am not a elitist of the genre but I enjoy them a lot. I speak from the casual dad, familiar with the genre.Graphics: Beautiful top down. Big note for me, I want to be drawn in. I don’t want to spot imperfections or remember it’s a game. I want to be excited, interested, and enjoy the developer’s hard work. That said, the game is flawless in artwork. The environment, layout, the detail kept me focused on the game. Nothing stuck out and made me get distracted and focus on the bad points of anything. The setting, the lighting, and the music and tone are married together in amazing harmony. In the artistic viewpoint, the game crushes it is setting the ambience, scene, and tone. Truly A+ Here.Weapons: This game is the best in the genre, my one of two comparisons I intend to make. This is the best in genre for picking a weapon you want, customizing it how you like, and playing with it. There’s only a couple of weapons that make the experience “easier.” From my view, any weapon is workable, and fun based on your style in this game. Sweats will say this is the case for any entry. I speak as a casual dad with sweaty hands (sometimes.)UI: The interface and HUD are very clean and simple. I like that the game has notifications for when side quests progress and reminds you of the location for the quests. It’s super helpful, and nice not to have to refer to google and fextralife to understand what steps need to be taken.Below is where we start to become critical of the game.Difficulty: I found this to be an easier game for the most part. Aside from 3 bosses with aggravating skills and status affects and 2 world areas where they throw lots of mobs and multiple effects at once. The aforementioned 5 points are not hard they are just punishing. This game is heavy on the parry, only in a handful of spots it’s your dodge helpful. You’re gonna be tested heavily on your parry. This game starts to fall off for me because, the “challenge” is punishing enemies with 2-9 attacks continuously, and one missed block can be detrimental. Now, some of you may read that and say, well that’s a fair challenge. But there’s 2-6 enemies doing the same thing. This may come off as a whine but play it yourself. You’ll see. Added note, You as the player have a plateau of damage, meanwhile the enemies will only get stronger and more health. Story/Mechanics: The story started very interesting, quickly got predictable. Loosely explaining it to a friend, we were able to guess the ending clearly. The story is easily found throughout the game in pick-ups, which is nice. Unfortunately, the plot twists don’t catch you off guard. The “Lie” mechanic that determines the ending, but “lying” in the game isn’t always clear what’s the lie, and what’s the effect? Theres a actually “nifty” easter egg drop, after the game for the sequel but personally I have no interest in a sequel. The game captures the bones of a SoulsBourne game but, it lacks some creativity to really be a great title for me. It’s a good game, but some glaring issues for me in between the lines. The last third of the game starts to get un-creative and punishing. It's great visuals and weapons don't pull it that hard. If they do make the sequel they hint at, there's a good amount to fix to really make it a great game and an original entry. It’s a solid 6/10 game, play it once.

2020 Fantastic little roguelite. If you used to play around with those falling sand browser games back in middle/high school (I was obsessed with them for a while), you'll find a lot to love here. It's got wonderful pixel art graphics, fun physics, chaotic gameplay, and a really great soundtrack. But damn is it hard. Usually my deaths are because I can't help but kick everything I see, which often sets off a chain reaction ending in myself being either lit on fire, doused in acid, or exploded. The games internal logic makes sense once you've played it for a little while, but when you start you may find it difficult to know what is helpful or not. If you're familiar with other rougelites/roguelikes, trial and error is the name of the game in Noita.The wand editing system is also a lot of fun and something unique to this game, besides the interesting physics system. Wands you find come preloaded with spells, but you can also take those spells off and put them into other wands, so you can mix and match until you get the perfect loadout of death. But you have to be careful, because sometimes the wands you make can end up killing you if you don't know what you're doing with it. It's a great system with a lot of risk and reward. You can make a wand that shoots crystals that explode on contact with enemies or projectiles, or a wand that digs through terrain, or a wand that literally just fires actual nuclear bombs. Or a wand that does all of the above at once. There's quite literally thousands of options. You can also pick up and use flasks which can hold any sort of element in the game, which can lead to a lot of interesting situations.There's also a lot of hidden secrets in the game that I've only just begun to uncover. I'm sure it will take me quite some time to see everything this game has to offer. Luckily, as much as I suck at the game and keep dying, I feel like I learn something new each time, and the deaths I suffer are more chances to learn. It never gets old kicking a powder keg into a shotgun-wielding enemy and seeing him explode into gibs and gold. The game also rewards you for these "trick" kills by making the enemies drop more gold.Overall, I've thoroughly enjoyed my time with Noita so far, and I don't think it'll get old anytime soon. There's a lot more that I could say in this review but it's probably best that you just pick up the game and see for yourself. It's well worth it.

2017 Portal 2 is a fantastic successor to a fantastic game. The original Portal was a game that had everything it needed and nothing more, and while this made for a tight, filler-free experience from start to finish. it also failed to satisfy many people, who saw the massive potential the mechanics had and demanded more to whet their appetites. This is the game to satisfy those people. Portal 2 takes the original game's concept and runs with it, adding a ton of new ways to sove puzzles and interact with the environment, from light bridges to lasers to three types of gels, each having a unique impact on the surface it coats. While this adds variety and a greater play time, it comes at the cost of adding some flab to the slim as a whistle Portal experience, meaning that some of this game's playtime is wasted on pointless filler, something that could not be said of Portal 1. However, the advantage of this is a much greater sense of scale and ambition, making the game feel more substantial and leaving the player less hungry. It's like choosing between a small portion of a fantastic steak and a medium portion of a fantastic steak that's just a tad overdone. Which one you prefer will depend on whether you want the best experience possible of if you don't want to feel hungry at the end of the night. The story is also top-notch. The principle of more carries over here, as more characters are added and more time is spent developing the world and the characters and the plot. Again, which plot you prefer is down to personal preference, but either way you'll be getting a lot of laughs. Finally, on top of all that, this game has a fantastic co-op mode, which, unlike the single player mode, is short, sweet, and has no filler to get in the way of some of the most brilliant puzzles in the Portal canon. If you can find a friend willing and able to play, this extra alone is worth the price of the game.

2017 TL;DR Nier Automata is the best game I've played since The Witcher 3 and it's expansions.Nier Automata tells a story about very bleak distant future where Earth became a battleground between human-like androids and machines controlled by aliens. Some time before events of the game humanity succumbed to alien invasion and relocated to the moon bases. Now elite android units are sent to the ruined surface to hopefully finally reclaim Earth. If this sounds outright bizarre and silly to you then I assure that there is more than meets the eye and story of Automata becomes much more complex and interesting as you go. It is sad, beautiful and very unpredictable.Gameplay is another part of Automata that stands out. Developed by people behind Bayonetta and MGR:Revengeance, it is fast, fluid, very responsive and deceptively simple at first glance. Between fast and heavy attacks, weapon switching on the fly, quick dashes and acrobatic dodges you have a lot of options to approach any threat that may come your way. Androids don't use ranged weapons, instead they are aided by robotic drones, with variety of different defensive and offensive functions. You can further customize your character by using performance enhancing chips that allow various buffs and passive abilities. Some chip combinations are borderline overpowered but there are four difficulty options that can be adjusted at any time should you fancy being brutally murdered in one blow. If that wasn't enough, Automata also contains parts that blends several action genres together. It is not uncommon for camera to move from classic third-person action to 2D platformer to top-down twin-stick shooter with bullet-hell elements sometimes even in a single combat scenario.Automata doesn't have classic New Game + mode. After concluding it (takes about 20-25 hours), you unlock effectively new chapters that flesh out this complex narrative even more. Including 5 main endings, there are 26 different ways to finish this story that vary depending on actions you take during your playthrough.Any gripes I'd have with Automata would be nitpicks. You could argue about how worldmap is designed, about washed-out color palette, about lack of tutorials for certain mechanics, but I feel that it was all done on purpose. It is rare to play a game with ambitious storytelling, polished combat system, replayability, incredible soundtrack, chunky jRPG elements and open world gameplay that doesn't suck.I hope to see another Platinum/Yoko Taro collaboration. Highly recommended.
