2017 Early Access Review General words:I have played a lot of early access games. After about 130 hours of gameplay I definately recommend this one! Its far beyond the average early access game's quality. It already feels complete in its current state, I did not encounter a single bug so far, it has already a lot of content and there is even a lot more to come.Your first mintes/hours in the game:You will need a couple of games before you can establish a stable, self maintaining colony, because every time you think you're safe something (thus far) unexpected happens. Maintaining power? Your oxygen gets low. Oxygen is ok? You're running out of food. There's always something new. And that's the main motivation of this game: Solving all of the problems which come up in a sufficient way and then, eventually, improve it.Every other colony you start is a bit more well planned from the start, but as soon as you keep satisfying your duplicants' basic needs, the struggle continues. You're now growing enough food and producing oxygen by electrolyzers out of water instead of using algae? Cool. But after several hunded cycles of your machinery running and your colony already reaching an average temperature of 48°C, how the get rid of all the excess emitted heat?After many more hours (still fun):The game reproduces the laws of physics in a very good fashion. While not being too strict and complicated, it lets you experiment with temperatures and aggregate states quite intuitively. My latest achievement was to "purify" polluted oxygen by building a machine thats cooling the polluted oxygen below its boiling point (approx. -183°C), thus liquifying it and then slowly raising the temperature again so that it "boils" into pure, clean oxygen. Getting this to work took me about 4 -6 hours of planning and testing and that's about a hunded times more complicated than just building an "air deodorizer", which is an included simple building that does the same thing. But the satisfaction of seeing your idea working is priceless. ;)10/10- today there will be a new content patch by the way!PS:I dont understand people having 200+ hours complaining about games in general. I mean, 200 hours of fun divided by 22 EUR (for this particular game) is roughly 10 ct per hour of gameplay. Watching a light bulb glow is almost as expensive...

2018 --The Good-- Combat is fun and engaging! Air and ground forces are unique and interesting. When battles go well (Balanced teams) The game is very exciting and rewarding! There are game modes for everyone. The game is split up in Arcade Battles (For new players) Realistic Battles (For veteran players and people looking for more authentic vehicle characteristics) And Simulator Battles (For experianced players looking for a challange)--The bad-- The grind for better machinery gets old pretty quick. Arcade battle hold the majority of the player base, causing the game to feel a little empty at higher skill game modes. If a team is loosing in a realistic air battle, but has slightly more ground units alive on the map, That player just flees from battle by flying off to the very far edge of the map where no one can find them OR if they have a fast plane they just outrun all the other players and climb away from battle, resulting in a 30 minute long game of hide and seek where no one wins just because the losing player was salty about losing. This issue doesn't happen all the time but it happens WAY too often.--The Ugly-- Battles can be short and unfufilling. Some end in just 5 to 10 minutes. Spawn camping is often a problem in battles that allow respawning. Bombers are almost useless in realistic air battle unless you cheese the enemy team with a bunch of bombers, ending the match early, robbing players on both teams of gameplay, and leaving a lot of players upset. Realistic battles, Arcade battles, Single missions, Dynamic campagins, and Simulator battles all have not been changed or really updated in many years plaguing battles with balance/gameplay issues that have never been resolved and likley never will be. Some players (Myself included) are concerned that Gaijin cares far more about making money than making a beter game. Every major patch just adds new content instead of fixing outdated game modes. Map rotation sometimes doesn't seem to exist. Forcing you to play on the same map 10 or more times in a row.--Final thoughts-- Honestly... Warthunder holds a very close place in my heart... but I can't reccomend it. It has too many small issues that, while not enought to keep new players from trying out the game, have many older players leave the game in disgust... Gaijin keeps adding content to keep players interested which on its own isnt a bad thing, but needs iron out the rinkles that have been in the game for many years now. Eventually Warthunder becomes exausting...If you haven't played but really want to, dont spend a single dollar on this game until you have played for at least 200 to 300 hours. Then see how you feel. I want to love Warthunder, but it still needs work it might never recieve. --TLDR-- Don't play until the game gets fixed, Its a not a bad game but has had issues for many years that need to be fixed.

2018 In the landscape of gaming, where publishers attempt to make the next Minecraft, Terraria rises to the challenge and makes its own name.However, inspiration does not mean copying, and to this end, the very core of the gameplay changes with the 2-D Perspective. While Minecraft tends towards a more casual playstyle, focusing on the creative aspect with the palette of materials you are given access to, Terraria is more heavily combat oriented and suitibly more challenging as a whole. While fast paced action may seem to indicate a controller preference, which is still quite effective and satisfying, keyboard and mouse are the way to go here due to the slew of combat options made available.The game emulates the 16-Bit style with sprite work that reminded me of the sprites in The Legend of Zelda: A Link to the Past. This carries through to the enemy design and environments you go through, which are admittedly par for the course until roughly the half way point, after which it explodes with vibrance.Regarding the approach to the storytelling, Terraria is largely open-ended, which makes sense considering the world, much like that of Minecraft, is randomly generated. While you can learn a bit from NPCs, this lore seems largely superficial. Regardless, the banter between NPCs is still an amusing sight and gives the world you explore just that much more character.The sound design is a bit of a mixed bag for me. The ambient noise and sound effects are well implemented and the soundtrack is varied and fun. My issue is that certain themes become grating. The overworld theme is nice on its own, but hearing it constantly loop kills the mood a bit. Luckily, the music is adaptive and changes to match the biome you are in, helping break up the audio monotony.In short, Terraria has something that a lot of other games lack, that being charm. It's a labour of love and it clearly shows, considering the witty writing, heartfelt references to a plethora of media franchises, and the fact that it's a game that plays well and is inherently fun. It plays well, and more importantly, it means well.

review: 2021 Early Access Review My friend and I bought Raft after she watched someone play it on stream and it is safe to say me and her are enjoying every single second of it. We both bought it last night and we ended up playing for 7 hours straight. I am yet to play alone but I think this is one of those games where you get the most out of it with a party of 2 or 3 people, lest it get mundane. It is surprising how fun it can be to be on a raft in the middle of nowhere jumping from island to island gathering resources for your raft that is slowly but surely starting to resemble a viable home, diving into the beautiful blue ocean and seeing the corals, resources, fishes and animals like dolphins. The game ran really well and I am yet to encounter any sort of glitch, bug or performance issues. My favourite thing about this game must be the research table and how you can learn all these "wacky" inventions to help improve your life on the raft - this can be addicting. The only annoying thing I found about Raft are the damn sharks... Whilst I do enjoy the danger of the shark roaming around the raft and having to be extremely cautious when you jump off or dive in the ocean, I hate the fact that it comes and bites you within seconds most times after jumping off into the sea. The shark starts to get really annoying after a while - and yes, I do know you can build shark bait, etc, but I just found this annoying. Other than that, this game is genuinely a diamond amongst rocks. I only paid about £15/$15 for this game, which is a bargain. Especially considering the game is still receiving updates and literally just got one last week that changed decorations, etc. TL;DR: Fun. Adventurous. Crafting is great. Exploration is amazing. Enhanced with friends. Worth the money without a doubt. Punishing survival game on the hardest difficulty.

2023 I just finished the game today. I am a completionist and try to do everything possible when I play... and it took me almost 115 hours to complete. Not sure if that includes the time I spent in the beta, which was around 20 hours. I read probably 8 books from The Horus Heresy to get a better understanding of the Warhammer 40k universe... and man, this game did a great job capturing it. I played as a "paladin" sanctioned psyker, who largely followed the dictates of the Imperium, and was not afraid to root out heresy if it seemed legitimate or could lead to legitimate heresy, but tried to balance that by making life as secure and pleasant as possible so that people would love the Imperium and be loyal to it out of genuine allegiance. I feel the game did a great job of showcasing the universe and all the various factions and races in it, though it was focused primarily on humans and the Aeldari and Drukhari (and of course, the agents of Chaos). No orcs. I loved the lore stuff and the various skills checks which really require a player to think carefully about the composition of their party, what skills their party members have, etc. Unlike Owlcat's previous 2 Pathfinder games, this one didn't have any atrocious mini-games. I personally enjoyed the ship combat... besides one ship battle at the end of the game... which I sent feedback to Owlcat about, because I believe it needs to be changed (I played the entire game with no advantages or disadvantages to the enemies or myself, just following the ruleset and everyone dealing the correct amount of damage).The writing is quite good, I wish there was more banter between the party members and they had more fleshed out stories and involvement with the main quest and character. That being said, all of them were interesting and good representations of different groups in the 40k universe and served as methods to learn more about them without it just being numbing exposition. And, unlike the Pathfinder games, I didn't dislike any of the characters. All of them have their understandable motivations and are exemplary in different ways.I highly recommend this game. I am an RPG purist and besides a handful of TRPGs, that is basically all I play. Don't expect Cyberpunk 2077 or Baldur's Gate 3 out of this. Owlcat is not nearly as large of a studio as CD Projekt Red or Larian (now). Do expect a great game that explores an interesting universe and gives you lots of different ways to play it and beat it. Do expect challenging combat where you are going to have to make sure you have the right equipment on your characters, that you have thought carefully about synergies they can create, and about weaknesses your party might have. Some advice? CASSIA. You will need her. If you are smart, you can use her a ton to counteract all the damage to the warp you do with psyker characters. When I fought the final battle, I had 2 sanctioned psykers and 1 unsactioned psyker just going wild... and then Cassia would get everything under control so we weren't inviting all the forces of chaos in. Besides that, you are going to have to think very carefully about whether you want high dodge or high armor + deflection. You can't really have both. If you have enough agility, you might be better off just sticking to light and medium armor. If you don't have high agility, you will 100% need to get heavy armor with as much deflection as possible... but I don't recommend this route. If you have low agility, you don't get to use that character until late in the combat round. By that point, they might have already been hit a ton or the target you could best use them against might be out of their reach. Having decently high agility is good for every character, because then you end up with your party making the first moves in the combat turn, hitting the bad buys before they can hit you. All of my characters had decently high agility or REALLY high agility, and it let me largely dictate how the fight started off and helped end them a lot faster. BIOMANCY. If you can repair the warp damage, biomancy gives you free healing. Between my 2 sanctioned psykers (both basically tanks) and Cassia, I was able to regularly keep everyone strong and healthy and even have bonus hit points... so if they DID get hit, they ultimately didn't lose many HP at at ("wounds").

Worst parts of DI have been rotten out, so you now have actually playable game.Gameplay is heavily parkour-styled, so your character, Kyle Crane, will climb and jump around the city of Harran in search of cure research for the zombie virus. Harran is made up from two large areas Slums and Old Town, which are enough distinct to spark your EXPLORE!-fire again when you change the map. The game world is quite amazing and graphics developers have been doing marvelous job to add lots of details all around. Exploring the world will give you XP, but when you hit the level cap the rewards from exploring won't account much unless you play for Steam achievements. On the other hand, as there aren't any practical reason to explore more, two large map areas will suffice.Movement is fluid and usually you get intended action (grab a ledge, jump off from the wall) so you actually feel like you're doing parkour moves. If surface looks like it could be grapped or climbed, that's usually the case. Movement skill level also adds to the feeling that Kyle Crane physically learns more as he goes on. Having seen some games which kind of sucked (Mirror World *cough* *cough*) and some games where all surfaces are fair game (Ninja Gaiden), doing parkour in DL is simply fun. Of course some movement restrictions are in place as game world is finite, there are surfaces you can't grab and gameplay area is confined by magical invisible walls. Later on you get grappling hook, while it speeds up gameplay considerably, you lose most of the illusion of being parkour runner.Combat system is fairly simple. Neverthless it's entertaining enough for few hours just to bash, slash, maul and maim zombies with whatever weapon you get on your hands. Zombies react to physics, so they can tackled, toppled over fences or forced to climb on high places to even reach you (and then they get kick in the face). You're able to target generic body area so usually button mashing is a great combat tactic. There is unfortunate auto-targetting when doing some combat moves but I guess it's price to pay for playing console game. Story is kind of mixed bag, as side quests have more story than the main quest. Most of NPCs have at least somewhat interesting dialogue and voice acting & animations are ok, some overacting, but also some really excellent performances. Most of the default story line aspects living in the city full of undead are handled in way or another through side quests or collectibles. Unfortunately main quest includes some really dumb forced story events, bad boss seems to have constant grip from Crane's balls whatever Kyle tries to do. Kyle Crane voice acting shows him as quite strong-willed character, he's not on par with JC Denton but delivers his punch lines with real punch well enough (except every time when Kyle meets evil boss he puts whimp clothes on so he can receive good spanking). I have kind of insight after my playthrough that Techland can't make a game without horrible main story twists. Dead Island was such a dog puke, DL is bit better though as side quests will give some credibility for the story writer.Of course the zombie game aren't zombie game at all if there aren't any gibs! In DL zombie gibs are also finite, for example you can't cut only fingers off, then palm off, wrist off and so on, you only chop off whole hand from elbow. Gore effects are fairly well done and stay within reasonable limits so you can enjoy the effects and do not get WTFs every time. Gore with taste, I say! Also splatter effects on walls seems to correspond with weapon you're using.User Interface is designed for consoles, game has "hold this key and move mouse"-style weapon/item menu. This might work if you have gamepad or such, but I played this with keyboard and mouse. You can rebind the keys, but you need to limit yourself to only some items or juggle through awkward inventory if you want to use more items (especially elixirs). Also keybinding on Linux version is horrible and mouse recognizes only 3 buttons.Of course review would not be completed without nitpicking about some things. Developers are marketing this game for Linux/SteamOS and then when you buy it you will experience about half of FPS of what it should achieve. DON'T BUY THIS GAME FOR LINUX/STEAMOS until developers fix this! Patch 1.5 recently came out and fixed some issues. I tested Linux version with same hardware and fact is game does not perform well enough to be playable.Also final battle with the boss is just one facepalm moment you can't forget. So, you're ready with best weapons with best upgrades, holding boss' own gun to give it back one bullet at time and lots of invulnerability elixirs to gulp. You climb on the final ledge ready to pump this guy full of lead and then chop him to tiny grilled evil zombi-snack bits with your Fiery Sword of Death. Well, that's how it should go? Instead you're treated with Quick-Time Event (QTE) where one-handed man beats your zombi-killing hero to ground only using one hand and whole battle... no, not battle... watching interactive movie... consist of pressing seven buttons in certain order. WTF? In fact, here's pro-tip for you: in this game you can discard your weapons before playing any main quests against boss as you can't never use them.Conclusion: despite some shortcomings this is quite fun game. Main story sucks but as one NPC said to Crane, blockbuster movies are all about happy endings and badly told stories. Here's story for 70€ (incl. Season Pass). As long you remember to turn your brain off for the main story quest, you should have fun. Worst letdowns are technical problems with SteamOS/Linux version (hopefully to be patched) and main story had lots of brain-dead parts in it.On the bright side, gameplay is fun and entertaining for one playthrough. Multiplayer might add some more hours, but I'll suggest you first try the game on single player or with newbie friends as best parts of the game experience is at the beginning of the game. I would say with more experienced story designer, ironing out all technical problems before release and adapting interface more for keyboard/mouse this could have been excellent gem. Anyways, it's worth of try if you buy game for Windows. I can't recommend buying this game for Linux/SteamOS and paying full price.

review: Amazing to play, a delight to watch

At its core SM2 is a polished, focused third person shooter that offers a refreshingly complete package compared to its contemporaries. Most of SM2s core elements are good *enough* on their own but get tied together with genuinely top class presentation that elevates everything on offer here. The core gameplay loop manages to be stripped down whilst staying just deep enough to be consistently entertaining. The combat model is built around snappy gunplay that flows in and out of hack and slash melee action that does manage to incorporate a decent parry and combo system, although do not go in expecting the depth of anything like a real character action game - what is here is far more comparable to something like the recent God of War games and even then not as complex. What matters most is that it doesn't need to be especially complex in order to stay consistently entertaining. The fights feel great, enemy variety is solid and mostly well designed and the game strings you from one fantastic set piece to the next at a brisk pace. In terms of difficulty this is a fairly challenging shooter at the higher difficulty levels although the single biggest influence on challenge is whether you are playing co-op or not as the bots here are not the best.In terms of overall variety you're getting three distinct game-modes here: A narrative campaign with optional 3 player co-op that will run you anywhere from 5-10 hours, a mission based PVE operations mode that again features 3 player co-op with a customisable class based progression system (should be noted that this is where the legs of the game seem to be and Focus have already committed to expanding it, this is also where the helldivers comparisons you have undoubtedly heard are relevant), and a pvp multiplayer mode that shares some progression elements and customisation with the operations mode. The campaign is a direct sequel to the original game narratively although Focus have gone to significant lengths to make this work as a standalone story not only for those who haven't played the original but also for those who have limited/no knowledge of the 40k universe. It does a pretty decent job of telling a pretty standard albeit compelling war story but for fans of 40k there are some pretty decent plot hooks here and cool wider implications. In terms of mission structure and the overall campaign experience, I enjoyed the back half of the campaign a lot more than the front, the early missions have a lot of "defend this point" objective set pieces that are uninspired at best and tedious at worst, thankfully the game moves away from this and focuses on letting you explore the combat sandbox through well structured arenas and big set piece moments. The last third of the game is thrilling and it keeps building managing to end really strong which is ultimately what you want from a fairly short campaign. Visual presentation and audio design are excellent, giving pretty much the best rendition of the 40k universe that has ever been put to a screen. Weaponry feels excellent with great feedback and weighty impacts that are reflected by responsive enemy modelling and animation. The overall atmosphere is peak large scale 40k, it doesn't quite match something like Darktide in terms of sheer oppressiveness and that game and Mechanicus both feature better OSTs but SM2 is no slouch in either regard. To briefly the discuss the other modes on offer: I think the PVE operations have a lot of potential, the game uses an AI director similar to Left 4 Dead and other horde based games and on higher difficulties you do have those "oh ♥♥♥♥" moments that have made the genre so popular. The missions also benefit massively from not being procedurally generated, something that was a major contributor to how stale Helldivers 2 became after a dozen or so hours. Everything here is handcrafted and whilst the drawback is that the content on offer is a bit limited and will take time to produce, it is all high quality with unique mission framing and compelling objectives. Progression and customisation are great as they kind of need to be for a game based on a miniature wargame famous for its sheer diversity of design. I have some nitpicks that will matter to passionate 40k fans: theres a lack of chapter specific visual flair e.g no thematic armour pieces like cloaks and tassels for white scars or scales for salamanders etc ; also everything here is very much a product of the uniformity of GWs Primaris designs and if you hate them, you are not gonna get much reprieve here, I would like to see some of the classic SM iconography e.g Corvus helmets brought in. Also Heretic Marines are only playable in the PVP and they have no armour customisation outside of basic paint jobs and decals, this may change down the line but for now its worth mentioning. On the topic of the PVP the original game was famed for managing to keep a small but dedicated community of players on board for over a decade after its release (shout out CM Valrak) and I think whats on offer here has similar potential but as it currently stands it feels unfinished. There is a real shortage of both game modes, weapon variety and especially maps. The maps here are way too small, spawns are bad and I would really like to see some different types of maps as most of them feel fairly similar. I like the foundations Focus have laid down but like the PVE this is a case of "good start but show me more". TLDR: SM2 is a fantastic package that stands out amongst a landscape of half-finished content poor AAA releases. The presentation and core gameplay loop are excellent, the Campaign is a blast that gets better as it goes, PVE has tonnes of potential (especially if you are fed up with HD2) and the PVP is fun but needs some work. Worth the money.

review: 2023 Tl;dr:One of the best games I have ever played! An excellent and beautiful 4x game (think civ, endless legend etc.) that motivates the player to always finish each run. If you loved the idea of 4x, but always struggled to get into them, then this is a must try. Held back, only slightly, by poor optimization and a "lower quality feel" then it really should have.Pros: - Customize the worlds - Beautiful, both in style and graphics - Customize the races - Clever story missions - Customize your leaders - Intriguing rouge-light and tech mechanics. - CUSTOMIZATION!!!!Cons: - Poor optimization - Feels a bit low quality at timesTHE GOOD:One of the biggest problem I have with games like these is finding the motivation to actually finish a scenario ones the writing is on the wall. The moment I know that I will win, it just becomes a slug, a drawn out tedious crawl to the finish line. I always thought that a clever way to solve this is by rewarding the player for finishing each run, sort of like in a rouge-light. This is the first game that I have come across that does exactly that. Across the multiple games you will play in this you will gradually unlock cosmetics, (and some actual game changing stuff) and form you own "pantheon" of heroes and rulers. This system, I think, could probably do with being expanded further, but for now is enough to help the player to keep coming back for more.I also LOVE how, in a game allllll about customizing your own fantasy race and ruler, the "story missions" do not restrict you to a pre-selected race and ruler. You get to choose who to play as on each mission, and the story does a decent job of adjusting to your choice. Some missions you are obviously "suppose" to play as a good guy, some as a baddie; but this is usually pretty clear and, at any rate, pure recommendation.Assuming that you have at least some knowledge of games like civ, endless legend etc, you should, by now, have a pretty good idea about what this game is all about. And, hopefully, if it's one for your library. Otherwise the questions you need to ask yourself are rather simple:Do you like tactical strategy games?Do you struggle to find motivation to finish 4x game scenarios?Do you think the pics and videos of this game are aesthetically pleasing?Do you love customization options in-game?Have you always wanted to create your own fantasy faction/race and ruler?The more your answers to these questions is in the affirmative, the more I would recommend this absolute brilliant game. The more your answers are in the negative... well if you are answering these in the negative, why are you even reading reviews about this game?THE BAD:So now that I have talked all about what makes this game so dam good, let's consider the negatives. I have played some of AoW in the past. Particularly AoW 3. I always struggled hard with that game for a number of reasons, but the main one was the lack of polish. The game looked durpy as all hell at times, some of the races where just uncanny... actually perhaps most where. And that might have presented it's own charm for some, but certainly not for me. The game felt cheep like that of a (good) toy version of a real gun. It wasn't exactly bad, just felt "plasticy" compared to a more high quality product (more on this latter). To make things worse the game struggled with finding it's own aesthetic. Because they essentially tried to put everything in a game, it ended up looking disjointed and mismatched. With AoW 4 they have solved these issues... for the most parts. I desperately wish that I could say that these issues where all fixed, but then I'd be lying. On the positive the game no longer looks durpy (actually the occasional cat-person still do, but that's acceptable); and, some how, they have managed to create a uniformed aesthetic. Everything looks like it belongs to the same world, which is something that still astonishes me from time to time. However the game is not very well optimized. On my, admittedly not-so-good-pc, it runs pretty badly, especially during battles. To the point where I always auto-resolve any battle. Which is a bit unfortunate, though this does show that the game is fully playable and enjoyable even with only auto-resolve. Still the game relay should be running smoother. I can run Stellaris, Ck3 and God of war, without to much problem, this game looks good and is clearly rather intense on the processing power, but it should be able to run smoother then it does.And the one unfortunate thing it carried over from it's predecessor is the occasional low quality feel. This is something that is pretty hard to describe but let me try. After I hit the end turn button, yet before my next turn begins, I always "feel" as if I could accidentally break the game, or flat out make it crash, just by interacting with it to much. This hasn't actually happened to me so far (the game has only crashed ones in 50+ hours (for unknown reasons)), but the feeling is there and it is, in away "immersion breaking". And why does the ai turns feel soooooo slow, Warhammer total war handles hundreds of factions... this game has what, 8 at most?! It's like the game wants to play out each move one at the time. But then it doesn't bother centering the camera on the moves anyway, so why not just have it all happen simultaneously? These little things brings you out of the game, it reminds you that you are just playing a game, and that can be enough to make you consider doing other things. I've played games where you could even interact with elements of the game UI whilst having the options menu open, fortunately AoW 4 doesn't go that far. But it does allow you to select armies whilst you are waiting for your turn and even see how far they will be able to go; and, more then ones, I have been tricked to thinking that it is my turn again sens the game really doesn't do anything to distinguish between the ai:s turn and the player... apart from the "should-be-obvious-to-anyone-hourglass" that sits in the bottom right corner... yaaa... I don't know how I keep missing that... Still the point remains. The game deserves to feel more quality then it does. The game deves should be experienced enough that many of these tiny issues should have been ironed out before launch. But I suppose someone just didn't think spending the time and money on game-testing to get rid of these "minor inconveniences" would be worth it. Whilst these are indeed minor, I think that this trend of cutting corners in the gaming industry is becoming ever more damming for the media as a whole. Game deves and producers should know better. And gamers should expect, if necessary demand, better!So that's my review for the best game I have played in years! A brilliant masterpiece, held back, only slightly, by a lack of polish.

2018 This game is a MASTERPIECE in my eyes! This is the first time in my life that I've seen a mix of the "3D Platformer" genre with the "Horror" genre implemented so well on a game and I love it! The game's atmosphere is eerie, dark and very creepy because of the excellent background sounds and environments. The game's enemies are scary, hideous and very dangerous as well, so approaching them is definitely not the best option (unless you want to die for a weird reason). They manage to keep you on the edge of your seat (especially in the DLC chapters and during quite a lot of parts of the main game) whenever they start appearing at random spots and rush to you in an attempt to get you, creating a lot of suspenseful moments which make you unsure of whether you can avoid these monstrosities or not in the end. The boss battles (especially the last one) are AMAZING and escaping from the grasp of your enemies can require huge amounts of attention and a lot of patience because one wrong move is enough to alert the enemy and reveal your location! I really liked how the boss battles were executed as well, since half of them required you to do a very clear objective to beat the enemy (which were hair-raising and full of suspense) and the other half required hiding, sneaking around an area or even running for your life in nerve-racking chase sequences. All in all, this game despite its lack of a clear narrative and information on what those monstrosities actually are or where the heck you're actually located to and how did you get there in the first place for example, it's definitely a game worth your time if you are a fan of 3D Platformers with puzzle elements in an absolutely astonishing horror setting or even if you love horror games with puzzle elements but don't necessarily fancy 3D platformers as well! 10/10P.S I recommend getting the game along with its DLC in order to blast through the whole thing all at once since the main game and the DLC chapters share a very interesting connection that definitely "wowed" me the first time that I saw it. Also, some of the questions about the game's lore were answered through 3 comic issues on the game which can be found online by any internet user but I've heard that they left some stuff unanswered on purpose for the sake of the sequel which is going to take place in the same universe as the first game and its DLC but at a different location than "The Maw" from what I recall).

2023 Early Access Review More than 100+ hours on mobile. Long-time Hearthstone competitive player. Lots of single-player card builders. Those are my only credentials here, so take my opinion with a grain of salt.Pros:-Fast games that always feel different-Unique card mechanics that are fun-Less "unfair" feelings because of the cube system (essentially like playing poker, with calls, folds, all-in style wagering) - got a crap hand and your opponent snaps? Leave and queue for a new match with a minimal loss of cubes. Think there's no way you can lose? Snap and force your opponent to call, raise, or fold.-Great artwork and lots of variety with card variants.-Great, canon-based flavor for most cards if you're a Marvel fan.-Reasonable progression from Pool 1 to the beginning of Pool 3.-Monthly updates, sometimes more than once a month. Balance patches are reasonably quick, but still thought out to make sure the meta remains healthy.-Separate matchmaking for Pool 1 and Pool 2 (to keep things fair for those beginning to build their collections)For experienced card games players: -Mostly every archetype feels viable. Control, Combo, Discard, Zoo/Tempo, Miracle, Destroy (Deathrattle), Disruption, and plenty of unique Snap decks can all be used to successfully climb the ranked ladder and there's not a rock, paper, scissors meta like other games.-No true Exodia decks. The closest things to Exodia are easily countered with multiple tech card options.-Tech cards aren't hate cards. Tech cards have tons of utility instead of being a one-note counter to very specific cards and most have fair stats. Neutral (to me): There's plenty of RNG in this game. If you hate RNG, this isn't the game for you. It's not as bad as Hearthstone's RNG imo, but it can absolutely be match-altering, too.Cons:-Progression slows down tremendously once you reach Pool 3 and is inconsistent. When you get a precious card unlock, it may be a meta-relevant card or it may be a card that doesn't see play. That would feel bad on its own, but unfortunately the same packs that *may* be a new card can also include avatars, titles, or card variants that don't help your collection whatsoever.-Matchmaking in Pool 3+ feels like a punishment. Most of the players you'll come across have one or two of the most powerful cards in the game (even more if you're unlucky), that you haven't even had the opportunity to unlock. This makes it feel like you are at a massive disadvantage (because you are).-Players that reach the top rank (Infinite) can reset their MMR by tanking matches and then will match with people who are in the lowest ranks with cards that can't come close to competing. Those Infinite players still get their top-tier rewards at the end of each season and there's zero incentive (or disincentive) for them to play competitively once they've reached the top rank. Basically, imagine an Apex Predator/Champion rank being able to queue with Bronze/Silver without losing their rank status.-Questionable monetization, arguably predatory. New cards are constantly being released that are gated by very low chance lootboxes or paywalls. This would be fine if the cards were released in fair states, but most new cards are released severely unbalanced, giving the lucky few who unlock them (or the whales who buy) an unfair advantage over 90% of the playerbase. Season passes can only be purchased with real money and can't be earned - again that's fine if the cards locked behind the season pass aren't meta-defining, but most of the time they are, pressuring players to pay up if they want to keep up with the meta.-*This is speculative and not proven* Matchmaking feels similar to a modern FPS style matchmaking algorithm. It seems designed to see-saw you and frustrate you. If you get an easy match, it's often a bot which comes after a few consecutive losses - basically the algorithm gifting you a win to keep you on the game. Then it's back to getting queued into other players that are often running a counter to your deck or one that is a 50/50 matchup. Competition is great, but it feels incredibly artificial here.TL;DR: I don't think the pros outweigh the cons here. This is a great game to endlessly sink unconscious hours into, like Hearthstone, COD, Madden, etc., but it's addictive and predatory in its design. It has its hooks in me, but I wouldn't recommend it to anyone I care about or anyone in general.

But here in this review, I’ll talk about my personal view about the main aspects of the game, after experiencing it for a long time and getting really involved in it, a game that made me meet a lot of people and even join Teams. The Positives: Mechanics – This game have the Cleanest and most Satisfactory mechanics, from Movement to Shooting. It's fairly easy to know how it works, but is very hard to master and get used to it, that’s what makes it a truly competitive game, having so many levels of complexity. Source It’s been out there for ages and is not even close to be outdated. Map Design – Overwhelming and Memorable designs they are unique, interesting to learn and different to get better on each one of them, some maps are improvements of older CS’s and still have a lot relevance Skill Game – It’s a game that the more you practice, the more you want to get better, even after 4.000 hours I can still improve my impact on the game, and when I reach that performance it’s an amazing feeling. Competitive Scenario – Probably the largest e-sports out there, with the most grown scenario… Cheer with friends and go out on events or tournaments all over the world it’s a really positive thing to the health and long life of the game, it’s also supported by Valve itself. Friendly for Casual players – There a lot of different modes and workshop maps that can make the game entertaining for casual people, the community provides a lot for the game with Workshop content! I think they could improve the experience for new players, there is no tutorial to help people that need it. Skins – Best designed skins for a game, most of FPS cannot give such quality for single skin like CS:GO can, it’s really enjoyable to have them in your inventory, making yourself a collection, and selling or trading them anytime you want. The Negatives: Variety – It’s not very common of Valve to release new Stuff, it’s been a while since the last operation and a new game mode release. They are changing the meta, but it takes a long time for these updates also… So, the game can become repetitive for a lot of people. 128 Tick-rate – I think everyone agrees that Matchmaking should be played in 128 tick-servers, that makes the game more fluid and smooth, but it’s not been announced or planned to be a feature anytime soon, so if you want to experience that, you have a lot of 3rd parties platforms that provides that with a lot of other interesting features! Toxicity – People in Lobby sometimes can be really toxic to one another; we can sadly see it around from time to time. Cheating – I think that’s my main problem with CS:GO at the moment, even though I don’t think it got any worse with it being Free… The real problem is Premium cheaters, the ones that use high profile cheats and trusted accounts to mess with MM experience, they know how to use it properly and probably will not get banned. So, if you start to think a lot about it, you’ll probably go crazy and lose faith on the system they provide against Cheating. Valve has been updating their Anti-Cheat with different methods, but it's a long process.I’ve been really enjoying this game for a long time, I love to dedicate myself and get better, training my aim, movement and knowledge about the game. Its even more fun when played with friends, trying to make yourself a team to play in tournaments or grind on Matchmaking. It’s really hard not to recommend at this point, the game have a beautiful Legacy and is now Free-to-Play , definitely worth trying it out. But be careful, you might get addicted… Rate: 9.1/10.0

2017 Product received for free Wow, just wow. A friend bought me New Vegas during the 2016 Autumn Sale after I won a bet. I played the game for a few hours and then put it down because the beginning was boring, and the baron wastes of the Mojave didn't captivate me. But then, on one day, I played it again. I couldn't stop, I don't know what got into me but suddenly the game was an absolute masterpiece in my eye. Now that we are done with that little introduction, here is a pros and cons list, which will also compare the game to Fallout 3 and how it did almost everything better than it in every single way possible.Pros:Weapons are fixed! Gone is the "zoom in aiming" from Fallout 3. They actually added aiming down the sights, which vastly improves gunplay. Repairing is also much easier; a perk allowing you to repair weapons with other weapons of similiar type. Unlike Fallout 3 where if you had a really rare unique weapon that degraded and became useless, you would need another version of that exact same gun to repair it. Choices and Dialogue are excellent! In Fallout 3, you rarely would have a choice in dialogue to spare someone, basically making the game full of "choices" which are either blast an important character to bits or...well that's usually the only choice you get. In New Vegas however, you were brought with peaceful alternatives to situations. For example, if you go with the NCR, a late game quest is to either wipe out the great Khan leaders, or try and find a peaceful alternative to get them to fight with you. But the beautiful part is, the game doesn't explain how to get the peaceful alternative from the main quest. You actually get to have a real talk with one of the 3 leaders, and he will propose you this whole seperate quest on how you can overthrow the "king" of the Great Khans and get him to fight with you! These are just one of MANY quests in where this occurs. Dialogue is also MUCH improved from Fallout 3. In Fallout 3, speech checks were just a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ dice roll, forcing you to reload over and over to get what you want. And improving your speech doesn't guarentee you a success either, it just slightly improves the chances. However, in Fallout New Vegas, they make use of all sorts of different skills in dialogue to help give an edge. The checks aren't a dice roll anymore, your skill has to be high enough to pass. And while you could argue that it breaks immersion, and I can see that, the game doesn't punish you for failing a speech check, they are usually just to make a quest go by faster or get a better deal on your reward. And if you don't meet the speech check, you get a hilarious joke option just for fun!The Narrative is WAY better! In Fallout 3, your character grows up in Vault 101 and sets out to find his father who had escaped for a reason that I won't spoil (although its nothing crazy or amazing). Fallout 3's narrative suffers greatly from the fact that Bethesda had already set up a full backstory for your character really limited role-playing and how you want your character to act in the Capital Wasteland. Oh yea, and Fallout 3's ending sucks really bad too, so bad that the devs had to make a dlc to remove it...yea that speaks for itself. In New Vegas however, you begin as a Courier getting shot in the head, and thats all you get. The beauty of this is that it really allows you create a full backstory and get immersed in your character, with the only real hiccup being that they're a Courier, but that isn't or doesn't have to be their defining trait as a character. And the narrative to the game is masterful. You essentially get 3 paths to choose from, each with their own motives and politics (aside from the third option but it's actually up to you to make the politics and rules and such). For example, take Caesars Legion. They might just seem like a bunch of crazy slave owners who burn villages and enslave people, but if you sit down and talk with their leader, he gives a legitimate criticism of democracy and has reasons for his actions. Where as in Fallout 3, I didn't even know what the main villians goal or reasoning for his actions were. And in Fallout 3, the story evolves once, and it's fairly simple. But in New Vegas, you start out trying to find the man who shot you, and once you do, the whole story turns into a huge political battle over a huge fresh water source, which will determine the fate of what is quite possibly the last intact human city in the USA (in the Fallout universe). Instead of Fallout 3, for when you find your father, the plot just turns into getting a large water purifier to work that concludes in a HUGE ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ ENDING that doesn't solve anything. I won't spoil too much, but basically if you let the real main characters (everyone except you really) who have been working through the entire story to achieve this goal do the thing, you are a coward. But if you do it, then you are a hero, even though through dialogue your character rarely experiences an extreme passion for the project. In New Vegas, the story is satisfying and each ending makes perfect sense and wraps everything up nicely.Better Perks and Level Up Systems: I'm going to keep this short and straight to the point because this review is insanely long. Fallout 3 had some pretty lame perks, just raising one or two of your skills by 5 or something lame like that. But in New Vegas, all of those lame perks are GONE! And perks are seen as almost a golden opportunity that can completely change the game in some instances (such as the aforementioned perk called Jury Rigging, which totally changes how repairs work.Traits are back!: If you didn't know, traits were in the original two Fallout games that were optional, and you could select them upon making a character. And these traits are like perks except they have positive AND negative effects. These really turned the game around and made for fun and hilarious gameplay moments. Fallout 3 removed these because "traits are scary" or some crap like that. But New Vegas has them back and they are as good as ever!Quests are great: So this gonna be real short but Fallout 3 and New Vegas both have excellent quests. They are all self contained stories and usually are never some crap like "fetch me 20 eggs" or something like that.Cons:Open World seem Baron and Uninteresting at times: While patrolling the Mojave to get to your next destination, there isn't much to see but desert if you just go from quest marker to quest marker. But if you look around, there is plenty to do. And I'll give this to Fallout 3, it REALLY nails the atmosphere and the open world is huge and NOT baron, filled with things to do and find.And that is seriously the only con I can think of. I seriously think this is one of the best video games ever created. It combines the masterful dialogue and choices of Fallout 1 and 2, while keeping the scale, fun gameplay, and content that Fallout 3 had.

2016 I've played Total War games since the very first Shogun. I've seen the series expand into a wonderfully entertaining and casual wargaming series.However, the Total War games have also struggled to provide challenging AI opponents, have suffered from numerous bugs and issues that seem to persist and we all know how disastrous Rome 2 was on during launch.So, my expectations for Warhammer were low before launch, though streamers and lets-players did give me enough hope that I ended up trying out the game myself. Turns out, this is probably CA's most solid launch in years and the gameplay is actually incredibly fun.I wondered how CA would solve the problem of fractured Empire or the numerous dwarfen kingdoms, I expected total war and conquest but in Warhammer the diplomatic conquests and uniting kingdoms is actually a viable option! This actually makes so much more sense lore-wise and such and I love the fact that CA managed to pull off this one.The battles? I did not play Attila, so I don't know if this was already a thing in it, but I am in love with the fact that AI is aggressively trying to flank my armies on field all the time, they love hitting me in the back or going after artillery.The unit balance is better than in tabletop for obvious reasons, yet the units, especially elite ones, certainly stand out in their effectiveness.The rock-paper-scissor mechanics also work out and make sense due to the fantasy settingThe battles can get hectic because of the routing-regrouping mechanics, which makes running evenly matched battles a real challenge. It feels more challenging than other TW-games in years, even if it is a bit too chaotic to keep up with, mostly because I'm the type to zoom in and enjoy the on-going battle up close.Siege battles are still a bit bothersome, AI isn't the greatest in defence and it's all too easy to exploit the mechanics but defending sieges can be fun. AI has also managed to surprise me by sending out flying units while playing defense, to harass my siege-artillery.Heroes, lords and legendary lords also stand out and can really turn the tides. I love that magic was implemented, though it feels a bit lackluster most of the time. I can see the effectiveness in numbers, but I would have loved to see more longer-lasting spells and more spectacular effects go off on the field, If I enchant units with burning swords, I'd love to see their weapons really on fire!As for the performance. Well, I'm running a four year old computer that I've upgraded with GTX 970. The game runs solid for me on ultra settings, not big FPS dips even in multi-stack battles which I hadn't expected at all. All in all, the game is fairly solid package and I do recommend it for all Total War and Warhammer fans. I've enjoyed the game, despite my initial expectations. CA has given us a game that'll hopefully provide entertainment for a long, long time.

review: 2021 Possibly the best action adventure game i have ever played.Sekiro: Shadows Die Twice presents you with a gripping story, filled with mistery and intrigue, Being thrown into the fantasy world of Ashina, it is up to you to discover the occultish and supernatural traditions of the world. 2020 This is the most stunning piece of software I have ever seen! Nothing even comes close to comparing to this. I have removed XPlane11 from my drive and I will have no reason to go back.First let me tell you I'm running a 2080ti, 9700k processor, 32g of DDR4, Gsync monitor and MSFS2020 is installed on an SSD.This is a sim folks. If you came here because of the incredible graphics you saw in videos or screen shots but you are new to flight sims you are in for a shock. I have been flying flight sims since they first appeared on the market. All flight sims are VERY demanding on your hardware. They ALL push the boundaries of what current hardware can handle when they first release. Hardware eventually catches up. This sim has a 10 year plan. It will only get better.My jaw dropped when I first saw the visuals for real. I'm running the sim in 2k with most of the settings on Ultra and the few I have changed are on high. To be honest, I see very little difference between the two. The software automatically set my graphics all to Ultra but I have been tweaking as I go. While flying over San Fran I was averaging about 45 fps with my settings as I stated above. I had MSI Afterburner running on the screen and my graphics card rarely moved above 70% and my CPU was sitting around 60% on all cores.At first I had an issue with setting up my Virpil controls. The stick was acting insane when I made small movements which I'm seeing commonly complained about in the reviews. I realized that my inputs were incorrectly set to digital inputs instead of axis. As soon as I corrected this everything worked amazingly without even touching sensitivity settings. I'm using a Virpil stick and Throttle along with Thrustmaster's Pendular rudder system. Everything including my TrackIr is working with no issues.I did not have any issues with downloading the software other than I had to do a restart of steam to get my DLC to be downloaded. This was clearly stated on the forums yesterday morning for anyone who bothered to check.I have to stress to those who are thinking this is an arcade flying game like War Thunder or something you are going to be sorely disappointed. This is a SIM and it takes time to tweak and setup your settings and controls. Afterburner is showing that I'm using at least 9 gig of my Ram on my Video Card. I'm using roughly 12 gig of ram from my board at anytime. I have a 500 mbps download speed from my provider. If you think you are going to run the sim at higher settings, streaming real world visuals on a 4 yr old computer or worse with 8 gigs of ram on your board and little on your card.....I don't know what to say and I assume that is where many people are having issues. This is cutting edge software people. ****Edit*** After the 2nd patch the FPS has increased and the stutters I was previously having have disappeared. The game is very smooth for me now.When it comes to the flying experience it just beats everything else hands down. No more looking at ugly scenery that you have to spend hundreds of dollars to fix and takes up hundreds of gigs of space on your hard drive just for improved scenery in 1 state that still looks nothing like MSFS2020. No more roads running off willy- nilly into nowhere like they were placed by a dev on a meth trip. Everything looks real! Roads go where they are suppose to and trains don't just drop off the map. I easily found my home and I do not live in one of the more hand crafted areas. The sim can be setup to fly in a more arcade fashion for new simmers or it can be setup for the hardcore enthusiasts. The Air Traffic control is so much better out of the box then it's competition. I will update this review as time goes on but I can safely say that Microsoft knocked this out of the park. Are there issues which need to be fixed and tweaked? Of course. I see graphical blemishes here and there. I see a few boats sitting on a road now and then. There are some instrument bugs that need to be fixed and they have posted this in the forums. The streaming will need to be optimized for sure.This fact is though. You buy something like this for the long term enjoyment. There are thousands of hours of value to be enjoyed here. It should only get better and I can't wait to see the helicopters and other things Microsoft has planned.Outstanding is all I can say! If you have the proper hardware and you are a simulator fan, this is going to blow your socks off. Just remember, it's new and it has issues to sort out like all software that hits the market. Show some patience and enjoy the ride.

Firstly, the game "optimizes its files" (shader pre-compilation) each time I start it, which is a bit of a hassle. Other games do it once during the first boot. Additionally, there are some performance issues, with the game suffering from minor to moderate stutter on my RTX 4080 and Core i9-11900K setup. The stability isn't great either with FPS dropping all over the place, especially during cut-scene transitions.Unfortunately, the game's visual clarity is also disappointing, and I'm not talking about graphical fidelity or detail of the assets, characters, or anything like that but the game forcing a 50% render resolution at all times. This means that even though I'm running the game at 4K, the image quality was only 1080p, which was a letdown considering the size of my monitor, and there's no way around it, at the moment at least. The clarity isn't there and I'm not going to hinder my vision I already don't have with this game too. Furthermore, the game only supports AMD FSR2, which is not ideal as it tends to look terrible on anything lower than 4K on a bigger screen, with all sorts of glitches and upscale artifacts. This is particularly frustrating because AMD FSR2 was useless in all games I had tried it with on the PC.Finally, there is no way to play the game on native resolution, as it always forces the 50% render scale. Overall, while the game had its good points, the gameplay is much improved and got me hooked right away, these issues at launch made it a less-than-stellar experience on PC, therefore, I'm happily refunding my purchase. 2022 I'll start with the negatives - Like most Paradox games, There's a significant hurdle to actually learning the game, and part of that is because the games are quite ridiculously complex. When i first bought the game, i tried it - found it too difficult to know what i was doing and i just let it collect dust in my library for months. The full tutorial of the game doesn't actually go far enough to explain all the hidden mechanics, what to do and how to actually make something successful. How to build a planet, all the inner politics of a species and their traits, etc... is left for you to figure out on your own, and you won't necessarily have the time to devote to learning the game, and know what is successful. However, one of my friends said we should play it, and we played a game where he taught me the basics of the game, dealing with pop-ups as we play. Naturally you make an awful lot of mistakes, and like long RTS games, there's a snowball effect of how strong your empire is. If you fall behind- you are gone for good, there's no coming back, and i was miles behind others by mid game, (a small weak race) so we started again.The game that followed actually told was kind of an epic story told of our galaxy and how it was developing, and i'l loosely tell you the story of our galaxy. The game didn't feel competitive, except in the fact that you're both competing against the AI, and your own mistakes. It felts like playing an RPG-RTS, something very unusual as most feel competitive.We started out as the initial tech alliance. My friend was basically an alien empire of space fish that made friends with many species and conquered the xenophobic aliens. I had turned into technological focused tree empire, that was pointlessly occupied with ferrying a gas species across my vast empire. At the time, my species had a terrible secret that nobody knew about. We were purging all other alien species, from our planets. Turns out my friends empire was an ally with the biggest enemy of all. (Secretly i had probably killed billions of his migrating population across our borders)By mid game we had a strong federation of 3 empires. The tree murdering technological powerhouse. My friends diplomatic powerhouse and an AI Species known as "Big Reach", who just had lots of fleets. Between us we had 2 thirds of the galaxy and were looking to gain control over the final third. In that third was our counter federation and big players who were flitting between joining our federation or joining the counter federation, also some smaller empires, that were using high defensive space stations etc.... (Highest fleet strength is about 40k now, average being 10k, but a series of choke points make big fleets difficult to use as wars end up panning out like a big cat and mouse game. I was having some issues with my economy and with some neighbours, and this is probably due to my secret race purges (i had issues with the space UN too), but i had the fleet power to prevent any unwanted wars.Suddenly a late game Crisis, an alien species more powerful than both of us combined spawns in the game hell bent on destroying EVERYTHING. It just *deletes* Big Reach. RIP Reach, he has like 2 planets on the borders of my friends empire now. My friends fleets aren't strong enough to deal with most of the enemy fleets, whilst I've got a lot of high level technologies, and possibly the technology to counter I don't have the economy or the amount of fleets. At this time I'm in the process of developing my first carrier strike fleet. (worth about 60k in fighting power)The unbidden as the crisis is known, (biggest fleet was 170k, but they have lots of 60-90k fleets), end up taking about a third of the game, and it looks like it's going to be a difficult battle to survive the galaxy. The other alien species are all struggling to win fights against them, The unbidden have reached my friends and my empire in what i would consider safe territory through a black hole. The attack force was just a recon force and we were able to push them out after some combined fleet action. My strike fleet, proving semi- effective. My friend has now taken his fleets, and after i reinforced our federation fleet with new technologies, that too to defend his borders with the unbidden knocking on the gates, with 3 60-90k fleets.Meanwhile, I'm looking at a developing crisis, as the bottom 3rd of the galaxy is turning unbidden and multiple fronts are soon to open up on my boarders with large fleet battles. I realise I need to increase the ability of my fleet to move around the big empire and develop defences long enough to delay the enemy advance in time for me to destroy his fleets, and then be able to counter attack successfully. Part of my empire is an issue, as it had taken it from the AI recently. There's a significant lack of infrastructure and defensive fleets, area has a lot of pirates and is more or less the wild west of my empire.It's turned into a very interesting game, as our snowball effect of wining the galaxy has been completely side-stepped by this new species. It'll be interesting to know if our empires are strong enough to defend from this catastrophe. One thing is for sure, we're in for a long war, and it's impossible to say if we will survive. Overall the game would get a recommend, as it can lead to the story telling of your own species, and it's quite polished, there's few other games like that, especially in RTS, I find them all feeling very competitive, whereas this feels more of an RPG. The downside is the mechanics aren't explained to you and its quite difficult to know what will be successful, as the mechanics are often complex and unexplained. Here is an example complexity of the game when it comes to military fleet design. Start with building a ship design:1. 3 categories of weapons - Missiles, Kinetic (bullets) , energy (lasers). (hidden stats are DPS and actual damage and range/ with 6 different technology upgrades). 2. 3 categories of defence - hull (hp), Armour (anti-kinetic), Energy (anti lasers) (6 technological upgrades).3. Tracking (aim),4. Evasiveness (combat speed/ determined by size and assisted by thrusters (also different sized weapons fit onto different ships altering range, rate of fire and damage). 6. drone abilities/ carriers/ hangars (Strike Craft). 7. Point Defence (flak guns or missile interceptors). 8. Overall Fleet Speed / Detection range.9. Utilities10. Combat designated AI (Does the ship think itself as an artillery role, or an interceptor role(changes behaviour and how it prioritises enemy ships).11. Special weapons.All of this interlinks in the hidden statsSo that's a lot of stats, you're starting fleet should aim to be like 20 ships, all small aircraft (1 size), Approx 1-2kk in strength). Will you use a combination or a hard focused fleet is questions you will have to ask.An all missile fleet with defensive armour could be highly effective against the right enemy, however a laser fleet that engages ships at mid range and relies on dps and evasiveness with Integrated specialised ships focused on intercepting missiles would be a hard counter. When it get to bigger fleets there's probably about 7 different sized ships, all completely interchangeable. It becomes very hard to know what is the optimum fleet design with how many point defence systems, how many missiles, how much armour, what combination of small to large ships, etc... So it's very complex.If you decide that example of complexity is too much for you then fair enough. Planet management etc, is similar- there is an automatic feature for the game to run your planets, and auto-build your ships, but I don't think the ai builds them competitively for you to make your own decision on how your empire plays and if its useful. If you choose to get it, and have the time to devote to learning the game, Good Luck! Look forward to hearing your own stories of your galactic empire.

2020 Early Access Review I think 100 recorded Steam hours plus countless more on Desura lends me the ability to give at least a somewhat knowledgeable review.The game is...okay. It's marginally passable as a zombie survival sandbox. It's nice that there no cure or chance of rescue. It makes for a more tightly focused game, removing possible options and letting it concentrate on other areas. Or in theory, it should. But this is not what's happened.I've been following this game for over 7 years. Since the beginning when it was just Kate and Baldspot and the town was much, much smaller, a couple dozen houses. And the zombies all had the same sprite. Even years later when I briefly returned because a friend wanted to try multiplayer. The starting town was much bigger but the game hadn't evolved much. It was still the same rote gameplay. Gather loot, fortify...and sit around.At first I felt that still lacking endgame goals was it's largest weakness. But after playing a lot the past couple weeks, I've been forced to reconsider. The biggest weakness is feature creep and lack of polish of ideas that's been in the game for years already.The UI and how you interact with the world is clunky at best and intensely frustrating at worst. It feels like the character loosely interprets what's asked of them as suggestions and shows a remarkable lack of urgency to accomplish tasks considering it is the apocalypse. For example, combat is cumbersome, repetitive, and still lacking in polish. You can take on several zombies without a weapon (the most I'd advise is 4 btw) and something as simple as holding CTRL, aiming with the mouse, and using the Space Bar can lead to frustration. You can shove zombies over and give them the ol' Mighty Boot. It's fairly straight forward. Until you've slightly adjusted the mouse, and your character starts shoving a tree immediately to the left. Nevermind the cursor is still hovering over the heads of zombies that are very much still animated and getting ready to stand up. So then the character must adjust their positioning to begin the stomppage once more. But now that's confused the targeting of the zombie who attempts to grapple your character by immediately flipping around 180 degrees and latching onto your leg. Or you're in the middle of the shove animation and the zombie you shoved takes a few steps back, rights itself, and then takes a bite out of the air and suddenly, there's a fresh laceration or bite on your torso or arm, despite being more than 6 or 7 tiles away from your attacker. Two handed weapons are another issue entirely. The graphic doesn't come close to intersecting with the zombie's model, yet they sustain damage. But when your two handed weapon cleanly bisects a groaning attacker, nothing happens. If you're lucky, you might get a shove animation to throw them back at least. This happens a lot regardless of your character's mood, level of panic, exhaustion, etc.Falling through stairs is still extremely common place unfortunately. It plagued the demo more than half a decade ago and now seems to be, while less common, still enough of a nuisance to warrant it's own category on Tvtropes.Nutritional information on foods is another example of something that is kinda neat, but there are more pressing concerns to be addressed in game. I know chips, chocolate, and ice cream are high in calories. And I understand fruits and vegetables are good for losing weight, thanks. What it doesn't display is what's the best for healing my broken legs after falling through another stairwell. Again.The lore starts out promising. Watching the people and world react as the contagion doesn't behave as expected is a very welcome amount of world building. But after a week or two, everything stops. Which is disappointing. It would be great to pick up pirate broadcasts over the radio or having a TV channel that's dedicated to informing the citizens on how the government is responding, even if it's just propaganda. With the removal of NPCs and for the beta patch, multiplayer, the game world feels very empty. Not oppressive or lonely, just empty of meaningful things to keep a character going.Which leads me back to what I mentioned at the beginning, the game lacks for things to do. It's very shallow. Your tasks are scavenge, farm, and survive. Even on low loot settings, it doesn't take much more than raiding a several house radius around your stronghold to have enough supplies to comfortably support yourself for a long time, even without starting up a farm. This leads to a frustrating scenario of lacking anything to do if you don't want to go scavenge or fight zombies. There's nothing at home entertaining to do. Literally, nothing for you to click on and interact with, to give you, the player, and your character something to occupy yourself in some downtime. I feel this is especially egregious considering the game has had 7 years to add tasks to occupy your time. Farming, fighting, maintaining your stronghold(s) and vehicle(s) does not take much time and can leave you for want of something more. The only system I can comfortably say has any depth is the car mechanics/maintenance. You have a lot of parts to repair and maintain, influenced by your knowledge or specialization.Outside of lack of depth, lack of endgame goals, and lack of something to occupy your time, there are a few nitpicks that could use some TLC.-The zombie AI is pathetic. Even cranked up to max, zombies are pathetically easy to evade. Just shout, disappear into a house or forest, exit the other side, and circle around. The zombies have lost you and you're free to move about.-Guns could use work. Customizing them would be welcome, especially if you could use metalworking to forge makeshift silencers, attachments, and more. Maybe use electricity skills combined with metalworking and electronic scraps to make items like laser sights or red dot sights than run on the many batteries we find. These skills are crying out for more fleshing out beyond building walls and chairs.-Speaking of skills, I should not need a magazine to help me figure out how to build a storage box. To learn how to make traps, poultices, and more? Absolutely. A box or shelf, no.Lastly, just some common sense things. More forms of entertainment like VCRs and tapes. When I hit E facing a door near a railing, I'd like to be confident that I'm going to close the door and not hop the railing down the stairs. And for gods sake, why do I need to fill a bowl of water to clean a rag when I have running water in the sink or tub? This is something that should have been resolved years ago.While I have spent the last essay basically crapping all over the game it's by no means bad. It's just that it could be so much better. It has so much potential to be a stand out in an over-saturated genre of zombie/survival games. Seeing the potential squandered after 7 long years is just very frustrating. I know there are mods and that seems to be the go to answer for a lot of the issues. I know it's also quickly pointed out that the game is still in early access but that's not a valid excuse anymore, not after a good chunk of a decade of development. While the game has its moments, I cannot recommend you spend actual money on the game. Not when the genre is over-saturated as it is.**EDIT**I've come back after about three years and while many things are still the same, the game is far more interesting. I've dropped another 75+ hours into the game and that speaks well when I've had a game for so long. Still waiting on NPCs though.

Everything from the font to the text size, to the button arrangement, to the tooltips is phenomenally and skillfully done. Information is available and accessible when needed.2. Gameplay 10/10: The original game is already a fantastic RTS, but they've added so much depth in critical areas that remove much of the "genericness" from the game. For example - now you can customize your capital ships as each one has multiple slots for upgrades to fit your strategy/playstyle. Additionally, planet management has much more depth as you can devote worlds to specific types of resources or economic functions. You can now build planetary research facilities as well so you're not completely limited by your orbital building capacity. They keep you on your toes.The additional campaigns provide a fresh map and playthrough experience, as well as offering new factions to choose for the Grand Campaign. There are so many factions to choose from at this point, that I have trouble making up my mind which to play. I probably have 20 saved campaigns, and I have only really touched maybe a third of the playable factions.The unit selection does leave a little to be desired, but some of the DLC's add some depth here and there, enough to where its not an issue for most factions.Multiplayer Campaign: I think this is one of the better selling points of the game. I like to play with others to try to conquer each other or to conquer the AI. Unfortunately, you can only choose to be always allied or always at war. I didn't like this decision, but it doesn't limit the game too much. You and your partner can choose any 2 playable factions for the multiplayer campaign. This means you can be as close to each other or as far from each other as you desire. This provides for some interesting opportunities. The downside is that they do take a while to play, as you can spend 5-10 minutes on a turn easily without even fighting a battle in there. Game options allow you to make a time limit on turns and battles, though, to make game play faster.The bottom line is this: If you are a Total War fan, you should be looking to buy this game. Ignore the original reviews, as they are no longer relevant. Possibly wait for it to go on sale, but this should be a definite buy at this point for anyone who enjoyed the original Rome Total War or any of the Total War series.

Hence we may deduce that the building in this game is very good.If anything, Valheim gives you too many options for it's own good, especially when building, because the engine can't actually handle the kinds of big landscaping projects you inevitably want to do without melting your cpu and lagging out the whole server. For example, our time in the viking world saw several football field land flattening projects and one extremely aggressive push to turn a small creek into a much larger inlet to dock our boats, which also involved completely removing a whole cliff face to build a walkway down to the landing platform. Steve was not happy about that one.Like it or not, I can think of a ton of great stories that have come out of this game, even if it still feels like a somewhat janky early beta. We will watch your career with great interest, and maybe--just maybe, if the stars align sometime in the distant future, we'll also complete the final boss.recommended if you liked "Spyro" on the Playstation 2
