Visions of Mana is mid-tier ARPG comfort food. These types of games are great to boot up at the end of a long day, knowing that you won't have to put much thought into it. There are a lot of things to like about Visions of Mana. The crisp UI and gorgeous general art direction are the two things that stick out the most to me. Everything from the party interface to the crisp damage numbers looks absolutely amazing in Vision of Mana. The sound design is also absolutely fantastic. However... the character design, particularly Val's character design, is extremely odd. Look... I usually stay away from commenting on these types of things in game reviews, BUT Val is a VERY androgynous looking protagonist. We're all mostly used to this when it comes to Japanese ARPG's. They have a tendency to make their main male characters have feminine features, but Val's design really takes the cake. Everything from his Reba McEntire hair style, to the mid drift armor sets are all...uh... very interesting design choices to say the least. Why Japanese JRPG artists seemingly make all of their protagonist look like Caucasian cross dressers, I'll never know. The main reason I comment on this in general is because I really do feel like this game would sell better if the male protagonist lead didn't look like American factory women during WW2. While Val's character design doesn't ruin the game, it is absolutely a constant distraction for me. It's hard to get excited about a new class knowing that Val will almost certainty put on his best Mid-drift, chain skirt combo. Having relatable characters goes along ways, especially with mid-tier RPG's that aren't making up the difference elsewhere. The combat also is not perfect. There are definitely some things to like here, particularly the boss fights, but overall the combat feels floaty, no weight, and has some pretty extreme balance issues. I have about half the classes unlocked at this point, and the shield/spear classes for Val are EXTREMELY under-powered. There's virtually no point in using these classes when the claymore does about x3 the damage. The combo's, class builds, and ability seeds are also extremely lack luster. Besides Val's weapon enhancements, and healing spells, there really no reason to use any other ability. Fireball does about as much damage as half a single weapon swing, regardless of your stats. They only give you 2 ability seed slots (atleast so far), and it's pretty much ALWAYS better to simply use stat increase ability seeds rather than seeds that give you actual new abilities. The spells in this game are very underrepresented, don't do enough damage, and is basically far inferior to simple meele attacks in just about every scenario. It's weird to have a game called Visions of Mana, and then proceed to make magic EXTREMELY underwhelming. All in all, this is most definitely a skipable game. You won't miss much by NOT playing Visions of Mana. You have seen all of these systems done better in other JRPG/ARPG's. However, if you like a change of pace from difficult games, and you're looking for something mid-tier, but enjoyable to put on at the end of the day, Visions of Mana can fill that void.

Pros:• This game has an amazing variety of dinosaurs. The models and textures are very detailed and its quite pleasing and majestic to see how the dinosaurs live, socialize and react. You will most certainly feel good when releasing dinosaurs into their habitats.• The graphics in this game are quite pleasing , and you will most certainly not feel let down on that department• Chaos Theory mode and Campaign mode were engaging enough to make time pass by quite a bit.Cons:• This game has most of its buildings and dinosaurs locked behind the Campaign mode, and expeditions and research in Chaos Theory. The sandbox is arguably the main feature many of us are mainly interested in a park management game, and its quite sad to see that you couldn’t jump into the game and build your dream park right away.• This game has a lot of micromanagement. review: 2014 Just a sad, sad entrant to the Total War series. This is probably the most dissapointing title I have played in the last twenty years. This is the product of a once passionate and aspirational studio which has now sunk under it's own weight of success and has lost all perspective on what makes a game work at it's core. At launch the game was simply utterly broken. The tutorials didn't work, the end turns took minutes, the graphics didn't work, the lag and stutter was incredible, the AI was non-existent, the mechanics weren't thought through. What's more, CA added some awful features (random capture points on the battlefield, magic spells and 1 turn per year anyone?) and removed many staples of the series that made the game so great (seasons, family tree, map trading). Eight full months on, some of this has been amended but the game today is still a shell of a TW title and doesn't really cut the mustard. Seasons have finally been introduced and the game has been optimised so that it actually runs properly but it's just not enough to overcome all of the weaknesses of Rome 2. Siege battles are absolutely redundant, the AI is simply non-functioning. Unit rosters are limited and generic, unit formations do not work properly and battlefield ai remains poor. Naval battles are a joke and sieges are an embarassment. The portraits in the game look abysmal. Because the number of armies is restricted and troops are so easy to afford, every army on the map will be a full stack, which is stupid. Public order and slaves are game systems that do not work properly and detract from the game. Generals and agents die far too quickly. Terrain has no effect in battle (ie archers will have the same range from the bottom of a hill as at the top). Armies can magically cross oceans without the need for building boats. The time it takes armies/navies to traverse the map is stupid (4 years to sail around Italy etc). You can't build walls or roads to improve a settlement. You can't control public order in your settlemets unless you own the entire province, which makes no sense. The civil war is a poorly executed idea which is unrealistic and stupid (armies just spawn out of nowhere in their thouands). The politics system is just tacked on as an afterthought, it's barely worth being there. The technology research is uninspiring and boring. The traits system for armies/generals is similarly unexciting and tedious. The game engine itself doesn't seem to be able to handle the simulation of armed combat (which is a bit of a problem). All in all, this is an absolute trainwreck of a game where the developers obviously looked back over the elements of the TW series that made the games so successful and then decided to jettison anything that was worth a damn and replace it with the worst features they could imagine. There is no hope this game will ever be in a decent state and meanwhile CA pump out the DLCs to be lapped up by devoted fanboys digging the grave of PC gaming by accepting a game made with such low standards.

It's a mix of jokes and serious stuff, you have to be prepared for absurd deaths and brutals happenings, but if you can't handle anything else than fashionable so-called "dark fantasy" you'll be disappointed. Character building. In DOS2, it's not a straightforward process. Sure, you can pick all deafult options and you shouldn't have too many problems - but if you don't enjoy doing things like selecting skills that go well together and/orcrafting, you'll also miss a good part of the game. It's not just about choice between different "specialities", it's really about elaborating strategies and enjoying battle plans.If you're ok with all this, you're likely to enjoy this game. You'll also need a lot of time, obviously, but the "quest log" is sufficiently well done to not lose you if you can't play a lot, and you don't need a lot of time to learn the game (everything is pretty intuitive, you don't need to spend hours on a wiki to know what does what or why you can't do X).Would kickstart again.

I almost never write reviews for games on Steam because I believe they're a complete waste of time, but this game is so offensively bad I actually feel obligated to. Rant ahead. I fell for the "oh it's just 1 euro how bad could it be" meme but my god was I wrong. I'll start off with the first thing I immediately noticed, which is the atrocious sound design. From the very first tutorial race I genuinely could barely hear my car's engine. Now, I don't know if it's an issue on my end, but I had to go into the settings to turn almost all the way down every other setting, while cranking up the engine sound to max in order to be able to actually hear anything. The second thing I noticed was the wonky driving physics. Cars just feel weird to drive, when you first start turning sometimes they just understeer like crazy only to snap on you a moment a later, making taking precise corners inconsistent. It kind of felt like driving on soap or ice. I looked over that, thinking it was just a question of getting used to different physics, but it felt pretty crap all the way through my 4 hours of playing. It kinda felt as if the devs were unsure if they wanted to go for an arcadey tap break to drift, or something closer to what forza horizon has. Next up is the map. It's so unnecessarily big and empty that driving around through it is mind numbingly boring. If you're not teleporting around between events, you'll find yourself driving through stretches of almost completely straight, wide open, middle of nowhere, nearly empty roads that just go on and on forever. If instead of trying to give us the entirety of the USA they only gave us a single more highly detailed State, the game would've greatly benefited from it. I'm not going really to touch on the story, since one of the first things I did was to turn off the dialogue volume and skip nearly every cutscene besides the first few. This game unfortunately suffers from the "horizonification" of racing games, where every game needs to be some sort of big dumb festival where everybody is just happy to be there and the player is treated like a lobotomized toddler. It's not about competition but just participation, and the races absolutely reflect that in the worst way since you're not even tasked to win, but just end up in the top 3. Hell the point of the game isn't even racing (story-wise) but to amass followers on some unspecified social media. Why would I even care about something like that? It seems as if the devs forgot this is a racing game, and in a race the whole point is to go from point A to point to B faster than your opponents, giving the whole thing a participation trophy bs type of feeling. The game tries to lecture you about cars and racing history, trying to act as if they actually give a ♥♥♥♥ about any of it, and then immediately slap you on your big dumb face with the reward and upgrade systems. These systems are so baffling that I genuinely feel like they must've been decided by some corporate dickwad, because I refuse to believe that any dev with any integrity would want to implement them. When you finish an event, you get rewarded with Bucks (which you get playing the game, not to be confused with the PREMIUM ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ CURRENCY IN A 50 EURO GAME called Crew Credits) and a random assortment of upgrade parts. These parts, as far as I can tell, are all random and can only be obtained by completing events or finding caches in the open world. The most insulting thing is that they're literally just stat numbers, they don't physically change anything about the car besides making it slightly go faster or have slightly more grip. But the most abhorrent thing is that they actually come with rarities and SET BONUSES like some sort of botched conception between forza horizon and a mediocre looter shooter. It baffles me so much that this game pretends to give a single ♥♥♥♥ about car culture, and then it doesn't allow me to actually customize the performance of my car in a straight forward and deeper way than just getting some moronic loot boxes after finishing a race. I can't just go in the customization menu and slap a new transmission, turbo or brakes on my car, I have to just play the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ lottery. But if the cars are not bad enough, the planes and boats are somehow worse. First off, who the hell even asked for those? The planes handle horribly (coming from someone who's played ace combat and other arcade flying games), and the boats are such a joke to drive that the races are a complete snoozefest. The offroading is passable at best, and the drifting events can be kinda fun, physics permitting. Didn't enjoy any of the bikes. Honestly, if you're stuck on PC, only have a single euro to your name and are desperate for an open world racing game to play, then sure go for it. For anyone else, do yourself a favor and don't waste a single minute on this sad excuse for a videogame. I wish I could get my euro back.

It's pretty satisfying being able to perform well timed jumps from high above to skip some of the challenges, but I'm not sure if thats intentional. They removed some shackles from the release version to make the movement customizable and more engaging, but I think they might have broken some aspects here and there and made some of these challenges trivial. But all in all, I had a lot of fun doing 100%.The cyberspace level on the other hand were very dissapointing. They put sonic into realistic environments with flying platforms, rails and such, which doesn't align with the cartoony sonic figures. There is also very ugly pop in, which could be easily fixed if there was some kind of fade effect. I mean the main theme is the cyberspace, why aren't the platforms coming in with some kind of pixelisque effect?I mean it's not as uncanny as sonic '06 but still not good to look at.dlc campaignWell, since this one was part of some free updates, I don't wanna be too harsh on that, but oh boy some of these challenges are just awful to play. Now we have 3 more playable characters, but they only differ slightly from sonic. But all of these new moves are either overpowered or debuffs/useless. Tails for example has some kind of move where he's able to fly all over the map without any limits whereas he can skips almost all jumping challenges. Knuckles on the other hand has his iconic glide, but whenever you're starting to do that, there is a long starting animation with terrible controlsBut even sonic has his down parts. There are some tower challenges which are straight up impossible to do them normally (on hard difficulty), because you need a very specific strategy which are difficult to come up by yourself. Some other challenges on the other hand are way too easy with more than a whole minute remaining time at the end. So yeah, it's pretty unbalanced with random difficulty spikes (don't wanna talk about the ridiculously insane damage the field bosses can make, since I ignored them as much as possible >_>).conclusionWell, this was a lot of backlash now, I know, but I can still recommend this game if you want a new sonic game. But I would suggest grabbing this on sale, because there are indeed some downer here and there, which can put you off. But most of them are part of the artistic choices, gameplay-wise it's an enjoyable experience with a lot of room for improving in future entries.

2021 “Yeah, we’re doing it so much better” - (Horizon 5 Opening Song) (A review of Forza Horizon 5 coming up as soon as I finish drifting down the volcano…) Summary- An open world racing game chock full of cars, races, drifts and sweet jumps, Forza Horizon 5 is a fun ride through Mexico that maintains the core fundamentals of what made Horizon 4 a lot of fun, while improving several aspects of the game. New and returning players alike are both guaranteed a lot of fun here. They are indeed, doing it better than any other open world racing game on the market! Should you buy this? Yes. Review in Detail Gameplay: I usually start my reviews talking about the game’s story, but since Horizon 5 doesn’t have a traditional story, I’ll discuss the gameplay in detail.At its core, Forza Horizon 5 is an open world racing game with a lean towards the arcade end of the “arcade-sim” slider. You’re dropped into 107 square kilometer (41 miles square) map of Mexico , complete with 11 separate biomes and a recreation of the city of Guanajuato. After you’ve been dropped off in the hub, the game gives you a small number of races and stunts to complete so that you can earn points and unlock more races and story missions. It’s then up to you to decide what you want to do. Maybe you’ll explore the whole map, discovering new locations and collectibles? Or maybe you’ll spend hours drifting a Supra, testing how many millions of combos you can get? Or maybe you’ll work your way up the volcano (yes, there’s a volcano in game. There are 48 active volcanos in Mexico!) and see how far you can launch the Corvette off a ramp? Let’s talk about what Horizon 5 offers you in terms of racing. There are 5 race types in game: Circuit (you lap a closed tarmac road course), Sprint (a straight dash to the finish line), Dirt racing (races on tarmac and dirt roads), Cross country (races primarily done off-road) and Street racing (like Sprint races, but set in the night without any protective barriers and the traffic turned on). You unlock every race type by progressing through the story mode and once unlocked, you can participate in any available race whenever you want. You’re also free to do any race with whichever vehicle you want and the AI will match your car type and performance class. Want to race down a volcano in classic muscle cars? You can. How about racing trucks through a rainforest? Go wild. With the exception of the weekly challenge races, the game never forces you to use a certain vehicle type for a race, adding immensely to its replay value. The game’s weather also changes every week, so a you might find yourself drifting in the middle of a sandstorm in the weather one week, followed by a race in a thunderstorm the next and then racing atop a frozen volcanic crater the week after that. One of the things that has had a substantial overhauling from Horizon 4 to 5 is the game’s progression system. The new “Accolade” system, which will be familiar to players of Horizon 4’s Lego Island, gives you challenges to complete for points. They range from the simple, like winning races or 3 starring a stunt, to challenging, like driving from one place to another in a certain car within a time limit or stringing together a specific skill chain. Once you’ve collected a certain amount of points, the game gives you an unlock point so you can unlock a chapter of your adventure. Every chapter costs 1 point apiece, so you’re free to unlock whichever chapter you’d like. Some challenges even unlock emotes, chat lines and new cars, so you’ll always wanna keep an eye out.I mentioned Horizon 5 being closer to an arcade racer than a sim racer earlier. Basically, before you start of any race, the game lets you choose from multiple available difficulty modes and driving assists, with harder difficulties and no assists rewarding you extra money. The game also has a pretty detailed car upgrade system, allowing you upgrade a car’s engines and transmission for more speed and acceleration, or tyres and drivetrain for better handling and so on. There’s also a pretty detailed tuning system that lets you fine tune exactly how you want your car to feel. It’s not a lot compared to any serious sim, but it’s still pretty extensive. Unfortunately, the game doesn’t explain the tuning system in much detail, but for those who just want to get to the racing without having to learn about rebound stiffness and camber, you can always download player made tunes for any car and get straight to the action. Speaking of player made tunes, let’s talk about some of the game’s online features. The game lets you share tunes, paints, stunt challenges and custom race tracks you’ve made with other players. If your work gets used, you even make some money in game! Every race in game can be co-oped against the AI with a team of upto 6 people, and you can also play PvP. Horizon 5 also offers two game modes exclusive to PvP, the Playgrounds mode and the Eliminator. Playgrounds mode is a series of modes where you team up with others to take on the enemy in games of tag and soccer. Eliminator is Horizons take on the battle royale, pitting upto 50 players in a game of survival. There are also hourly events, the Horizon Arcades, where you have to complete a bunch of mini missions with other players in 10 minutes for points that you can redeem in the game store for rare cars or cosmetics. Want a certain car, but it’s too expensive or rare? There’s the auction house in game where you can bid on cars against other people! With so many online features and the weekly challenges, it’s easy to see why Horizon has sometimes been called a racing mmo.Graphics and Sound: Making an open world look and sound good is a huge part of the immersion. How does Horizon 5 stack up in this?Freaking phenomenally, that’s how. Each of the game’s biomes looks and sounds spectacular. A lot of detail has been put in the game and it shows. Even on medium and low graphics settings, you can go on top of a cliff in the canyons or the volcano and look around for miles in game. The world is full of little details, like small dogs and donkeys roaming about in fields and villages, who will always manage to avoid your car! Driving in the desert, through a sandstorm is as thrilling as you’d expect, because you can see it’s size looming over you as you approach it. The lakes and canals in game dry up in the hot season and then fill back up in the rain and storm season. All of this is exceptional attention to detail, and its brought to life with amazing graphics. The city of Guanajuato is also reproduced pretty well, with great recreations of its historic landmarks, streets and tunnels. A plus work all around in the graphics department.The game sounds just as great as it looks as well. The cars sound great, and when you change their engines or exhausts, that change is reflected in game as well. That is great attention to detail and a massive improvement on Horizon 4’s stock car sounds. The game’s soundtrack is good. I’ve already found a few new favorites, though you mileage might vary on this.Final Words: Forza Horizon 5 is one of the greatest racing games I’ve played and certainly a top contender for best game of 2021. If you’re a fan of any sort of racing game, you’re gonna have a fun time playing this. Even at full price, this game is worth every penny.

2019 Age of Empires 2: Definitive Edition is a faithful remake of the original. This is the second such “remake, ” although it is far more substantial that the “HD edition” which launched back in 2013. I have owned this game since original disc in 1999, along with “The Conquers” (2000) expansion, but have bought all subsequent digital versions simply because I enjoyed the way this game plays.In brief, it is a good game and definitely worth playing if you’re a long-time fan of the series or strategy games in general. In addition to including all the DLC from the HD edition, it also adds a few new civilization and campaigns. If you’re picking this up for the first time, it is definitely dated in terms of mechanics (don’t expect Company of Heroes or Dawn of War) but it is intended to stay faithful to the original design. Mostly Quality of Life Improvements This game starts with a new 3D engine that makes everything look much nicer and graphics are now able to smoothly scale up to 4K. One important addition is the villager-per-resource on the info bar up top. Newly added civilizations get their own building styles, which is a nice touch.The campaign map is now sub-divided into continents, which makes it easier to navigate through and the missions are labeled from which “expansion” they come from. One suggestion here would be to add a filter to select a specific set of missions (i.e. only Age of Kings, only The Conquers, etc.).LAN was supported as of launch, which was great because this is how I usually play with family! It’s not obvious and somewhat hidden in the multiplayer “Create Lobby” menu under the “server” options. There are some strange de-sync issues, but that will probably be patched with time.As of the launch window, Xbox Live is not “required” to play (at least for casual games) as it seems to have its own Steam lobby system, but you can still sign into Xbox Live if you have it. Currently Xbox Live based games have the Xbox logo beside them. I’m not sure about the competitive multiplayer side of things, as I do not use it. Where it falters Firstly, Steam Workshop! I don’t really understand why we had to be gated behind MS’ systems as Workshop worked well enough with the 2013 HD edition. My only guess would be it has something to do with the Xbox Live integration. For every great step forward in the PC gaming space MS seem to take two backwards. But I digress…Given this Definite Edition was created anew from the ground up, I was hoping to see regional/cultural clothing for units as it is very jarring to see an Asian Halberdier look exactly like the European one. I understand this would take more effort, but would absolutely haven been worth it considering everything was re-worked for the new engine anyway. Alas, being the cynical old gamer that I am, I think this was shovelled away so that MS can sell AoE 4 as demonstrated by the short trailer during X019. (Just speculation on my part, only time will tell!)Unit formations, while generally good, definitely have some pathfinding issues as grouped units will very often scramble back and forth and awkwardly re-organize themselves from time to time as they move about the map.Another commonly occurring pathfinding issue includes a villager occasionally ceasing work upon reaching the gather limit and failing to return to the drop off point, with no apparent obstruction. However, these are not game-breaking bugs and I have hope these trivial things will eventually be patched out. Conclusion This is a game that stays true to the original launched back in 1999 and adds many quality of life improvements, along with great modern graphics! Since it's original Definitive Edition launch, it has added a ton of new civilizations giving users many options to play.

2016 I had never imagined that Stellaris would be such a great game. Having played other Paradox games such as Europa Universalis 4, Crusader Kings 2 and Victoria 2, I had expected a very intricated and complex game in terms of strategy, but Stellaris has accomplished much more than this. Firstly, Paradox managed to get the genre perfectly. Being a Star Trek fan, I can say that there are inumerous features that are very resembling to the world of the original series. The game, however, does not restrict itself to Star Trek and there are references to various other classical features of the genre. Regarding the other Paradox games, I feel that in Stellaris war is not so important and it in peace that you wil play most hours of the game (specially at the first decades). Of course, being a mix of grand strategy and 4X, Stellaris was expected to have some exploration mechanics, but Stellaris also have loads of ways to develop your empire at peace. Moreover, the complexity of the mechanics are fantastic. They are in no way difficult to learn and it is very fun to manage the social and political aspects of your empire. The empire creator is also amazing with a lot of different governments to choose in addition to ethics and general characteristics of your people. The AI empires react to your presence mainly according to their and your ideology which makes for very funny games. Finally, the UI is a thousand times more accessible than in past Paradox games and the tutorial does a good job, which in my view makes the game not so difficult to learn to newcomers to the grand strategy genre.

These elements can detract from the overall immersion and polish of the game.Map Design and EnvironmentWhere CarX Street shines is in its map design. The highway loop provides a fantastic venue for high-speed maneuvers, while the dense city roads are perfect for street racing. The game’s settings are deeply rooted in street racing culture, reminiscent of the beloved Need For Speed Underground series, which adds a nostalgic touch for fans of the genre.Customization and ContentCarX Street excels in car customization, offering a depth that rivals or even surpasses many alternative racing titles. Furthermore, at just $20, the game is a bargain compared to the $80 price tags of many AAA racing titles, making it an accessible option for budget-conscious players.ConclusionCarX Street may have some rough edges, particularly in handling and optimization, but it offers a rewarding experience for those who appreciate its strengths. review: (Warframe player's review, this is from a non bias POV as I am treating this game as a separate entity and new player to the genre not just a competitor as personally I am glad us looter shooter fans are getting a new game, and I am more than happy to help it grow and get better so I can have multiple games to play.)The Good:As a big fan of this genre, and a veteran who has played almost every single one of them, some for longer like warframe, I must admit that I was hesitant to even start this game(bc of Nexon) even though I played the betas. I first were introduced to this game from trailers at big events and I quickly got into the week long crossplay beta. When I first played it I fell in love as it mixed a lot of the things I loved from Warframe with Destiny bosses and gunplay. I feel as if this game took a lot of the best ideas from those games and in some ways improved upon them with a fresh look into the genre. Now do I think this is as polished as Warframe? No, but I think this is the perfect game to give me a break from my other games, and this is a game I will come back to every time a major update is out as for a F2P game I cannot complain. No one knows what the future holds, and I am very excited for the road map they showed off, and I truly think this game "could" rival Warframe in terms of F2P looter shooter if handled properly and updated regularly with meaningful changes given from the community.The Bad:This game is from Nexon, a company I do not like, and I know most people do not, now as of right now I don't really care about the prices in the shop as you don't need to buy them and I am proof of that as I have 5 descendants already, and I am very late game. I have not bought a single thing yet, but because of how good this game is I will for sure buy the battlepass, and maybe a skin for whoever ends up being my favorite. HOWEVER, the prices in this game are not the best, or they are all over the place, and this is one of the reasons I suggest playing the game first then buying things if you like it. For those calling this game "Pay 2 Win" all I can assume is that they have never played Warframe, or is not used to grinding as this game has never forced me to pay for anything, nor have I ever thought about buying anything to "skip the grind". This game does have "skip the grind" in the shop very similarly to Warframe, where you can pay to speed up crafting something, or out right buy any of the Descendants you want. Trust me when I say to not buy anyone unless you really want to, as most of the Descendants are pretty easy to get you just need to grind for them, and in many cases they are given through story missions with a 20% drop chance, or easily obtainable after you unlock "hard mode" after you beat the story.The Eh: 1. This game needs trading already, I know it's coming as one of the devs did confirm it's being made for a content update in future and I can only tell you what trading has done for Warframe. If this game gets trading that is similar to that of Warframe's then you will truly be able to play this game "F2P" as you would be able to grind and get about almost anything you want by trading with real people for it. I can already see the amount of players at the end of this week that will be wanting to trade and it's sad that they didn't include that at launch.2. One of the MTX in this game is called "descendants slots", as you only have so many of them starting out, which means if you make "x" amount of descendants you will need to pay real money or "50 Caliber" in order to unlock more slots so you can make more descendants. This wouldn't be a problem if the game had trading as you could just trade when you got to that point, and the only reason why I am not putting this in "the bad" tier is because this game has a lot for you to do, and I think most normal people that are grinding the game normally won't get to that cap until the trade update is soon to be out. However, if you start the game now just know you might have to get more slots if you are quick to farm the descendants.Overall: I believe this is a very fun game, one that has kept my attention for multiple days, and I found myself thinking about it when I wasn't playing it. This has the potential to rival Warframe or the other great games of the genre, however, I don't think it's there yet but maybe with updates it will get better. This game isn't "Pay 2 Win" it's "Pay 2 Lose" as you're really just giving yourself less game to play. TFD needs trading already, and if trading is implemented well then I would be very happy to be completely positive about this game as most things would be able to be obtained by "grinding" only. Overall I think this game has potential and should look upon Warframe for future quality of life updates as it isn't perfect by any means, but it's oddly addicting, and it reminds me of when Warframe first came out with all the bugs, builds, and failed attempts at boss fights.

2014 Early Access Review If I was asked to describe Unturned in two words, those words would be "DayZ Lite". Yes, I would cheat and turn "Day Z" into a single word, because it's just that apt of a comparison. Everything I could say about this game could just as easily be used to describe Day Z. The main differences outside of the graphics is that the map is smaller, and the zombies are easier to fight. Oh, that and it's free, so that's always a plus.Unturned has players starting on the shore of a beach on an island that's been overrun with zombies. They start with literally nothing, not even clothes on their back. As a survivor on the island, it's the player's job to outwit the zombies, salvage for supplies, and survive against the odds. Players must find sources of food or water, lest they starve. They will need medicine to keep from dying of sickness, and of course they will need first aid; not only to keep their health up, but also to heal any fractured bones or bleeding. Oh, and don't forget about weapons to fend-off zombies and hostile survivors.Gameplay-wise the game is very functional. While it isn't flawless, there aren't as many bugs as one might expect from an Early Access title. It really feels like an all-but finished product that's just getting some polish out of the way before it can be said to be ready for prime time. The only niggling issue in the current build is that the zombies only have AI once they've spotted a player, otherwise they stand stock-still; not even turning or moaning. Hopefully the developer(s) have some idle AI in the works that will be implemented before the game is officially "launched", as the lack of zombie AI is just another thing that contributes to this game feeling like "Day Z Lite".At the end of the day, whether or not Unturned can be recommended is directly linked to how you feel about zombie games. Anyone who's sick of tired of them and wishes that a new trend would finally come along, Unturned is unlikely to feel fresh and new-enough to sway their opinion. Anyone who can't get enough of zombies, on the other hand, will likely find that Unturned is competent as what it does, especially for a game that is both free and has an Early Access label. Further, if you're someone who's always wanted to check-out Day Z but never felt quite confident-enough to slam-down $30 for the entry fee, Unturned makes for a good preview. Anyone who enjoys Unturned but finds themselves wanting something a little more robust will very-likely be happy with the $30 spent on Day Z. Likewise, someone who's played Day Z but wants something a little more lax will probably find Unturned to be a very comfortable vacation spot.

2014 Total War: Rome 2 suffered from a rough start, releasing with many questionable design choices and numerous severe bugs and optimization issues. This led to poor fan reception and a Metacritic score lower than that of any Total War title to date. At launch, and for quite some time after, I would not have recommended Rome 2. Thanks to Creative Assembly's continued support of the game, it has now reached a stage where it is reasonably enjoyable with the recent release of the Emperor Edition. The game has metamorphosed drastically since the game received is initial reviews.The Emperor Edition, released on September 16, 2014, drastically overhauled the game. The building system was redesigned for the better, factions all underwent extensive rebalancing and recieved new, more natural factional colors, unit abilities were overhauled, and last but not least, a new free campaign, Imperator Augustus, was released. All of this was added to the game free of charge! With the changes introduced in Emperor Edition, I'd recommend Rome 2 to anyone interested in a grand strategy game with RTS and TBS elements set in the ancient world.All of the DLC is recommendable, though depending on your personal preference, you may wish to skip the unit packs. The two DLC campaigns, Caesar in Gaul and Hannibal at the Gates, offer an experience different from that of the Grand Campaign and Imperator Augustus. They are more focused experiences, zooming in on the world map to flesh out Gaul and the Mediterranean, respectively, in greater detail than what is found in the Grand Campaign. Caesar in Gaul, Hannibal at the Gates, and Imperator Augustus all also operate at a slower yearly rate, with one turn per season, as opposed to the Grand Campaign's one turn per year. This greatly increases the number of turns you will have generals and agents at your disposal before they die of old age, allowing them to accrue more experience than they would be able to in the Grand Campaign. All of the DLC content is reasonably priced for its value, especially during sales.My biggest gripe with the Rome 2 is how visually disappointing it is. The lack of true AA makes the game so much uglier, and the art direction really is vastly inferior to that of Shogun 2, in the UI, graphics, and soundtrack.The UI itself is my second biggest problem with Rome 2. Playing as an egalitarian pacifist democracy or a xenophobe military dictatorship does not feel all that different. I want the choices I make lead to games that feel qualitatively different, not just the same thing with slightly different stats.For example, it would be great if, as a democratic nation, you had a mandate within which you could operate and for decisions outside that mandate you had to gather enough support in parliament from the different factions. 2021 Before I go into the reasons I can't recommend this game, I will say that there are many aspects of this game that are simply marvellous. This is a beautiful game, with a rich story I haven't seen in 4x sci-fi games before. The tech tree is interesting and well fleshed out, with research that can truly feel like you are shaping the society you are building. The AI isn't completely stupid, and unlike many games I've played, they make relatively understandable choices when it comes to diplomacy (though they still sometimes will pick a fight they can't win) There are a lot of options when creating your race, and it feels like there are a lot of societal differences that are meaningful, and not as shallow as "more research" or "better attack" The art and soundtrack are good, the writing is good, and the user interface is pretty friendly.So why don't I recommend this game? I'm sure these themes will be familiar if you've read other critical reviews of this game:1) The base game feels incomplete, and a number of the features that come with the DLC feel like they are features that really should have been part of the base game. They would have been better served to simply not have certain mechanics in the game at all rather than have a bare bones version (e.g. federations, espionage) that is effectively useless without the relevant expansions. They also plant the seeds for events and development that simply goes nowhere (or perhaps only goes nowhere until you have the relevant DLC) One example I'll give is AI research. The game warns you that certain AI technology is dangerous, but as near as I can tell, without certain DLC there is nothing in the game to MAKE them dangerous (i.e. having AI revolts, or having them seek independence)2) It feels like the end game hadn't been thought through. I played a race through to the point where I have technologically ascended, and I was looking for a win condition there that simply wasn't there. It feels like the technology trees run out long before the game does. And there doesn't seem to be any win condition outside of galactic conquest.3) Combat. I understand that options are limited given it is a real time game, but it's hard to see what's happening in combat, and just as importantly, why your fleets are winning or losing (are my weapon choices ineffective? Is there a particular type of attack my opponent uses that I lack a defence for?) This information is SORT OF there if you dig, but a more detailed breakdown would be helpful. 4) Ship Design: I also have a personal beef that the game auto-designs your ships for you, but makes odd choices at times, at times choosing weapons or systems that are vastly inferior to other ones researched (e.g. lv1 mass drivers instead of the lv3 lasers or missiles), and you have to turn off auto-builds entirely to be able to create a unique design of your own. It would be much easier to manage a fleet if you were able to tweak the auto-designs, or to be able to have your own unique designs in parallel to the automatic ones. There is also no way to save or copy designs that I could see.5) Race types: Though they give a generous range of options for your race, there is one aspect that is only cosmetic and could have added a bit more depth: species. You can choose humanoid, avian, fungus, etc., but that particular choice is only cosmetic. It would've been interesting to make different categories of race have an impact on game play, if only by offering one or two unique technologies, or other minor tweaks. This is a minor beef though.There should have been a "season's pass" option, or simply offer the DLC at a price lower than the base game itself. It's frustrating to feel like you don't get a complete game without the DLC. DLC, in my opinion, should be for adding new/additional content, but not mechanics that feel more-or-less essential to the experience.

2020 To anyone who is a die-hard strategy gamer, I cannot recommend any game more than this one. For this review, I will first cover the negatives, and then the positives. In my view, if you can't get over the negatives, then there is no point in reviewing the positives.-Negatives:1. The game is expensive, and has a lot of dlc attached to it. I would recommend (like with all Steam items) to wait for a sale to get the game and it's dlc's. Doing so will end up saving you a LOT of money.2. You will need a relatively high-performance computer. Total War games are notoriously heavy in terms of storage needed and performance. The game is loading in thousands of soldiers per battle, each with their own individual model.3. The victory conditions on campaign are brutally large and hard to complete. This is a minor one, since most of the time the player will set goals for themselves to meet instead of the superficial one the game provides.4. Vortex campaign (the vanilla campaign) is somewhat gimmicky compared to the Mortal Empires campaign, which I considered the definitive Warhammer 2 experience. The only way to play Mortal Empire is to buy Warhammer 1, which is another expense the consumer must put up with. That being said, buying Warhammer 1 also unlocks another 5 races to play as in ME, without any other dlc, so you could consider it a large dlc package.Pros:1. The games offers hundreds to thousands of hours of content. From dozens of unique campaigns, to custom battles that can test infinite possibilities, and multiplayer coop and vs modes, this game won't grow old anytime soon.2. The dlc (for the most part) offer enough fun content for the price given. I would recommend every dlc available except Blood for the Blood God, Warriors of Chaos, Call of the Beastmen, Wood Elves, and the Grim and the Grave. (If you are having enough fun to warrant buying dlc, of course.)3. Any problem you find with the gameplay itself (lore conflicts, small unit rosters, gameplay bugs or annoyances) can be fixed through the mods you can find in the Steam Workshop. I use several mods in my campaigns, and greatly appreciate the enhanced experience they offer.4. I genuinely believe that this is one of the best strategy games on the market. From the empire management, to the battle tactics, to the sheer degree of content offered, you can't do much better than Total War, Warhammer 2.In summary: If you can overlook the price tag of the game and dlc attached to it (or be smart and wait for a sale), you will love this game. 2015 Firstly, I would like to thank the 4X-enthusiast group eXplorminate for giving away this game. I typically don't pay much attention to giveaways, but I actually won something that time. And that something happened to be a game that seemed somewhat fascinating to me at the time.As of now, Endless Legend is a whole lot more than "mildly fascinating," and I am shocked I did not know about it sooner. This is one of the few games that I wish so many more people did know about. My opinion of this game is from the perspective of a[nother] person stepping into it from Civilization V. I also have some Total War to be comparing it to, so I have that to reference as well. That said....Endless Legend is a beautiful game. There are few other words that can describe it so aptly. The presentation of Auriga (the gameworld) from the map anomalies to the tile improvements that match the civilization's stylistic impressions to the special effects during winter to the GUI, everything about the game is beautiful. The UI deserves a special shout-out, because everything is placed so intuitively, and it's simple, clean, and elegant. There is no other game that matches the polish of Endless Legend's UI (although vanilla Civ and G+K were both very meticulous through the menus and what-not). As a turn-based strategy, the gameplay is sufficiently balanced, and the overall war mechanic is somewhat more sophisticated than what you'd find in Civilization, using Total War's army-building model. The quest functionality provides a lot of deep lore, and it really is amazing how intricate Amplitude's universe is - they have clearly committed a lot of energy to just... being creative here - so I have to mention it even though I really don't care for it much in my playthroughs. I don't have to, though. It's there if you want it, but I'm just not an RPG person. My biggest gripe about the game is how much ALL CAPS ARE USED IN ITEM DESCRIPTIONS. I MEAN, IT'S KIND OF ANNOYING TO READ.All in all, it's a fantasy version of Civ that is very, very polished, endlessly replayable (see what I did there?), full of character, surprisingly strong on the war/conflict front, and I am recommending it now solely because I want more people to know about it. I encourage you to pick it up, or at least look into it a little deeper.

There are few characters who talking like 10 years old with weird slang, but not every character is like that. Also, few characters are actually characters and have proper development throughout the game. Not even mentioning to some fourth wall breaking topics and questions which the game brings up throughout the playthrough, making it more interesting and not "cringe". The style of the game is unique, and I do understand that some people don't like this kind of visuals, but I was okay with it. It wasn't annoying nor distracting to watch for me.Game is too difficult! Not gonna lie, this is the first NFS after I don't know how many years, where it had some challenge in the story. Races are not easy, you need to use your nitro and boost properly and strategies to have a good finish, because you don't have to win every race, you just need to get money. Police chases got more difficult as well, since the AI got a bit more advanced and they can actually make your time more difficult. You can get to high heat levels early pretty fast, where you can get destroyed easily if you don't know what are you doing. Not even mentioning the 3 difficulty levels, well at first I tried to go on the hardest difficulty but after seeing the drift scores to beat, I decided to stick to challenging difficulty. I understand some people disappointment with this part, but I was delighted to see that this game is actually not "a pushover" and I have to try harder to beat the police or the races to advance, so git gud.Controls are trash! Sadly the controls were annoying in Heat as well, but it somewhat got better in Unbound in my opinion, it's not that understeery than it was before and it don't get too drifty that many times. I can recommend playing with traction control on when you drive A+ or higher class cars, which helped to control my cars. Also, you have to understand the pros and cons for grip and drift cars. I'm not saying Criterion did wonders with this control scheme, but it's not that bad than it was before, but this is certainly a field to get better for the devs.Game is not optimized / Multiplayer is unplayable due to disconnects! On lowest settings playing in fullHD I had 60 FPS no problem on PC, meanwhile the game was still alright looking. It could be better but my 1050 Ti handled it alright. About the multiplayer: I got disconnected only two times in my 25 - 30 hours of online play and that's due to inactivity. I never had issues with disconnects, but maybe I was lucky to play in general.Soundtrack is horrible! Yes I get this one, but comparing to Heat where I liked only 2 - 3 songs, there are atleast 5 - 6 now which I enjoy for real and only 4 other songs which I skip instantly when I hear in Unbound. So yeah, the soundtrack is not that good but it's still an upgrade comparing to Heat.Even though I countered most of the critical points of the game, I have to add that it's a bit disappoint to see the lack of tracks in the game, not even mentioning the long and grindy challenges to get cars in multiplayer. I also had troubles with the confusing UI in the multiplayer and the lack of replayability of the story mode, because after a playthrough you cannot replay it from scratch, except if you delete your save file, which also deletes your progression in the multiplayer. The game also lacks anything new to racing games, it uses the well known formula of open world racing games, which works but gives nothing new really in terms of gameplay.In my opinion Need for Speed Unbound is a fun and challenging game if you into it, it also offers some fresh air with it's style and I can recommend to play it. 70€ is too much for this title, but getting it around 15€ is a good deal in my opinion.

Lots of room for more buildings to be added, obviously an EA title so to be expected- Combat is quite bare bones. The focus of the game is city builder at the core, but I think there would be so much wasted potential if combat wasn't the second major focus as it's such a strong gameplay loop. I'm hoping over time it's refined and fleshed out more, but I'm happy that it's included at all- There aren't many missions other than your win con, but I believe missions are planned to be added at a later date. Otherwise we have to wait for more content in the form of missions- Some resources I haven't figured out if they even do anything. Some resources are barely even used, if at all- I work in game audio and I'm just going to say it now... I had to mute music because it's depressing - a great track maybe for Main Menu, but need a little bit more chill or slightly more uplifting music during gameplay. 2016 What is WARFRAME?It's an Online, Third-Person Shooter, Hack & Slash, Action Adventure Game with Co-Op and MMORPG elements, among some other things mixed in together for good measure.It's also completely Free to Play!Warframe is set in the far distant future, where you play as an armored cyborg space wizard ninja warrior with weird magic powers, travelling across the Solar System, exploring and completing various missions, uncovering the hidden purpose and deep lore behind everything.In this game, you are the Judge, Jury and Executioner for every member of the various alien factions you meet along the way, dispensing justice in the most stylish way possible with a huge variety of different customizable weapons.While the game definitely can be played as an enjoyable Single-Player experience, it was primarily designed around playing together with other people.This game breaks all the rules for traditional RPG's, you are not limited to specific classes, skill builds and weapon choices. You can switch and change anything as much as you like. You can totally be a sneaky stealthy tank healer while using a bow with explosive arrows, dual-wielding machineguns, carrying a heavy two-handed greatsword all at the same time and still be very effective at all stages of the game.On the ranged side of weapons, you have everything from shotguns, assault and sniper rifles to guns that shoot lasers, rockets, fire, ice, lightning, blades or even black holes.On the melee side of weapons, you have everything from swords, hammers and axes to nunchakus, whips and gunblades. You can also change their entire movement set by using different Stances.There are quite a few actual main storyline quests and not that many cinematic cutscenes, but most of those quests are very well made and can be extremely rewarding to players that invest a lot of time in to the game.As you progress thoughout the game, you will unlock more and more new gameplay modes and mechanics, the game can always suprise you with something even after hundreds and hundreds of hours of playtime.The lore is quite interesting and isn't shoved in your face, most of it is hidden away and you have work for it if you're really interested.This game puts alot of emphasis on style in every part of it, you also can spend hours on just making your Warframe look as terrible or as fabolous as you want it to. It's way better than Space Barbie.You can also have a Space Dog. You can also have a Space Cat. You can also have a Flying Space Roomba with a shotgun. You can also have a walking Robot Chicken with a Robot Top Hat.The majority of the game currently consists of relatively short missions (similar to instance-based dungeons), however they also have large open world areas with more traditional MMO-like content, with even more to come in the future.The devs are extremely friendly and even livestream their current progress on the game, showing off future stuff and taking feedback from the community.Warframe can eventually boil down to just a grinding farming simulator if you go hard at it, but that's the nature of every dungeon-crawling type of RPG's, at least in this game you can wallrun and do backflips while your at it.The game is in no way Pay-to-Win, you can easily complete all the content with stuff you can get very early in the game. As far as Free-to-Play games go, this one is quite generous and is pretty fair overall.The more you play, the more you will understand that there isn't actually anything you really need to spend money on, especially considering you can earn the real money currency in-game for free by trading items.I would recommend investing just a little amount of real money to make your life a bit more convenient, but it's totally optional and completely unnecessary to progress through the game.I personally spent most of my real money on purely Quality-of-Life and cosmetic items that I could've gotten eventually anyway, so take from that what you will.Solid recommendation, one of the best Free-to-Play games ever made! :)

2022 SHORT REVIEW:One of the most atmospheric and stunning games I've ever played.It takes only a few hours to finish and the whole time you'll be engaged by a beautiful yet vividly twisted world, fantastic monster designs, a brooding ambient OST, simple yet captivating enough gameplay and, of course, plenty of little goblin guys with big funny hats that go "chkchkchkchkchkchk" when they run (and yes- somehow even they manage to fit the desolate atmosphere, mainly due to the way you interact with them, I think.)All in all it's a little masterpiece and I hope to see more games of its format in the future (games that are akin to the likes of INSIDE and LIMBO.)Very excited to play the second one whenever the price drops a fair bit lower.LONG CAMERA-ORIENTATED EDIT:There is something so flawless about the camerawork in this game. In moments it will be working to build tension by keeping both the monster and Six framed perfectly in the same shot, really capturing the villain's sinister, looming presence, and then during other sequences it will focus in on Six, blindsiding you from what follows during a chase in the best way possible.However sometimes the camera is not used for tension so much at all, panning out at certain calmer points in the game to reveal some of the most breathtakingly beautiful shots imaginable, whilst still maintaining the atmosphere and further pushing the integral concept that everything in the game is gargantuan compared to you, that you don't stand a chance against it. It encourages you to stop for moment and drown yourself in the fully expanded views of this strangely beautiful world. These moments don't inspire any particularly good or bad feeling, in fact the only appropriate phrase I have for the feeling they create is pure awe.So yeah, props to whoever did the bulk of the work on the camera in this game, it worked perfectly for me at least.

2021 Titanfall 2 is one of the best first person shooters to date. Yet it is unfortunately plagued by many factors that are not directly it's fault. Which has lead to it being vastly under rated and under played. But I will discuss these later.Titanfall 2 takes the gunplay from Call of Duty, adds one of the best movement system to date, and of course; Titans. You play as a 'Pilot', a near superhuman elite soldier and a significant force in their own right, who has the special right to call in and pilot their Titan. Titans are heavily armed, heavily armored bipedal mech walkers, which is bonded to it's Pilot. It can fight independently, but is strongest when Pilot and Titan are united. The gunplay is similar to Call of Duty (Some of the Dev's used to work on CoD). Weapons that have low recoil, high firerate, and high damage. Because of this the 'time to kill' is very low, often less than a second. Gameplay is inherently very fast and rewards quick reflexes and good aim.Pilots are incredible mobile. They are outfitted with a 'Jump-Kit', a series of thrusters, anti-gravity boots and various other devices that cover their entire body. This allows them to double jump, slide, ignore fall damage, wall run, and move at incredible speed through the battle field. The primary purpose for this is to avoid enemy Titans. Pilots are incredible vulnerable to enemy Titans, their weapons being able to reduce a Pilot to paste in one shot. Direct confrontation with Titans is therefore unwise, so Pilots prefer to use their high mobility to flash through the battle field and stay to the roof tops and/or indoors, places where Titans cannot go. They are not completely at the mercy of Titans however, Pilots carry Anti-Titan weapons and can do serious damage to Titans from hard to reach places. The movement system is relatively simple and easy to learn, but allows for extremely fast and precious movements with proper mastery. In my opinion, it is the best overall movement system in any game that currently exists.Titans are the poster child of this game and a significant part of it. You often start a match on foot as a Pilot, with your Titan having a build meter, that increases passively, but killing enemy Pilots or Titans will add a large chunk to your meter. Once at 100% you will get to call in your Titan, it's will be launched from orbit to where you called it in too after several seconds (this process is called Titanfall). Unlike Pilots, Titans are very durable and the time to kill is much longer. Their firepower is significant, extremely lethal to Pilots, and capable of cutting through an enemy Titans heavy armor with ease. Unlike Titanfall 1, Titan's cannot regenerate their shields (in multiplayer), so damage take is permanent, and the Titan will eventually die even to chip damage. Another change is that Titans in multiplayer are now set classes, with their own weapons, ability, ultimate, role, and theme. Their are 7 Titans; - Ion (energy based). - Tone (mid-ranged explosive shooter). - Ronin (close range weeb). - Northstar (sniper, and can hover). - Scorch (fire, area denial). - Legion (big gun).- Monarch (one man army). This game also has an actual Story Mode (unlike Titanfall 1), and it's actually really good, though a bit short. The game has many levels that take advantage of the Pilots mobility in fun and creative ways. Their's also a good bond between the games protagonists, Jack Cooper (Pilot) and BT-7247 (Titan). Good chemistry between the two and some emotional moments. Overall a very well done story mode, way better than it had any right to be. Multiplayer is good, though a bit hard. Various modes but the main mode is Attrition, which is 6v6, Pliots and their Titans along side AI forces. If PvP multiplayer isn't your thing, their is also a PvE coop mode, called Frontier Defence. 4 Players vs several waves of AI soldiers, Titans and various other forces. The objective is to destroy them all and defend the 'Harvester'.Now to talk about the negative factors I mentioned earlier:1. EA/Origin. Unfortunately, this game's publisher is EA, which is already bad, but it also means that you have to use Origin. Requiring an Origin account and Origin client software installation. The game cannot function without Origin so there is no way around this. This is by far the biggest issue, and something you're going to have to accept if you want to play the game. Worth noting that the Origin version used for the Steam version of Titanfall 2 seems to be a 'lite' version, and hasn't caused me many issues. Unlike the full version of Origin which is prone to crashing.2. Small Player base. Due to many factors (that I don't fully understand), Titanfall 2 has a small pool of players (2000-6000) at any given time. Match making times can be several minutes. It also has little to no skill based match making. It is fairly common that a new player will be paired with a G100 Veteran and get destroyed. This isn't always the case but expect that most people you play with will be experienced, and this game has a very high skill ceiling.3. As the Dev's focus on Apex Legends, Titanfall 2's development is mostly dead. Don't expect any new updates any time soon.4. Minor issue, but when the game launches it's a bit odd. The green 'Play' button on the Steam Client goes Blue (indicating it is running) for a second then back to green. Then Origin opens briefly, then the game opens for real (play button goes blue again). Some issues with this; 1. The game always opens in Windowed mode, even if you set it to Fullscreen. You have to manually set it to Fullscreen every time you launch the game. 2. Sometimes Steam doesn't sync properly after Origin opens briefly, resulting in the game opening, but Steam doesn't think it is (Play button is still green), and can't uses Steam overlay ingame. Only way I've found to fix this is to simply restart the game and hope for the best, some times multiple restarts.Overall, Titanfall 2 is a very good game, but it requires you to put up with several issues and EA's annoying client. If you're willing to put up with that, I'd highly recommend Titanfall 2. If not, don't.

Each time you play, it's a completely new experience, with it being randomly seeded and each seed has massive differentials, so it's always fresh and always new.To get to higher scores, you have to use Jokers {Multipliers that increase either chips (points) or mult (Multiplier){. 2023 I try a lot of different games when they go on sale and most get turned off in an hour or so. So when I bought this on sale I went into with a cynical attitude but it didn't take long until I was completely hooked. It's firmly in my top 10 all-time now and maybe even top 5. Exploring the unknown and gradually progressing your resources and revealing the story are very compelling and satisfying all the way to the end. The progress is well-scaled all the way up to the end. The construction of the modular bases is so much fun and I appreciate that they give you a very long leash to build a base pretty much however you want without it ever feeling like a grind. I even kept playing for hours after beating the game with 100% just to continue experimenting with building/modifying bases. I'm hopeful in the next installment that they take the opportunity to take the depth of crafting and resource mechanics much farther e.g. Skyrim. There is also potential to build on this in future installments by droping in endless Easter eggs and secret/rare items 5 very hard-to-find cuddlefish eggs for example was a simple fun little thing, now do like 50 more things like that. I wish I'd known how much I would like this game going in because I would have paid much closer attention to the story from the start. I blame my cynicism going in on most other games which often have lazy stories that feel half-baked and forced. If the story is an afterthought of your game then please don't bother having one? I was shocked when they really DID answer all my questions by the end and every question was eventually explained logically. The entire game I kept thinking "the map is limited by 'dead zone', oh well they get a pass on that." Then I was shocked that it was actually logically explained and actually was in service to the story. Other devs take note THAT's proper world-building and it really does matter. Just like it did 25 years ago when Half-Life showed how much it can enhance the experience. If you want the best possible experience from this game I can't stress the following enough...go in fresh, avoid spoilers, hints, walkthroughs etc. If you ever feel "stuck" just keep pushing farther from your comfort zone and you WILL progress in no time. If you feel overwhelmed exploring because there is no map...the game has an answer for that too. Just always bring some beacons and leave them on landmarks all over the place to note where you've been or where you need to return to later etc. Pick a direction and go if you don't know what to do. The game will always nudge you in the right direction without holding your hand. The map is not so big that you can't be almost anywhere in five minutes so if you are struggling to find that next thing just keep exploring everywhere you can. 10/10

The game design could have died a death by a thousand antithetical cuts at the hands of suits and contemporary standards. But, for better or worse, here's dragon's dogma 2. They didn't mess with it.You will jump and climb on giant monsters and stab them in the eye while stuffing potatoes into your face. You will hear your pawn remark about the same ladder in Vernworth more times than you've heard "hello" in your lifetime. The story is anemic and arbitrary, forgetting its own beats. The characters are plentiful but cardboard. There are two saves. You will lose pawns to terrain despite your best micromanaging. Your pawn will pick up all your worst combat habits and embarrass you in front of strangers online. Progression scaling is lackluster: you will feel hopelessly desperate at the beginning only to wake up one level and feel like god. Fast travel is artificially limited but similarly scaled where suddenly you are awash in ferrystones. Big mob hunting is made more tedious by the large map, and minotaurs are the griffins of this title it feels like. Quests are still easy to bungle due to time, progress, or simply missing them. And, most importantly, all of this is gift wrapped in the meta of the dragon's literal dogma so of course everything I just mentioned is thematically deliberate and why there's no "2" in the main menu title.Frankly, it was everything I wanted and once again, my complaint is give me more.But that's obviously not my only complaint. I actually didn't have many crashes in 100 hours but the game still runs like molten molasses. Framerates are mostly fine in the wilderness but low in cities which is mildly problematic later on. Normally this would be least concern, easiest fixed, but the fact the game shipped like this, that they thought even the poor performance on the PS5 was acceptable, hints that maybe that's not the case. Beaucoup hardware won't save you here. Something is fundamentally wrong and it's currently setting your CPU on fire while the frames hitch.If you like dragon's dogma, warts and all, and circumstances have prevented you from buying it at release, try it anyway. I found it playable on my potato rig once I acclimated to the framerate dips. If you think you could like dragon's dogma, play dark arisen instead as the price point for curiosity is lower (5 bucks on sale usually) and it won't melt your rig. If you didn't like dragon's dogma 1, this isn't going to change your mind and you'd just be engaging the definition of insanity.

2020 Early Access Review It took me years before I finally decided to buy this game. And now I'm banging my head for not getting it earlier.This game's presentation is not the best. It's probably what kept me from purchasing it. The title is pretty bad, if you ask me. The graphics aren't the best either. Most gameplay videos don't do it much justice, to be honest.Then, one day, I said "Meh, why not. Let's buy this game."I've been playing it non-stop ever since.It's the kind of game that isn't flashy and focuses on the actual gaming experience. You can only understand how great it is once you play it.I believe the first time you play this game is crucial to your overall appreciation of it. I don't recommend reading too much about what you can or can't do. Just play it as if it was a real zombie outbreak. What will you bring with you? Where will you go? How will you deal with the zombies? Such questions will determine whether or not you'll survive the next 24 hours in this game. You're most likely to die early on, but when it happens, you'll want more and more. By your third or fourth game, you'll probably have enough experience to last much longer. As the weeks and months go by, nature will creep its way back to the town. Grass will find its way through the asphalt roads. Plants will grow on buildings and fences. Trees will repopulate the area. What's great about this game is noticing the slow evolution of such things. Eventually, you'll reach fall, maybe even winter, temperatures will drop. The more you go, the harder it gets. After emptying nearby habitations, you'll be forced to venture further and further, increasing the risks of finding yourself in unpredictable situations. Will you risk entering large buildings knowing there's a potential horde inside of them? Or will you stay safe in a farm house, away from the city? There's no wrong way to play this game, but there's no way to "win" it either becaue it can only end once you die.One of the best elements in this game is the crafting system. You can make plenty of things that'll help you survive, from weapons to fortifications to cooking recipes. You can deconstruct various objects and furniture, even cars, chop and saw wood, build useful items out of scratch, etc. Almost everything you collect can be useful in this game. Discovering the many ways to combine or deconstruct things is part of the fun of this game, so I highly recommend not checking out wikis or discussion boards unless you're really stuck with something important.I've tried to play online. Unfortunately, my experience so far hasn't been the best. There are many servers but not many players. Encountering someone is kinda rare, and it's even rarer to encounter someone who wants to play with you for real. I think the survival aspect of Zomboid turns many players into selfish people and that they will regard you as a nuisance more than anything else. But maybe that's also part of the simulation aspect of the game. I think lots of people wouldn't want to team up in a zombie apocalypse when ressources are running low. I wish players would roleplay more, though. This game is several years old and it seems lots of old players got used to it and don't play it the way they probably used to at first. But keep in mind that's just my own experience so far. I'll give it another try eventually, but I think this game's atmosphere can only reach it's peak when you play on solo.And talking about atmosphere, man, this game has tons of it! The darkness, the fog of war/sight, the mist, the music, all contribute to creating a sometimes tense, sometimes desperate feeling, very similar to the best The Walking Dead episodes.I've noticed the devs still deliver updates but that they are very slow at doing so. I personally don't mind it. I'd rather have quality updates rather than hasted, half-finished ones. I'm hyped for the (re)inclusion of NPCs and the big city of Louisville. In the meantime, I'll just clean the town of Rosewood, little by little.

2020 Two years late to the party but still glad I got around this one.While Manhunt will still be my guilty pleasure, RDR2 is probably a top favorite from Rockstar Games.RDR2 tells the downfall the infamous Van der Linde gang before the first game, from the perspective of Arthur Morgan, the top gunman. His entire arc is the things of beauty, and to say doubting I’d like him as much as John was foolish of me. He is a character full of likable traits who can stand proudly among my favorites. Robert Clarke deserved every single praise he received alongside the rest of the cast, with especially Benjamin Davis stealing every single scene he shows up.Now, RDR was almost entirely a love letter to the Italian Western, with mostly deserted and dry locations-and people. However 2 goes beyond to cover more classic takes too. If you have enjoyed any of the tales of the western genre, you will absolutely be satisfied in some way. From small to large heists, insane shoot outs in towns and bar fights, mountains to deserts, forests to dirty swamps, every single activity in the savage times you could like from the West is here. The soft harmonic guitars, gospel chanting, gorgeous visuals and beautiful vistas just deserve that you to take your time and enjoy a slow horseback ride.Everything you do in the world comes to bite your bottom eventually. Being a carcass to people will not result in kindness, the lawmen are ruthless to hunt you down, meanwhile bounty hunters and rival gangs seek to ambush you at any turn. Exploring the environment, paying attention to the surroundings, and finding side missions and quests always benefits you, from some good looting, rare materials to sell or craft, maybe simply amusing characters that go about their antics. The hours I spent just taking a break to go about my leisure is probably half my playtime. Hunting alone is a good example of how much you can go by, hunt to eat in a makeshift camp, donate to the gang, sell for profit, use to craft. There is almost nothing you do that can be considered a waste, and letting loose to invest yourself in the people (and especially your trusted horse) will always be worth it.I'll be straightforward, however: This is a slow game. So slow, that I wouldn't blame you for getting tired of it by the first hours. In game play terms, we have a similar mannerism to Max Payne 3, the shooting mechanics being deliciously brutal, and combat as a whole feels impactful, as it should. You must keep your body well with some light rpg style mechanics and the game will not be afraid to pull a rabbit with a gun if you do not watch your back. Being able to gunfight in first person is a neat addition, not too good for the rest.As a whole, I cant deny I am biased for adoring the genre this game pays so much homage and respect to- but in it's own it's a fantastic story of it's own that does everything to immerse you in.If you liked Clint Eastwood or John Wayne's movies (if you don't please get out of my sight and leave your testicles by the door), you enjoy a slower approach to open world, and can put up mildly annoying design choices for sake of a plot, I can absolutely recommend RDR2 even at full price, and on sale it's damn worth the price.Please do not even try Online
