review: Early Access Review I came expecting a Stardew Valley clone. I was pleasantly surprised to find a game that has enough similarities to feel familiar and intuitive while also having enough unique elements to not feel entirely derivative. If you enjoy this type of game I highly recommend this one.Though it is in early access, there is a lot of content to enjoy. I went 38 hours before running into a quest progression wall, this as someone who tends to play this kind of game fairly efficiently. Character customization is lovely and I found that I was able to represent myself pretty well in the game, with lots of options unlocking as the game progresses. If I could make a request, I would love to be able to find a "skullet" hair style (bald on top, long hair) and have more beard options in general. A big strength of this game is its characters. The cast all interact with each other often, offering unique and often amusing dialogue. Every character has relationship events with the player that felt worth going out of my way for, though I did not explore any character relationship exhaustively (ended up with a fairly even spread maxing out at about 4 hearts). I didn't experience any character romance beyond making some of the other folks in the game blush with dialogue options, but I like the cast and look forward to exploring this more in subsequent playthroughs. I also enjoyed the animal breeding. Mistria keeps raising animals interesting and exciting by having the player unlock new colors and patterns through breeding them. I do note that barns and coops are not modular/upgradable, so when you unlock a new size for these, you have to build a new building. You have the option of tearing down your old one. Maybe I just didn't find it but one criticism I did have was that I didn't seem to be able to move animals between barns/coops. So when I had mating pairs of chickens in my small coop, I couldn't use them to populate my recently built medium coop, a bit of a let down. Another criticism I have of games like this is that they often overlay human relationship dynamics on the animal breeding mechanics. I felt like my rooster should be able to breed with multiple hens simultaneously but he was not able to do so. This makes some sense if I view it from the perspective of keeping game progression balanced, but it still felt a little silly. I liked the way perk progression works in this game, which is skills leveling up with use and also allowing you to buy perks with skill points that drop when you do various actions. That said, farming and mining are both overpowered and will provide you with far more points than you could possibly spend in the mid-game if you are a fan of "biggering" and like to push your farm production to its limits. Cooking involves unlocking recipes through social quests, but perks help the skill pay off significantly by having foods you create offer unique buffs like speed, turning dishes into universally liked gifts, and stamina regen. Considering that this skill requires you learn recipes - usually from building relationships with the characters, the perks are rewarding. Additionally it tends to increase the value of the ingredients used so it's good for making money. However, a criticism for this and all crafting/shopping that is easily fixed: PLEASE make it possible to type in the number of items you want to craft/buy or at least allows the player to click and hold to increase the value rapidly. When I want to craft 200 cranberry juice, I shouldn't be tempted to install an auto-clicker to get this done.Fishing is a little more like Animal Crossing than Stardew with the mechanics requiring you to see the outline of fish in the water and just be patient and careful in the process of landing them. I did find that fish would sometimes get stuck on the edge of bodies of water and thus couldn't be landed. I also think that while there was a decent variety of fish, this part of the game could benefit from more unique encounters and maybe just a little more depth. I had a lot of fun in Fields of Mistria and I'll be back for a new playthrough when the game is finished or closer to finished. PS: There's a jump button ;)

2022 "there ain't no gettin' offa this train we're on, till we get to the end of the line."IntroductionFinal Fantasy 7 Remake Intergrade is a twist on the original cult classic that has been reimagined with cutting-edge graphics, all-new game mechanics, and fast-paced combat. This game will push you to the edge of your seat, but how does it hold up compared to the original? 🟩 Positives 🟥 Negatives 🟩 The story is essentially the same as the original, with little to no altering to the overall sequence.🟩 Probably some of the best voice acting I've experienced in a game to date in quality and actor choice.🟩 Summons make a return, and are as cinematic ever before.🟩 Minigames at some dumb fun to the intense story line and are pretty amusing for the most part.🟩 Boss fights are fun and quite often a decent challenge.🟩 Multiple difficulties to help scale your experience. 🟥 Fights are far too finicky, not quite as responsive or technique based as I would have hoped.🟥 Checkpoints are awfully placed, especially during boss fights.🟥 Side quests feel like filler content, devoid of any real personality. StoryThe planet is in pain, suffering from the endless consumption of its lifeblood called Mako by the mega corporation, Shinra, to fuel their cities and technology. It's here you meet the heroes, a group of rag-tag misfits called Avalanche who are taking the fight to Shinra in hopes that they can save the planet.Cloud Strife, a former member of SOLDIER, an elite group of soldiers used to do Shinra's dirty job's has joined forces with this group and are on their way to destroy a reactor in the mega city known as Midgar.But things begin to unravel quickly.Shinra plans to unleash their entire force with the intention to destroy the group. All the while, Cloud is fighting to stay afloat in his fractured memories and must battle for control against his demons.The story remains entirely faithful to the original game, with some content in between to help bolster it. The writing is superb, and the overall story is perfect to say the least. Side quests are the contrast here, as they are totally devoid of personality and storyline and seem to act purely as filler for the entirety of the experience. Please keep in mind that you only get to play as 4 of the total party in the entirety of this game, and it consists of Cloud, Barret, Tifa and Aerith.Gameplay AnalysisLet's take the fight to Shinra!The remake is a decent rendition of the original game in nearly every aspect. Memorable boss fights return with new mechanics to learn and master that pose significant challenges. Yet standard combat doesn't meet the same standard. Fights are tediously long, button mashing events that don't encourage you to get better, but force you to overcome a barrage of spam abilities and interruptions. The alternate game-mode provided called "classic" really helps with this, making the game more reminiscent of the original and closer to the traditional turn-based gameplay. Combat and abilities menu that allows you to pick your strategy for every encounter. A Screenshot of FINAL FANTASY VII REMAKE INTERGRADE By: Preator Materia and equipment are impressive concepts that have remained the same and allow you to customise your heroes to your own liking and build them how you see fit. Materia is essentially the magic in Final Fantasy 7, taking the shape of coloured orbs that give you special abilities when equipped that also bolster your individual stats. Equipment is precisely as you can imagine, the different armour and weapons your characters can brandish in combat, obviously increasing their defence and damage output. Each weapon can also be upgraded now to improve their damage output, defence and materia slots, you can also learn a new weapon skill for each weapon you level up. There are special kinds of materia that allow you to summon creatures to help in big fights, these are extremely rare but worthwhile investments to find as they can really turn the tide of some of the more brutal fights. The character menu where you plan your builds. A Screenshot of FINAL FANTASY VII REMAKE INTERGRADE By: Preator Better get this right the first time!Checkpoints take place at every significant milestone. Sadly these can be few and far between, sometimes taking place every 30-45 minutes. The game does allow you to manually save, but it's very easy to forget about this during heated story sequences and running back after dying is tedium made manifest.A game within a game within a game.Anyone familiar with the original Final Fantasy 7, will be all too familiar with the mini games. Intergrade is no different as many of the original games make a return and a few fresh ones grace us with their appearance. You will spend countless hours doing squats, fighting boxes or competing in the coliseum just to earn that rare item you can’t get anywhere else! These really help break the intensity of the story as quite a lot happens in the story and it's nice to take a breath, even though it doesn’t make immersive sense.Audio and VisualIntegrade offers a breathtaking visual experience to say the very least. A masterfully detailed world coupled with high quality cinematic graphics is just beyond words. Particle effects and creative use of its physics engine naturally immerse and connect you to the journey. FINAL FANTASY VII REMAKE INTERGRADE A Screenshot of FINAL FANTASY VII REMAKE INTERGRADE By: Preator The audio is just well done, contrasting the visual atmosphere with its crisp quality audio and overwhelming atmosphere, all of this is topped with the deliciously nostalgic soundtrack that has been lovingly remastered and reworked.PC Performance and SpecificationsWith the game set to ultra, and at a resolution of 2560 x 1440, I never saw the game drop below 60 FPS.No issues arose during gameplay.RAM: 32GB (Under Load Usage: 28%)CPU: i9 10900KA 3.70GHz (Under Load Usage: 18.7%)GPU: MSI Ventus RTX 3080 (Under Load Usage: 62.1%)Final Thoughts - GoodReview chart here.Intergrade offers a true experience to the original in nearly every way even though I feel it has lost a little bit of its charm in the revamp. Combat is less satisfying than I remember, story sequences are less compelling and intriguing, and the overall experience is drowning with overwhelming filler content that becomes repetitive quickly. Also keep in mind, this is only 1 part of the FF7 story, and it sits at a whopping $114.95 AUD. With that all being said, this game is a stunning re-creation to the original and it will keep you captivated throughout, I just can't recommend it at full price, so give this one a go if you can grab it on a steep discount.If hunting for materia and fighting monsters didn't give you the thrills you seek, come check out Summit Reviews , for some high quality reviews.

The game boasts an impressive attention to detail and realism, from the highly detailed truck models officially licensed from iconic truck manufacturers to the simulation settings that allow trucking enthusiasts to experience the feel of being inside a real cabin.MechanicsThe game mechanics are based on the highly successful model from Euro Truck Simulator 2 and have been expanded with new features, creating a captivating game experience from SCS Software. Players start off as a driver for hire entering the local freight market and work their way up to becoming an owner-operator and eventually creating one of the largest transportation companies in the United States. The game offers a rich variety of cargoes to choose from, ranging from food to machinery and even hazardous cargoes, and players can deliver these cargoes to a wide range of locations such as refineries, gas stations, and car factories.RealismAmerican Truck Simulator also offers various simulation settings for trucking enthusiasts, such as air brake simulation, different types of brakes, multiple types of transmissions straight from real trucks, and more. Players are required to drive safely, follow the rules and speed limits, and ensure that they are not delivering overweight cargo, as they may be checked at the weigh scales. The game also includes a route adviser as a personal assistant during travels.CustomisationOne of the most enjoyable aspects of American Truck Simulator is the ability to customise your truck and make it your own. Players can change cabins, chassis, paint jobs, add tuning accessories, or even more powerful engines. They can also build their own fleet of trucks, buy garages, hire drivers, and manage their company for maximum profits. The game also includes a built-in music player and streaming radio stations to make the trucking experience even more immersive.GraphicsAmerican Truck Simulator's graphics are stunning and truly capture the breathtaking landscapes and widely recognised landmarks around the States. The game's long-time support and regular updates make it a solid investment for anyone interested in truck simulation games.

review: 2022 Titanfall 2 is a heck of a lot of fun. Definitely the best advanced-movement game I've ever played, plus big stompy robots. But it's not without it's shortcomings either. Let's get in to it.The campaign is amazing. An decent story complemented by excellent gameplay. The voice acting is good, but the length of the campaign is unfortunate. I completed it within about 5-7 hours, and it's not very replayable immediately. Plus if you do go back and play a mission, you might have to sit through unskippable cutscenes. The boss fights were decent, however. Each one has a different loadout that you will eventually get to use later after killing them. Good but short campaign.The multiplayer by itself isn't great, the servers have a tendency to suddenly stop working, but they gameplay is great. Leveling is ok, but hindered by server crashes. You also might have to wait up to ten minutes to find a match. THERE IS A FIX, though! The Northstar mod is super easy to install, and once you do, their servers are much more stable and there is always people online. There's even custom gamemodes. Nobody really plays frontier defense, the PVE mode, and I have never been able to join a match, so I won't review it here.Titanfall 2 was lightning in a bottle for advanced movement shooters, but unfortunately it was abandoned by it's creators. Campaign is great but too short, multiplayer is great but basically requires mods to run. Good game, bad company.VERDICT: 8.5/10- Good game, get on sale

2019 To start off, the story is great. Some of the characters are very likable and funny while others are easy to dislike. The story is very good and is probably one of the best of the decade. Arthur Morgan is a great character, and his voice actor did an incredible job. The game world itself not only feels alive but it also feels lived in, Rockstar added in the smallest of details to the game and I have had many moments where I say to myself wow I didn't expect something like that. From game mechanics like eating/drinking, bathing, buying individual items off of store shelves, caring for your horse, hair cutting and beard trimming, right down to the clothing and gun options, this game leaves very view stones unturned. The only part that really upsets me is Rockstar's outdated mission design. For the most part missions are very linear and hardly allow players to experiment or try to approach the objectives in different ways. Its one of the game's few major letdowns and it's really unfortunate that they messed mission design up.Besides the main story there is plenty to do in game. You can be a good guy and do camp chores, help out strangers, and spend hours hunting and fishing. If you want to be on the other side of the law you can rob stagecoaches, stores, people, horses, trains and any other living thing you chose to interact with. There is always the option of going on a rampage, however the wanted system in this game is a double edged sword, and another let down of the game. You start a fight with an NPC? Wanted. You accidentally press the wrong button and try to rob a store? Wanted. You are out in the middle of nowhere and you kill a person? WITNESS. Its got a lot of flaws. Not to mention the NPCs who beat the crap out of you right next to a lawman while he stands there and watches - but once you put a finger on the NPC, WANTED. Its not completely broken but like most Rockstar games with a wanted system its pretty artificial and only spawns enemies around you as you try to escape.It is important to remember that this game has many complex, intertwined systems, and they all work pretty well most of the time. Rockstar deserves all the praise they get for the Single Player portion of the game. As for Red Dead Online it can be fun but as a solo player you will encounter a lot of other players and posses come after you whenever you are doing your own thing. Its definitely a grind and the pricing of items is designed to make you think about buying gold bars. The story serves as a basic plot and of course your character is mute. If you enjoy endlessly doing the same things over and over again to unlock a new shirt or horse, only to find out it costs 10 times more then you have in your wallet, this is for you. RDO needs a lot more content to be a great experience, and most will find GTA Online to be more fun, but RDO is still worth it for a few hours at least. RDO does not have anywhere near as much content as GTAO and it is rather obvious that it is not Rockstar's top priority.Overall this game is nearly perfect, and it will take a lot of effort for anyone other than Rockstar to top this absolute gem of a game. All video game devs and publishers should strive to create masterpieces like Red Dead Redemption 2, and I am super excited to see how the next GTA game turns out, especially if they use a lot of what they did in RDR2.This boah is a 9.5/10, and I highly recommend it to anyone who can match its hefty performance requirements.

2023 Europa Universalis IV is a very mixed bag for me, since while part of me absolutely wants to love it - with it being down right addicting at times - I honestly can’t recommend it, especially if you’re new. It’s such a shame too, since there’s so much potential for this game to be so great. First things first, we gotta get this out of the way; this game is simply DLC hell, no way around it. At the time of writing this there is $565 CDN worth of it, meanwhile the base game sits at nearly $50 for a game that came out in 2013. I get that the game does go on sale quite regularly ($12 for the base game), and in the past there have been the rare bundle deal for most of the content for around $20, but the prices are still flat out inexcusable and still not worth it. It’s plainly criminal that the base game is so bare bones that it’s required to own at least some DLCs to actually begin to enjoy the game, and let alone benefit from any recent updates as the developers just assume that the player base owns all of them. Plus, most updates are just flat out DLC themselves. As for the game itself, it is nothing like advertised. Yes, there are complex systems, but everything is more unnecessarily archaic than anything and has very little depth or flexibility. For the history of this game it covers late mediaeval to napoleonic which is just way too ambitious for its own good, as it can barely get the contents of its start date right even after so many years of updates, let alone eras that are so far removed from it. It can also start to become problematic with how it simplifies colonization, cultural and religious genocide, and how it just flat out erases non-europeans non-christians (such as making all north america ‘totemist’ or ignoring pagans in places such as the nordic or baltic regions). This isn’t even all counting the countless things that have been broken for years which have yet to be addressed, like the late start dates or multiplayer. Even with all that though, I do still think at the core of EU4 there is a decent game, even if it’s just map painting with quirky AI. I think it’s honestly commendable that the community and developers have stuck around for this long trying to make the best of what’s here, especially mods like Abennar, Ante Bellum and MEIOU and Taxes which show the true potential of this game. But while the newest development team behind the game is doing some great stuff post-Leviathan, there’s only so much patch work you can do when your foundation is on a landfill.

I would say that other popular roguelikes seem to balance out the difficulty to fun ratios a bit better though, at least in reference to Dead Cell's later sections.After enough playthroughs, the random generation starts to feel a bit lacklustre and everything starts to feel kind of samey. The enemies and time it takes to get through the first few starting area start to feel more like a chore than a chance to explore different passages and challenge yourself. Basically, there are issues with the game, don't let the overwhelmingly positive reviews fool you in to thinking this game necessarily has a huge amount of depth even if the first 40-80 hours are a lot of fun.It did take me a fair while to get tired of this game though, and before the 60 hour mark I absolutely loved my time playing Dead Cells. 2021 Game was amazing at the start. (talking about release) I could play all day and never lose interest. I have thousands of hours in FPS games as I'm writing this review. I have worked hard to develop skills that I'm proud of but it matters very little in this game. Most players have a hard time telling the difference between hackers and aim assist in this game. Mouse and keyboard players are like 10% of the player basis and that is me being generous. Slowly I've watched the game be mishandled and the developers show their true colors. They have little interest in community feedback and only care about their views and profits. The skill gap is lowered almost every update (updates are far and few). PC players are second to console and controller. Investing time in mechanical skill and game sense is something the devs frown upon. Wall hack meta has been around for a long time. It is unfun and oppressive to the players, especially to the confident aggressive players and legends. This game started out being about gun skill, decision making and positioning to hold more value than the abilities but now feels like Overwatch when you play. Hackers run rampant through the ranked ladder. There is only a few people who actually deal with them. The anti cheat is a joke flat out. Little innovation to the way the ranked system works makes it feel stale and easy to abuse. This game seems popular right now because of the influx of Fortnite and Warzone players but really this game is headed the same direction as them just not as far down the hole yet. If you haven't played the game before I wouldn't start its a waste of time. If you have been playing the game a little here and there the only reason to login even is just because there hasn't been anything fresh released yet. I give this game at most a year more before it's in a unrecoverable spot and people give up on it.

2017 A few days have passed after I finished the game, and I'm still emotionally agitated. The story and the characters dragged me deep into the world that is "Life is Strange".Small spoilers ahead for Episode 1-5:Similar to the Telltale games, Life is Strange is an interactive tale, which tells you a mostly linear story. The player character "Max" has the ability to turn back time for a few moments, or, later in the game, going far back in time to any moment in her life, by looking on one of her photos. This is quite similar to the movie "The Butterfly Effect".You're playing a teenage/young adult character on a high school and therefore you're confronted with typically high school problems. Besides mastering your daily school problems, the main goal of the story is to find a vanished girl. This kinda reminded me of the "Veronica Mars" series, because you do all these little detective like stuff.Another great thing in the game are the characters. I can't remember of a single dull character. Every person had a unique and interesting personality, even the story-unimportant ones. Especially Max' friend (or sidekick) Chloe will grow fond on you.The wonderful Soundtrack alongside with the atmospheric art style lets you stare at the monitor and enjoy the little things in life (is strange).Overall a clear recommandation if you like high school drama, with the theory of time travel ala Butterfly Effect.

2021 Early Access Review This is a 'difficult' review, as the price for this game was very low, there is definitely fun to be had and the potential is very high. Sure, the game is in early access so i'll give it some slack and update my review as we go along. However, I keep getting errors. First, took me a while to get the game installed due to a 'read error'. Of course, after searching online for a bit I found several work-arounds... running as admin being one of them. Deleting some lines of text (that I was not able to find) another. How come this game needs that, when no other game I have in my library does? Isn't that one of the main reason for programs like Steam to exist, so that we don't have to deal with that anymore?I play the game, 5 hours or so. Nice game. Stop for the day, return the day after. Big red error in the screen. Whatever error it is doesnt seem to affect the games functionality but for the fact that there is now a big red text bubble obscuring my game... Again it's complaining about not having some kind of read rights, though I'm running as an admin. And again: which other game needs this to begin with, as I cannot remember ever successfully installing a game in Steam but then playing it is not working. I'm sure if I go online, this problem will be reported and there will be work-arounds but again, how come those are needed at all?On the game itsself: it's fun, gameplaywise, though it's lacking some nuance which is fine for an early access game. Some things are not really explained very well, and I once even restarted my savegame cause I thought I was stuck only to find out I had to do something which just wasn't very clear. The game is like the English inside it: serviceable, but definitely lacking.Edit: I'm also a bit skeptical on the reviews. Decent game so far. Performance issues are something that will most likely get fixed within the month. Just look at what happened to Cyberpunk on release, and know that this is noooooowhere near as bad as that.As for an actual breakdown on the game, the story starts off weaker than the original game. Simple and epic is how I'd describe the first game. Just a random villager who got attacked by a dragon. After a bit of fighting, you seemed to be the only one to even scratch it so the dragon chooses you. Here it gets complicated even before you select your character. You are already the arisen, and a sovereign ruler at that. But something happens and you wake up elsewhere, not the arisen but also the arisen... It's way too complicated. I get what they were going for, but I feel like this detracts from the dragon focus way too much. I'm about 4 hours in and the only stuff about the dragon is from a flashback that lasted about 60 seconds just to show how we got chosen as the arisen. Everything else has felt sort of Game of Throne's ish and the monsters just don't feel like a threat compared to the weird political nonsense happening.Story complaints aside, the combat feels pretty good so far. Early on, gear is gonna be important as it felt like I was always getting 3 hits before I died. I chose archer so I had enough mobility to keep a distance on most enemies, but sometimes one sneaks up behind or one just launches themselves at you from really far away. Once I got to the main town and could buy the most expensive armor, it was no longer an issue. I could get stun locked for a small duration and survive with a little health. As for the mechanics of the class, I enjoy being able to free fire arrows without aiming all the time. I do usually spend most fights aiming, but after getting used to the free fire it made close encounters much more fun. Mobility skills are where this game shines for me, and for an archer it's the kick ability. You can jump and use an enemies face as a springboard and fire shots mid air. I really enjoy bouncing around the battlefield and throwing arrows around to drop targets that I can't see because there are too many bushes.

2016 Early Access Review Fantastic game. It's early access, there have been and will continue to be abrupt and significant balancing changes as development progresses.IGNORE THE NEGATIVE REVIEW BOMBING THAT OCCURED ON OR AROUND DECEMBER 5, 2015.There was a huge nerf to all the tamed dinos that made them mostly useless... and those changes were then iterated on and tweaked back to perfectly fine WITHIN A WEEK. Unfortunately, this left the Steam reviews of the game with a massive pile of ill-advised, overblown, cry-baby negative reviews followed by a circle jerk of pissed off children flagging each others' negative reviews as helpful. So rather than a fair, balanced collection of reviews to help someone choose whether or not to buy the game, the "Helpful" reviews section makes the game sound awful. I strongly suggest checking out the reviews with an eye to ignoring any dated January 5-10.Now, on to the review.The Negatives:- Official PVP servers have little internal balancing, thus the strongest tribe(s) (refered to as Alpha Tribes) wield enough power to interfere/prevent other tribes advancing. They don't always choose to abuse this power, but it happens. Hey, that's PvPers.- Official PVE servers suffer from abuse of a mechanic where a tribe/solo player cannot build structures within a certain range of another tribes structures. This leads to small pillars or foundations being placed all over to prohibit others from building in any given location. Again, doesn't occur everywhere, but it is an issue.- Optimisation, it's not as bad as some reviews would make you believe ("10-30 fps slideshow - 10 is bad, but 30 is hardly a slideshow). ARK is playable on a high end laptop at medium-high settings, a medium laptop at lower settings, a medium-strength gaming PC at medium or better, and a higher end PC at high settings. But the framerates will spike, there will be hitches, there will be crashes. It's early access, and optimisation is the last major stage of game dev.- Like all online games, there are "hackers" (not really hackers, rather mostly morons downloading software to let them cheat). Again, a thing you'll find on the Official Servers, as the private servers nuke these clowns.The Positives:- Like Minecraft, the game can be played solo, with a friend or two hosted locally, on any of the various Official Servers, or you can host your own dedicated server (locally, or through a hosting service for a monthly fee) or play on someone elses dedicated server. Private dedicated servers are where the game shines. They are moderated by the owners, there is a wealth of settings that can be configured (e.g. faster XP, lower taming times, or more hardcore gameplay, etc), and there is a growing, dev-supported modding community.- Sense of wonder. The game can be brutal to beginners, but that's what the genre is all about. My wife and I had the (mis-?)fortune to pick up the game during the winter event. That was some harsh starting out :) Was pretty awesoem though. The island is big, beautiful, and dangerous. It's like washing up on the deserted Isla Nublar from Jurassic Park with nothing. Even if you're going to start on a private server with frinds who have an established tribe, I strongly suggest going it alone for a bit. After all, it's a survival game, nto much surviving if you are handed a base, food and a T-Rex to ride.- Mods. As noted above, the game can be modded. With official support, no less. It's early days so far, expect things to get even more active once the game stabilizes and goes officially live.- Frequent patches. The devs are always patching, sometimes more than once a day. The list of features in the game is great, the list of stuff coming is fantastic.- Performance. Yes, I said there were some negatives above. But the flip side of that is, this is far and away the most stable running and performing early access title/alpha I think I have ever played. I have a private server, which has yet to crash. I have an older, previously high end PC (i7-4770K, 16GB DDR3, GTX780, SSD) that (very, very rarely) gets occassional disconnects from the server, but otherwise has yet to crash. I run the game at mostly max settings, getting 15-35FPS on average, unless I'm doing something like hunting on foot or moving through very dangerous terrain, in which case turning things down to High nets me 25-60 fps. Certainly playable.Over all, a wonderful game, especially on a friendly private server or your own server with friends and family, or even a good PvP server if that's your thing.The game can be difficult, it can be frustrating, but that's to be expected from a survival game. It's well supported by the devs, surprisingly stable for Early Access, and has a lot going for it now, with more promised and liekly to appear in the future.At the price they are asking, it's well worth diving into provided you are adult enough to understand that there will be bugs, there will be changes, there will be design decisions you don't agree with. It's Early Access. And I've played much, much worse officially released triple-A games for twice the price.
